A SECOND SUBPROJECT ADVANCES OPERATIONS RESEARCH, SUPPORTING FOREST PLANS THAT ARE FEASIBLE, EFFICIENT, AND SUSTAINABLE. A THIRD SUBPROJECT EVALUATES HOW WATER USE AND SOIL CARBON RESPOND TO ENVIRONMENTAL FACTORS AND SILVICULTURAL TECHNIQUES OVER TIME. IN THE AREA OF MANAGEMENT OF FOREST AND RELATED WATERSHED LANDS TO IMPROVE CONDITIONS OF WATER FLOW AND TO PROTECT RESOURCES AGAINST FLOODS AND EROSION, ONE SUBPROJECT WILL ASSESS EFFECTIVENESS OF ENHANCED BEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES TO ENSURE THAT FORESTLANDS IN THE SOUTHEAST PROVIDE A RANGE OF ECOSYSTEM SERVICES IN ADDITION TO WOOD PRODUCTS, INCLUDING HABITAT FOR NATIVE SPECIES, RECREATION, CLEAN AIR AND WATER, AND MITIGATION AGAINST FLOODS AND DROUGHTS. IN THE AREA OF MANAGEMENT OF FOREST AND RELATED RANGELAND FOR PRODUCTION OF FORAGE FOR DOMESTIC LIVESTOCK AND GAME AND IMPROVEMENT OF FOOD AND HABITAT FOR WILDLIFE, SEVERAL SUBPROJECTS INVESTIGATE HOW FOREST LANDS CAN BE MANAGED TO SUPPORT WILDLIFE AND FISHERY RESOURCES. BY MONITORING DEER, COYOTES, REPTILES, AMPHIBIANS, BIRDS, AND FISH, AND MODELING RESPONSES TO FOREST MANAGEMENT AND ENVIRONMENTAL FACTORS, THESE PROJECTS WILL INFORM PRACTICES THAT IMPROVE HABITAT FOR NATIVE SPECIES, ENSURE RECREATIONAL OPPORTUNITIES SUCH AS HUNTING, FISHING, AND BIRD WATCHING, AND INCREASE RESILIENCE TO ENVIRONMENTAL CHANGE. IN THE AREA OF MANAGEMENT OF FOREST LANDS FOR OUTDOOR RECREATION, ONE SUBPROJECT USE RANDOM STRATIFIED EXIT SURVEYS ALONG WITH VISITATION ESTIMATES TO CALCULATE ECONOMIC IMPACTS OF TENNESSEE VALLEY AUTHORITY'S (TVA'S) STREAM ACCESS SITES. IN THE AREA OF PROTECTION OF FOREST LAND AND RESOURCES AGAINST FIRE, INSECTS, DISEASES, OR OTHER DESTRUCTIVE AGENTS, ONE SUBPROJECT IS FOCUSED ON PROTECTION AND RESTORATION OF NORTH AMERICAN ASH SPECIES UNDER THREAT BY THE EMERALD ASH BORER. A SECOND SUBPROJECT INVESTIGATES THE BIOLOGY AND ECOLOGY OF NATIVE AND EXOTIC INSECT PESTS AND EVALUATES BEST MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES TO SUSTAIN FORESTS UNDER THREAT FROM THESE PESTS. IN THE AREA OF UTILIZATION OF WOOD AND OTHER FOREST PRODUCTS, ONE SUBPROJECT ADDRESSES THE STRUCTURE, PROFITABILITY, AND EFFICIENCY OF SMALL, INDEPENDENT LOGGING BUSINESSES, AND AIMS TO HELP THESE BUSINESSES BE MORE EFFICIENT AND PROFITABLE. THE SOUTHERN FOREST INDUSTRY IS RESPONSIBLE FOR $230 BILLION IN ECONOMIC OUTPUT AND OVER 1 MILLION JOBS, AND DEPENDS ON THOUSANDS OF SMALL, INDEPENDENT LOGGING BUSINESSES TO HARVEST AND DELIVER TIMBER. RESULTS WILL HELP THEM OPERATE MORE PROFITABLY AND DELIVER THE TIMBER NECESSARY TO SUPPORT THE FOREST PRODUCTS INDUSTRY. FINALLY, IN THE AREA OF DEVELOPMENT OF SOUND POLICIES FOR THE MANAGEMENT OF FOREST LANDS AND THE HARVESTING AND MARKETING OF FOREST PRODUCTS, ONE SUBPROJECT WILL EVALUATE RISKS TO TIMBERLAND INVESTMENTS FROM MIXED ASSET PORTFOLIOS. ANOTHER WILL USE IN-DEPTH CASE STUDIES, EXISTING PERFORMANCE DATA, AND REMOTELY SENSED LAND COVER DATA TO EVALUATE OUTCOMES OF CROSS-BOUNDARY FOREST MANAGEMENT POLICIES. COLLECTIVELY, THESE OUTCOMES WILL HELP TO IMPROVE THE DESIGN, IMPLEMENTATION, AND MONITORING OF POLICIES AND PROGRAMS TO BETTER MANAGE FORESTS FOR ECOLOGICAL, ECONOMIC, AND SOCIAL GOALS. TARGET AUDIENCES FOR ALL M-S WORK INCLUDE FOREST MANAGERS, INDUSTRY PLANNERS, PRIVATE OWNERS, STUDENTS, SCIENTISTS, AGENCY AND NGO PARTNERS, INVESTORS, AND MORE.

OKLAHOMA HAS COMMONLY BEEN AFFECTED BY WEATHER EXTREMES, RESULTING IN INCREASED RISKS TO HUMAN SAFETY, AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION, AND SHIFTS IN NATURAL COMMUNITIES OF PLANTS AND ANIMALS. ACTIVITIES TO BE PERFORMED INCLUDE RESEARCH CONDUCTED TO DESIGN AND DEVELOP MANAGEMENT METHODS TO USE NATURAL RESOURCES THAT ARE SUSTAINABLE, ECONOMICAL AND ENVIRONMENTALLY SOUND. EXPECTED OUTCOMES WILL INCLUDE RESULTS THAT WILL POSITIVELY IMPACT THE EFFICIENT USE OF OKLAHOMA'S NATURAL RESOURCES THAT ULTIMATELY WILL MITIGATE NEGATIVE CONTRIBUTIONS TO CLIMATE CHANGE. THE INTENDED BENEFICIARIES OF THE RESEARCH ACTIVITIES WILL BE THE CITIZENS OF THE STATE OF OKLAHOMA PRIMARILY AS WELL AS THOSE CITIZENS IN OUR NEIGHBORING  STATES WHERE OUR RESULTING CHANGES IN PRACTICES MIGHT BE RELEVANT.

THE MCINTIRE-STENNIS PROGRAM IN THE UNIVERSITY OF THE VIRGIN ISLANDS STUDIES THE FORESTS OF THE USVI, BOTH ON A LAND SCAPE SCALE AND A SPECIES SCALE. IT FOCUSSES RESEARCH ON BOTH FEDERALLY ENDANGERED TREE SPECIES SUCH AS BUXUS VAHLII AND CATESBAEA MELANOCARPA AND LOCALLY ENDANGERED SPECIES SUCH AS GUAIACUM OFFICINALE AND ZANTHOXYLUM FLAVUM. IT IS NECESSARY TO STUDY SITE REQUIREMENTS SUCH AS SOIL AND CLIMATE, PHENOLOGY, AND SEED DISPERSAL IN ORDER TO PROPAGATE THESE SPECIES IN A NURSERY SETTING AND SUCCESSFULLY PLANT THEM IN THE FOREST. THE MCINTIRE-STENNIS PROGRAM ALSO PROMOTES THE PLANTING OF NATIVE TREES IN PUBLIC SPACES AS OPPOSED TO NURSERY STOCK IMPORTED INTO THE ISLANDS. SINCE THE MAJORITY LANDSCAPE OF THE US VIRGIN ISLANDS IS CONSIDERED URBAN, DUE TO NUMBERS OF INHABITANTS PER SQUARE MILE, A MAJOR CONSIDERATION IS “PLANTING THE RIGHT TREE IN THE RIGHT PLACE” TAKING IN CONSIDERATION TREE SIZE AND AVAILABLE PLANTING SPACE. THE CORRECT CARE OF TREES IN THE URBAN AND SUBURBAN ENVIRONMENT IS ALSO PROMOTED. IT ALSO ENCOURAGES THE PLANTING OF NATIVE TREES IN THE AGRICULTURAL LANDSCAPE FOR WINDBREAKS AND AS SHADE TREES FOR LIVESTOCK IN PASTURES.

THE UNIVERSITY OF GUAM (UOG) HAS REACHED ITS 50TH ANNIVERSARY AS A LAND-GRANT UNIVERSITY IN 2022. THE WESTERN PACIFIC TROPICAL RESEARCH CENTER (WPTRC) IS THE RESEARCH BRANCH OF CNAS AND MANAGES RESEARCH PROJECTS FUNDED BY THE HATCH, MULTISTATE HATCH, AND MCINTIRE STENNIS PROGRAMS. FOR THE MCINTIRE STENNIS PROGRAM, CNAS FACULTY CONDUCT A LIMITED NUMBER OF PROJECTS BECAUSE OF SHARP FUNDING REDUCTION ON FORESTRY ISSUES RELEVANT TO GUAM. OUTPUTS FROM THE PROJECTS ARE PUBLICATIONS IN PEER-REVIEW JOURNALS, TECHNICAL REPORTS, AND INFORMATION IN WEBSITES AND OTHER OUTLETS. IN AN EFFORT TO BE RELEVANT AND ACCOUNTABLE, THE NEVADA AGRICULTURAL EXPERIMENT STATION (NAES) HAS CONTINUOUSLY AND SYSTEMATICALLY REVIEWED AND FOCUSED ON PROGRAMS TO ADDRESS NEVADAS HIGHESTPRIORITY NEEDS RELATED TO FORESTRY RESEARCH. NAES FULLY SUBSCRIBES TO AND SUPPORTS THE UNIVERSITYS GOAL TO ACHIEVE RECOGNITION AS A "FULLY ENGAGED" INSTITUTION AND IS COMMITTED TO THE PRINCIPLES OF ACCESSIBILITY AND PROGRAM UTILITY THAT HAVE GUIDED THE LAND GRANT UNIVERSITY SYSTEM FOR MORE THAN 150 YEARS. CRITICAL ISSUES IN THE STATE TO BE ADDRESSED BY NAES INCLUDE THE PROTECTION AND MANAGEMENT OF OUR NATURAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL RESOURCES. SPECIFICALLY THESE ISSUES INCLUDE THE MANAGEMENT OF OUR FORESTS FOR OUTDOOR RECREATION AND IMPROVEMENT OF FOOD AND HABITAT FOR WILDLIFE; PROTECTION OF FOREST LANDS AND RESOURCES AGAINST FIRE AND OTHER DESTRUCTIVE AGENTS; MANAGEMENT OR FOREST AND RELATED RANGELANDS FOR PRODUCTION OF FORAGE FOR DOMESTIC LIVESTOCK AND GAME. NEVADAS FOREST/WOODLANDS AND RELATED RANGELANDS ARE HIGHLY SUSCEPTIBLE TO WILDFIRES THAT CAN DESTROY MILLIONS OF ACRES PER YEAR. RESEARCHERS WILL CONDUCT STUDIES TO DEVELOP MANAGEMENT PRACTICES TO PROTECT THESE NATURAL RESOURCES FROM THE DEVASTATING EFFECTS OF THESE MEGAFIRES. THEY WILL ALSO LOOK TO DEVELOP WAYS TO BETTER DETECT THESE FIRES IN ORDER TO PROVIDE A MORE RAPID RESPONSE AND MINIMIZE THEIR SPREAD. RESEARCHERS WILL ALSO CONDUCT STUDIES ASSESSING THE IMPACT OF CLIMATE CHANGE INCLUDING PERSISTENT DROUGHT AND INCREASING TEMPERATURES ON FOREST HEALTH AND WILDLIFE HABITAT IN THESE FOREST/WOODLAND AREAS.

positiveFlows.title: THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL HELP OSU COLLEGE OF FORESTRY CARRY OUT RESEARCH PROJECTS IMPORTANT TO THE  STATE OF OREGON. SUPPORTED PROJECTS WILL SUPPORT TRAINED FOREST SCIENTISTS IN THE FOLLOWING RESEARCH  TOPICS: REFORESTATION; FOREST, WATERSHED, AND RANGELAND MANAGEMENT; FOREST RECREATION;  PROTECTION AGAINST FIRE, INSECTS, DISEASES, AND OTHER DESTRUCTIVE AGENTS; FOREST PRODUCTS UTILIZATION;  AND FOREST POLICY. PROJECTS FUNDED BY OSU INCLUDE UNDERSTANDING CONTEXT OF, BARRIERS TO, AND  IMPACTS OF ACTIVE FOREST MANAGEMENT IN THE FIRE-ADAPTED WEST, REVIEWING AND DEVELOPING SOUND  POLICIES FOR THE MANAGEMENT OF FOREST LANDS, HARVESTING PRACTICES, AND MARKETING OF FOREST PRODUCTS,  MANAGEMENT OF FOREST AND RELATED WATERSHED LANDS TO IMPROVE WATER FLOW AND PROTECT AGAINST FLOODS  AND EROSION, RESEARCH ON ADVANCED WOOD PRODUCTS IN MASS TIMBER BUILDINGS, IMPROVEMENT OF  SCIENTIFIC TOOLS FOR MANAGING FORESTED WATERSHEDS, USE OF REMOTE SENSING TECHNOLOGIES TO ESTIMATE  DIMENSIONS AND DIFFERENT QUALITIES OF TREES, AND UNDERSTANDING THE CONNECTIONS BETWEEN FOREST  GOVERNANCE AND LANDSCAPE PATTERN AND PROCESS, AND THE WAYS IN WHICH PUBLIC PERCEPTIONS AND  VALUATIONS OF FEDERAL FOREST LANDSCAPES AND SCIENCE INFLUENCE THOSE CONNECTIONS. THE OBJECTIVE OF THE MCINTIRE-STENNIS (M-S) COOPERATIVE FORESTRY RESEARCH PROGRAM AT THE UNIVERSITY OF GEORGIA (UGA) IS TO CARRY OUT APPLIED RESEARCH WHOSE OUTCOMES SUPPORT SUSTAINABLE MANAGEMENT OF FOREST LANDS FOR MULTIPLE BENEFITS TO PEOPLE AND NATURE IN GEORGIA, AND TO TRAIN FOREST SCIENTISTS TO SUPPORT RESEARCH AND PRACTICE. OUR PROGRAM SUPPORTS RESEARCH IN ALL M-S FOCUS AREAS. IN THE AREA OF REFORESTATION AND MANAGEMENT OF LAND FOR TIMBER PRODUCTION AND OTHER RELATED FOREST PRODUCTS, ONE SUB-PROJECT WILL EVALUATE GENETICALLY IMPROVED PLANTATIONS IN TERMS OF WOOD QUALITY, GROWTH, AND YIELD. A SECOND SUBPROJECT ADVANCES OPERATIONS RESEARCH, SUPPORTING FOREST PLANS THAT ARE FEASIBLE, EFFICIENT, AND SUSTAINABLE. A THIRD SUBPROJECT EVALUATES HOW WATER USE AND SOIL CARBON RESPOND TO ENVIRONMENTAL FACTORS AND SILVICULTURAL TECHNIQUES OVER TIME. IN THE AREA OF MANAGEMENT OF FOREST AND RELATED WATERSHED LANDS TO IMPROVE CONDITIONS OF WATER FLOW AND TO PROTECT RESOURCES AGAINST FLOODS AND EROSION, ONE SUBPROJECT WILL ASSESS EFFECTIVENESS OF ENHANCED BEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES TO ENSURE THAT FORESTLANDS IN THE SOUTHEAST PROVIDE A RANGE OF ECOSYSTEM SERVICES IN ADDITION TO WOOD PRODUCTS, INCLUDING HABITAT FOR NATIVE SPECIES, RECREATION, CLEAN AIR AND WATER, AND MITIGATION AGAINST FLOODS AND DROUGHTS. IN THE AREA OF MANAGEMENT OF FOREST AND RELATED RANGELAND FOR PRODUCTION OF FORAGE FOR DOMESTIC LIVESTOCK AND GAME AND IMPROVEMENT OF FOOD AND HABITAT FOR WILDLIFE, SEVERAL SUBPROJECTS INVESTIGATE HOW FOREST LANDS CAN BE MANAGED TO SUPPORT WILDLIFE AND FISHERY RESOURCES. BY MONITORING DEER, COYOTES, REPTILES, AMPHIBIANS, BIRDS, AND FISH, AND MODELING RESPONSES TO FOREST MANAGEMENT AND ENVIRONMENTAL FACTORS, THESE PROJECTS WILL INFORM PRACTICES THAT IMPROVE HABITAT FOR NATIVE SPECIES, ENSURE RECREATIONAL OPPORTUNITIES SUCH AS HUNTING, FISHING, AND BIRD WATCHING, AND INCREASE RESILIENCE TO ENVIRONMENTAL CHANGE. IN THE AREA OF MANAGEMENT OF FOREST LANDS FOR OUTDOOR RECREATION, ONE SUBPROJECT USES RANDOM STRATIFIED EXIT SURVEYS ALONG WITH VISITATION ESTIMATES TO CALCULATE ECONOMIC IMPACTS OF TENNESSEE VALLEY AUTHORITY'S (TVA'S) STREAM ACCESS SITES. IN THE AREA OF PROTECTION OF FOREST LAND AND RESOURCES AGAINST FIRE, INSECTS, DISEASES, OR OTHER DESTRUCTIVE AGENTS, ONE SUBPROJECT IS FOCUSED ON PROTECTION AND RESTORATION OF NORTH AMERICAN ASH SPECIES UNDER THREAT BY THE EMERALD ASH BORER. A SECOND SUBPROJECT INVESTIGATES THE BIOLOGY AND ECOLOGY OF NATIVE AND EXOTIC INSECT PESTS AND EVALUATES BEST MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES TO SUSTAIN FORESTS UNDER THREAT FROM THESE PESTS. IN THE AREA OF UTILIZATION OF WOOD AND OTHER FOREST PRODUCTS, ONE SUBPROJECT ADDRESSES THE STRUCTURE, PROFITABILITY, AND EFFICIENCY OF SMALL, INDEPENDENT LOGGING BUSINESSES, AND AIMS TO HELP THESE BUSINESSES BE MORE EFFICIENT AND PROFITABLE. THE SOUTHERN FOREST INDUSTRY IS RESPONSIBLE FOR $230 BILLION IN ECONOMIC OUTPUT AND OVER 1 MILLION JOBS, AND DEPENDS ON THOUSANDS OF SMALL, INDEPENDENT LOGGING BUSINESSES TO HARVEST AND DELIVER TIMBER. RESULTS WILL HELP THEM OPERATE MORE PROFITABLY AND DELIVER THE TIMBER NECESSARY TO SUPPORT THE FOREST PRODUCTS INDUSTRY. FINALLY, IN THE AREA OF DEVELOPMENT OF SOUND POLICIES FOR THE MANAGEMENT OF FOREST LANDS AND THE HARVESTING AND MARKETING OF FOREST PRODUCTS, ONE SUBPROJECT WILL EVALUATE RISKS TO TIMBERLAND INVESTMENTS FROM MIXED ASSET PORTFOLIOS. ANOTHER WILL USE IN-DEPTH CASE STUDIES, EXISTING PERFORMANCE DATA, AND REMOTELY SENSED LAND COVER DATA TO EVALUATE OUTCOMES OF CROSS-BOUNDARY FOREST MANAGEMENT POLICIES. COLLECTIVELY, THESE OUTCOMES WILL HELP TO IMPROVE THE DESIGN, IMPLEMENTATION, AND MONITORING OF POLICIES AND PROGRAMS TO BETTER MANAGE FORESTS FOR ECOLOGICAL, ECONOMIC, AND SOCIAL GOALS. TARGET AUDIENCES FOR ALL M-S WORK INCLUDE FOREST MANAGERS, INDUSTRY PLANNERS, PRIVATE OWNERS, STUDENTS, SCIENTISTS, AGENCY AND NGO PARTNERS, INVESTORS, AND MORE.

THROUGH INTEGRATED RESEARCH AND EXTENSION PROGRAMS, NC STATE IS SOLVING CHALLENGES RELATED TO THE PRODUCTIVITY AND PROFITABILITY OF BOTH LARGE- AND SMALL-SCALE FARMS. RESEARCHERS AND EXTENSION EDUCATORS ARE ALSO DEVELOPING AND DISSEMINATING KNOWLEDGE AND TECHNOLOGY TO IMPROVE LANDSCAPING AND GARDENING. RESEARCH AND EXTENSION PROGRAMS IN ANIMAL SYSTEMS ARE FOCUSED ON DEVELOPING AND DISSEMINATING KNOWLEDGE AND METHODS FOR ANIMAL BREEDING, REPRODUCTION, NUTRITION, GENETICS AND GENOMICS, PHYSIOLOGY, ENVIRONMENTAL STRESS, PRODUCT QUALITY, AND HEALTH AND WELL-BEING. THESE INTEGRATED RESEARCH AND EXTENSION EFFORTS ALSO AIM TO TACKLE THE CRITICAL ISSUES IMPACTING THE QUALITY OF OUR SOIL, WATER AND AIR BY PROVIDING SCIENTIFIC SOLUTIONS FOR ANIMAL WASTE MANAGEMENT, WASTEWATER TREATMENT, NUTRIENT MANAGEMENT, SEPTIC SYSTEMS, WETLAND MANAGEMENT, SOIL PROPERTIES, AND FISHERY AND POND MANAGEMENT. NC STATE'S RESEARCH AND EXTENSION EFFORTS TO ENHANCE FOOD SAFETY, NUTRITION AND HEALTH AND TO KEEP AMERICAN'S HEALTHY AND FREE FROM FOODBORNE ILLNESS NECESSITATE A FOCUS ON PREVENTING FOOD SAFETY PROBLEMS RATHER THAN TAKING A REACTIONARY APPROACH. NC STATE'S INTEGRATED RESEARCH AND EXTENSION EFFORTS FOCUS ON PROTECTING THE SAFETY OF FOODS ALONG THE ENTIRE SUPPLY CHAIN, FROM PRODUCTION TO CONSUMPTION. TO MEET THE GROWING  NEED FOR HEALTHY FOOD, RESEARCHERS ARE DEVELOPING AND PRODUCING NEW FOOD PRODUCTS THAT PROMOTE HEALTH AND PREVENT DISEASE. AT THE SAME TIME, EXTENSION PROVIDES NUTRITION EDUCATION PROGRAMMING TO ENSURE THAT INDIVIDUALS, FAMILIES, AND COMMUNITIES HAVE THE KNOWLEDGE THEY NEED TO MAKE INFORMED CHOICES ABOUT FOOD AND HEALTHY LIFESTYLES. IMPROVING PLANT AND ANIMAL AGRICULTURAL SYSTEMS: WITHIN THIS AREA, WE WILL WORK TO ADDRESS CROSS-CUTTING AND EMERGING ISSUES OF ANIMAL AND PLANT HEALTH AND PRODUCTION. IN ANIMAL SYSTEMS, RESEARCHERS WILL STUDY THE EFFICIENCY OF DIFFERENT FEEDING SOURCES TO IMPROVE ANIMAL PRODUCTIVITY AND GUT HEALTH. IN PLANT SYSTEMS, THE FOCUS WILL BE IN SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE, ALTERNATIVE AND HIGH VALUE CROP PRODUCTION, SEASON EXTENSION, CLIMATE CHANGE ADAPTATION, VALUE ADDED AGRICULTURE, DIGITAL AGRICULTURE, SOIL HEALTH, PEST CONTROL, AND AGRO ECONOMICS. EXTENSION WILL CONTINUE TO EXPAND ITS WORK WITH LIVESTOCK PRODUCERS, PLACING SPECIAL EMPHASIS ON LIMITED RESOURCES, SMALL- SCALE MINORITY FARMERS. THE FARM PAVILION WILL FOCUS ON SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE AND LOCAL AND COMMUNITY FOOD SYSTEMS, HOUSING ITS APPLIED RESEARCH AND DEMONSTRATION PROGRAMS' STAFF AND PROVIDING SPACE FOR MEETINGS, FORUMS AND CONFERENCES.

THE MCINTIRE-STENNIS COOPERATIVE FORESTRY RESEARCH (MSCFR) PROGRAM ASSISTS ALL STATES IN CARRYING OUT A PROGRAM OF STATE FORESTRY RESEARCH AT STATE FORESTRY SCHOOLS AND COLLEGES AND DEVELOPING A TRAINED POOL OF FOREST SCIENTISTS CAPABLE OF CONDUCTING NEEDED FORESTRY RESEARCH UNDER THE FOLLOWING RESEARCH TOPICS: 1) REFORESTATION AND MANAGEMENT OF LAND FOR THE PRODUCTION OF CROPS OF TIMBER AND OTHER RELATED PRODUCTS OF THE FOREST; 2) MANAGEMENT OF FOREST AND RELATED WATERSHED LANDS TO IMPROVE CONDITIONS OF WATER FLOW AND TO PROTECT RESOURCES AGAINST FLOODS AND EROSION; 3) MANAGEMENT OF FOREST AND RELATED RANGELAND FOR PRODUCTION OF FORAGE FOR DOMESTIC LIVESTOCK AND GAME AND IMPROVEMENT OF FOOD AND HABITAT FOR WILDLIFE; 4) MANAGEMENT OF FOREST LANDS FOR OUTDOOR RECREATION; 5) PROTECTION OF FOREST LAND AND RESOURCES AGAINST FIRE, INSECTS, DISEASES, OR OTHER DESTRUCTIVE AGENTS; 6) UTILIZATION OF WOOD AND OTHER FOREST PRODUCTS; 7) DEVELOPMENT OF SOUND POLICIES FOR THE MANAGEMENT OF FOREST LANDS AND THE HARVESTING AND MARKETING OF FOREST PRODUCTS. THE UNIVERSITY OF ARKANSAS DIVISION OF AGRICULTURE (UADA) UTILIZES OUR MSCFR FUNDING TO SUPPLEMENT STATE APPROPRIATION SUPPORTED F ACULTY AND STAFF SALARIES. DIVISION RESEARCHERS CONDUCT BASIC AND APPLIED RESEARCH FOR ARKANSAS PRODUCERS, BUSINESSES, COMMUNITIES, AND FAMILIES. THE UADA FACULTY HAS A LONG HISTORY OF PROVIDING LEADERSHIP IN THE DEVELOPMENT, DISSEMINATION AND DELIVERY OF KNOWLEDGE, INNOVATIVE PRACTICES, AND EMERGING TECHNOLOGY.

positiveFlows.title: AGRICULTURE IS THE PRIMARY INDUSTRY IN SOUTH CAROLINA, WITH 25,000 FARMS ACROSS 4.7 MILLION ACRES THAT CONTRIBUTE OVER $46 BILLION TO THE STATE'S ANNUAL ECONOMY AND PROVIDE OVER 247,000 JOBS. FORESTRY IS ALSO AN IMPORTANT ECONOMIC DRIVER IN SC, CONTRIBUTING OVER $21.2 BILLION ANNUALLY. WITH DIVERSE NATURAL RESOURCES ACROSS THE STATE, TOURISM IS AN ADDITIONAL ECONOMIC FORCE, ACCOUNTING FOR EXPENDITURES OF $24.4 BILLION ANNUALLY. SUPPORTING AND IMPROVING THE LIVELIHOOD AND QUALITY OF LIFE FOR SC RESIDENTS ARE WHAT DRIVE THE PROGRAMMING AND RESEARCH FOCUS FOR CLEMSON UNIVERSITY. THE PLAN OF WORK REFLECTS RESEARCH ACTIVITIES TO BENEFIT AGRIBUSINESS, COMMUNITIES, AND CITIZENS OF SC. THE RESEARCH IS CONDUCTED ON THE MAIN CAMPUS OF CLEMSON UNIVERSITY AND IN EACH OF THE SIX RESEARCH AND EDUCATION CENTERS (RECS) LOCATED ACROSS THE STATE. FOCUS AREAS INCLUDE ADVANCING THE COMPETITIVENESS OF THE AGRICULTURE AND FORESTRY, ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT, SAFEGUARDING THE FOOD SUPPLY, PRESERVING NATURAL RESOURCES, AND PREPARING YOUNGER GENERATIONS TO BECOME PRODU CTIVE CITIZENS. RESEARCH TO IMPROVE THE PRODUCTIVITY AND PROFITABILITY OF AGRICULTURAL SYSTEMS INCLUDES OUR ADVANCED PLANT TECHNOLOGY (APT) PROGRAM AND OUR PRECISION AGRICULTURE PROGRAM. THE APT PROGRAM USES TRADITIONAL PLANT BREEDING AND MOLECULAR GENETICS TO DEV ELOP NEW CROPS AND CROP-BASED PRODUCTS. THE PRECISION AGRICULTURE PROGRAM DEVELOPS DEVICES AND METHODOLOGIES FOR SITE-SPECIFIC AND MORE EFFICIENT USE OF INPUTS (E.G., WATER, FERTILIZER, PESTICIDES). OTHER RESEARCH EFFORTS STUDY LIVESTOCK FORAGE PRODUCTION TO ENHANCE FARM PROFITS AND ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY. RESEARCH PROGRAMS TO SUSTAIN CONSERVATION OF NATURAL RESOURCES INCLUDE: 1) REMOTE CLIMATIC DATA COLLECTION AND DATA MANAGEMENT ON FORESTS, 2) TECHNIQUES TO ENHANCE FOREST GROWTH AND QUALITY (SILVICULTURE, HARVESTING OPERATIONS, FOREST MANAGEMENT, AND FOREST HEALTH), 3) HYDROLOGIC AND FOREST PRODUCTIVITY PROCESSES ALONG HYDROPERIODS AND SALINITY GRADIENTS.

VAES IS COMMITTED TO DEVELOPING AND IMPLEMENTING RESEARCH THAT ADDRESSES SOCIETAL NEEDS, EXPECTATIONS, AND FUTURE PRESSURES AND OPPORTUNITIES. VAES IS FOCUSED ON CREATING KNOWLEDGE, INTEGRATING ADVANCED TECHNOLOGICAL AND SCIENTIFIC INNOVATIONS TO CREATE EFFICIENCIES AND ECONOMIC GROWTH, AND TRANSLATING KNOWLEDGE INTO PRACTICE TO ENHANCE AGRICULTURAL AND FOOD SYSTEMS, INCLUDING AGRICULTURE AND FOOD, NATURAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL RESOURCES, AND LIFE SCIENCES. RESEARCH ENCOMPASSES NEAR- AND LONG-TERM ISSUES AND OPPORTUNITIES PERTAINING TO INVASIVE PESTS AND ORGANISMS, INFECTIOUS DISEASE, HEALTH AND WELLNESS, QUALITY, SOCIAL INTERACTIONS, AND ECONOMICS IN ANIMAL, PLANT, HUMAN, NATURAL RESOURCES, ENVIRONMENT AND CLIMATE, ADVANCED TECHNOLOGY AND COMPUTER-HUMAN INTERACTIONS. THE AGRICULTURAL VIABILITY, PROFITABILITY, AND SUSTAINABILITY CRITICAL ISSUE WILL DEVELOP LOW INPUT AND PROFITABLE INDOOR AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION SYSTEMS; IMPROVE THE SUSTAINABILITY AND PROFITABILITY OF SMALL RUMINANT PRODUCTION; ASSESS LABOR AND ECONOMIC EFFICIENCIES ASSOCIATED WITH ADVANCED TECHNOLOGICAL AND SCIENTIFIC INNOVATIONS. THE BIOTECHNOLOGY, BIOMATERIALS, AND BIOENERGY CRITICAL ISSUE WILL IDENTIFY NOVEL GENES THAT CAN BE USED TO IMPROVE CROP TOLERANCES TO ENVIRONMENTAL STRESSES, ESPECIALLY DROUGHT, HEAT AND METAL TOXICITY; USE GENETIC AND GENOME APPROACHES FOR BREEDING NEW CROPS TO ADDRESS GLOBAL CLIMATE CHANGE; DESIGN SUSTAINABLE VALUE-ADDED ALTERNATIVES FOR AGRICULTURAL, FOOD, AND MATERIAL WASTE; AND CREATE CELLULAR-BASED ALTERNATIVES FOR ADDRESSING ENVIRONMENTAL CHALLENGES, INCREASED AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION, AND EXPANDING FOOD RESOURCES. THE FOOD, NUTRITION AND HEALTH CRITICAL ISSUE WILL DEVELOP AND DESIGN INNO VATIVE APPROACHES AND PROCESSES FOR MAINTAINING AND IMPROVING QUALITY, NUTRITIONAL VALUE, AND SHELF-LIFE OF FOOD; AND IDENTIFY, DEVELOP, AND EVALUATE NOVEL BIOLOGICAL AND CHEMICAL RESOURCES FOR ENHANCING HEALTH AND WELLNESS FOR PLANTS, ANIMALS, AND HUMANS. THE NAT URAL RESOURCES, ENVIRONMENT, AND CLIMATE CHANGE CRITICAL ISSUE WILL DEVELOP A RESILIENT FARMING SYSTEM THAT CAN COPE WITH THE ADVERSE IMPACTS OF CLIMATE CHANGE; MINIMIZE THE EFFECTS OF CLIMATE CHANGE ON LOW-INCOME COMMUNITIES; AND EVALUATE CARBON SEQUESTRATION AND METHANE EMISSIONS RELATED TO NATURAL RESOURCES, AGRICULTURAL PRACTICES, AND FOOD PROCESSING.

THE MAINE AGRICULTURAL AND FOREST EXPERIMENT STATION HAS BEEN CONDUCTING RESEARCH FOR MAINE AND ITS PEOPLE FOR OVER 125 YEARS. ANNUAL APPROPRIATIONS UNDER THE HATCH AND MCINTIRE-STENNIS ACTS, IN COMBINATION WITH UNIVERSITY OF MAINE FUNDS, PROVIDE THE BASE FUNDING FOR RESEARCH PROGRAMS OF THE STATION. THE RESEARCH CAPACITY PROVIDED BY BASE FUNDING LEVERAGES ADDITIONAL FUNDING FROM COMPETITIVE GRANTS AND CONTRACTS AND INDUSTRY SUPPORT. MCINTIRE-STENNIS FUNDS ARE USED AT THE MAINE AGRICULTURAL AND FOREST EXPERIMENT STATION TO SUPPORT RESEARCH IN FOREST RESOURCES SPANNING A RANGE OF CURRENT ISSUES IN SILVICULTURE AND FOREST MANAGEMENT, WOOD SCIENCE AND FOREST PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT AND MARKETING, TO WILDLIFE HABITAT, OUTDOOR RECREATION, AND LAND USE POLICY. THE MAINE AGRICULTURAL AND FOREST EXPERIMENT STATION WILL USE ADMINISTRATIVE MCINTIRE-STENNIS FUNDS TO SUPPORT THE RESEARCH PROGRAM ADMINISTRATION AND FINANCIAL RECORD KEEPING AND REPORTING ACTIVITIES REQUIRED BY THE FEDERAL REGULATIONS THAT GOVERN THE EXPENDITURE OF MCINTIRE-STENNIS FUNDS. THE STATION HAS 25 RESEARCH PROJECTS IN THE MCINTIRE STENNIS PROGRAM. TYPICALLY, EACH MCINTIRE-STENNIS PROJECT WILL HAVE SEVERAL A SSOCIATED PROJECT ACTIVITIES SUPPORTED BY COMPETITIVE GRANTS OR OTHER SOURCES.

IN 2023, FOREST LANDS TOTALING NEARLY 20 MILLION ACRES PROVIDED $1.48 BILLION IN PRODUCTION FOR 130,000 MISSISSIPPI FOREST LANDOWNERS AND GENERATED MORE THAN $13 BILLION IN ECONOMIC IMPACT. THE FOREST INDUSTRY SUPPORTED 67,833 MISSISSIPPI JOBS WITH A $3.37 BILLION PAYROLL. THE MISSION OF THE COLLEGE OF FOREST RESOURCES (CFR) AND THE FOREST AND WILDLIFE RESEARCH CENTER (FWRC) IS TO FOSTER THE MANAGEMENT, CONSERVATION, AND SUSTAINABLE USE OF FOREST, WILDLIFE, AND AQUATIC RESOURCES TO BENEFIT THE PEOPLE OF MISSISSIPPI, THE NATION, AND THE WORLD. THROUGH TRANSFORMATIVE TEACHING AND LEARNING, RESEARCH AND DISCOVERY, OUTREACH, AND ENGAGEMENT, WE PREPARE FUTURE LEADERS, ENHANCE THE RESTORATION AND SUSTAINABLE USE OF RENEWABLE NATURAL RESOURCES, AND TRANSFER TECHNOLOGY INTO APPLICATION TO SOLVE THE GRAND CHALLENGES IN FORESTRY, FOREST PRODUCTS, AND WILDLIFE CONSERVATION. OUR RESEARCH INFORMS MANAGEMENT PRACTICES THAT MAKE OUR FOREST LANDOWNERS MORE PRODUCTIVE, PROFITABLE, AND ECOLOGICALLY SUSTAINABLE. THE GRADUATE EDUCATION PROGRAMS OF THE CFR TRAIN AND EQUIP THE NEXT GENERATION OF NATURAL RESOURCES PROFESSIONALS AND LEADERS. OUTREACH AND TECHNOLOGY TRANSFER PROGRAMS FACILITATE COORDINATION AMONG SCIENTISTS, AGENCIES, AND INDUSTRY STAKEHOLDERS. MISSISSIPPI FOREST LANDS PRODUCE MYRIAD FOREST PRODUCTS INCLUDING DIMENSIONAL LUMBER, VENEER, PALLETS, AND PAPER PRODUCTS. SCIENTISTS IN THE FWRC ARE DEVELOPING NEW SUSTAINABLE BIOPRODUCTS INCLUDING; MASS TIMBER ENGINEERED WOOD PRODUCTS, ADHESIVES, PRESERVATIVES, GRAPHENE?BASED COMPOSITE MATERIALS, AND LIGNIN?BASED NANOPARTICLES. THESE NEW VALUE?ADDED WOOD PRODUCTS WILL EXPAND MARKETS, SUPPORT ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT, AND INCREASE PROFITABILITY FOR FOREST LANDOWNERS. FWRC RESEARCH PROGRAMS SUPPORT ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT. AS AN ILLUSTRATION, SOFTWARE AND METHODOLOGY DEVELOPED BY FWRC ARE USED BY THE MISSISSIPPI FORESTRY COMMISSION AND MISSISSIPPI DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY TO INFORM SITING OF SAWMILLS AND PELLET PLANTS AND ATTRACT NEW INDUSTRIES TO THE STATE. THESE TOOLS DETERMINE THE IDEAL LOCATION TO BUILD A FACILITY, BASED ON AVAILABILITY OF THE RESOURCES AND ACCESS TO MARKETS AND TRANSPORTATION NETWORKS. EMERGING CARBON MARKETS PROVIDE AN OPPORTUNITY FOR MISSISSIPPI FOREST LANDOWNERS TO MONETIZE ENVIRONMENTAL SERVICES THAT PROVIDE A PUBLIC GOOD. FWRC SCIENTISTS ARE DEVELOPING DECISION SUPPORT TOOLS AND OUTREACH PRODUCTS TO HELP FOREST LANDOWNERS UNDERSTAND THESE MARKETS AND WEIGH THE COSTS AND BENEFITS OF HARVEST DEFERRAL FOR CARBON CREDITS. FWRC RESEARCH ON SHORTROTATION WOODY BIOMASS CROPS REDUCES OFF?SITE NUTRIENT TRANSPORT FROM AGRICULTURAL LANDS, SEQUESTERS CARBON, AND PROVIDES A CARBON?NEUTRAL ENERGY FEEDSTOCK. EMERGING WILDLIFE DISEASES THREATEN WILDLIFE POPULATIONS, HUMAN HEALTH, AND ASSOCIATED RECREATION AND ECONOMIC ACTIVITY. MISSISSIPPI IS ON THE GEOGRAPHIC SOUTHEASTERN LEADING EDGE OF THE SPREADING CHRONIC WASTING DISEASE (CWD) EPIDEMIC. SCIENTISTS IN THE FOREST AND WILDLIFE RESEARCH CENTER HAVE PARTNERED WITH THE MISSISSIPPI DEPARTMENT OF WILDLIFE, FISHERIES AND PARKS, AND THE MSU COLLEGE OF VETERINARY MEDICINE DIAGNOSTIC LAB SYSTEM TO RESPOND TO THIS NEW THREAT WITH SURVEILLANCE, DIAGNOSTICS, RESEARCH, AND POLICY DEVELOPMENT. DETECTION OF THIS EPIDEMIC WHILE GEOGRAPHICALLY LIMITED AND AT LOW PREVALENCE, PROVIDES A UNIQUE OPPORTUNITY TO APPLY A SCIENCE?BASED RESPONSE AND PROACTIVELY GET OUT IN FRONT WITH; DEVELOPMENT AND TESTING OF CONTAINMENT STRATEGIES, REGULATORY POLICIES, HUNTER EDUCATION, AND HUMAN HEALTH GUIDELINES. MCINTIRE?STENNIS FUNDING IN THE FWRC/CFR SUPPORTS 36 INDIVIDUAL ACTIVE M?S PROJECTS AND 27 GRADUATE STUDENTS ANNUALLY. MCINTIRE? STENNIS FUNDING IS LEVERAGED WITH $6.4 MILLION IN STATE APPROPRIATED AND MORE THAN $14 MILLION IN EXTRAMURAL FUNDING THAT COLLECTIVELY SUPPORT RESEARCH AND EDUCATION PROGRAMS TO ADVANCE MANAGEMENT, CONSERVATION AND UTILIZATION OF FOREST RESOURCES.

WE SEEK TO INITIATE CUTTING EDGE INTERDISCIPLINARY RESEARCH RELATED TO CLIMATE CHANGE, ECOSYSTEM HEALTH AND RESTORATION, SOIL HEALTH, WATER QUALITY AND QUANTITY, ENVIRONMENTAL CHEMISTRY, HABITAT EVALUATION, NATURE-BASED RECREATION, VALUING ECOSYSTEM SERVICES, GREEN TECHNOLOGY INCLUDING ALTERNATIVE AND SUSTAINABLE ENERGY, SUSTAINABLE LANDSCAPES, ENVIRONMENTAL INFORMATICS AMONG OTHERS. (3) THE HEALTH OF EARTH'S ECOSYSTEMS HAS DETERIORATED SO MUCH THAT THE PUBLIC IS CONCERNED ABOUT A LOSS OF LIFE SUPPORT FOR ALL ORGANISMS. ECOSYSTEM HEALTH INCLUDES BOTH THE BIOPHYSICAL AND SOCIOECOLOGICAL DIMENSIONS. THE BIOPHYSICAL REALM INCLUDES CLIMATE, AIR, THE ENVIRONMENT, WATER, ENERGY, WILDLIFE, FOOD, SOIL HEALTH AMONG OTHERS. THE SOCIOECONOMIC ASPECTS INCLUDE ECONOMIC SUSTAINABILITY, SOCIAL SERVICES, RECREATION AND HUMAN AND ANIMAL HEALTH AND WELFARE. WE SEEK TO REVITALIZE AND EXPAND OUR ENVIRONMENTAL AND NATURAL RESOURCES AND ANIMAL, AND HUMAN HEALTH RELATED PROGRAMS, STRENGTHEN PARTNERSHIPS WITH THE SCIENTIFIC COMMUNITY AND STAKEHOLDERS, AND PROVIDE A TRANSLATIONAL PLATFORM WITH FOCUS ON ENVIRONMENTAL SUSTAINABILITY, ANIMAL AND HUMAN WELFARE AND HEALTH, ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT, AND POLICY REFORMS. (4) MISSOURI IS AN AGRARIAN STATE SUPPORTING A $93.7 BILLION AGRICULTURE INDUSTRY. OVER THE NEXT DECADE, THE AGRICULTURE, FOOD AND FORESTRY INDUSTRIES IN MISSOURI ARE PROJECTED TO GENERATE 13,000 JOB OPENINGS ANNUALLY. TECHNOLOGICAL ADVANCES, INCLUDING SMART FARMS AND BIG DATA AND DATA ANALYTICS, HAVE CREATED SEVERAL NEW JOB OPPORTUNITIES. HOWEVER, FINDING SKILLED LABOR CONTINUES TO BE A CHALLENGE. WE SEEK TO PROVIDE HANDS-ON TRAINING THROUGH BASIC AND APPLIED RESEARCH RELATED TO AGRICULTURE PRODUCTION AND PROCESSING, FOOD AND NUTRITION, NATURAL RESOURCES MANAGEMENT, AND AGRIBUSINESS AND AGRICULTURAL POLICY THAT WILL PRODUCE A WELL-TRAINED WORKFORCE FOR THE AGRICULTURE INDUSTRY OF THE PRESENT AND FUTURE AND FURTHER THE ECONOMIC IMPACT OF AGRICULTURE. DELIVERABLES AND OUTCOMES: THIS PROJECT WILL GENERATE SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE THAT WILL ADVANCE AGRICULTURE, FOOD AND NATURAL RESOURCES FOR A HEALTHY FUTURE; BETTER CROPS AND CROPPING SYST EMS THAT WILL BE RESILIENT TO CHANGING CLIMATE AND EXTREME WEATHER EVENTS; BETTER UNDERSTANDING AND QUANTIFICATION OF ENVIRONMENTAL BENEFITS AND ECOSYSTEM SERVICES OF SUSTAINABLE AND REGENERATIVE CROPPING; AND, ECONOMIC AND POLICY ANALYSIS THAT CAN HELP FARMERS/R ANCHERS/POLICY MAKERS MAKE APPROPRIATE DECISIONS. ALL THE ABOVE OUTCOMES WILL ALSO GENERATE PEER REVIEWED PUBLICATIONS, GRADUATE THESES AND DISSERTATIONS, PROFESSIONAL PRESENTATIONS, DEMONSTRATION TRIALS, NEW VARIETIES, INVENTION DISCLOSURES AND PATENTS AND DATA AND MATERIALS. BENEFICIARIES: THE DIRECT INTENDED BENEFICIARIES ARE FARMERS AND RANCHERS IN MISSOURI PRIMARILY, BUT OVERALL, IT BENEFITS THE CITIZENS OF THE STATE. SUBRECIPIENTS: N/A

THE UNIVERSITY OF MONTANA'S PROGRAM OF RESEARCH IN FY2025 CONSISTS OF CONTINUING TRANSDISCIPLINARY PROJECTS THAT ADVANCE SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE ACROSS THE RANGE OF TOPICAL AREAS TARGETED BY THE MCINTIRE-STENNIS COOPERATIVE FORESTRY PROGRAM. IN FY2023, UM'S MCINTIRE-STENNIS RESEARCH LAUNCHED A LARGE NEW FOCUS LINKING CARBON STORAGE AND TIMBER PRODUCTION AND WE CONTINUED THAT WORK IN FY 2024. OUR WORK FOR THIS YEAR AIMS TO CONTINUE THAT RESEARCH. FORESTS IN THE WESTERN UNITED STATES SERVE MULTIPLE ROLES ON THE LANDSCAPE. FORESTS STORE CARBON, PRODUCE TIMBER, SUPPORT BIODIVERSITY, PROVIDE RECREATIONAL OPPORTUNITIES, AND SERVE AS RANGE FOR LIVESTOCK. BALANCING ALL THESE OPPORTUNITIES REQUIRES AN UNDERSTANDING OF THE PROCESSES SUPPORTING EACH AND, PERHAPS MORE IMPORTANTLY, THE INTERACTIONS AMONG THE VARIOUS USES. OUR RESEARCH PROJECTS AIM TO UNDERSTAND THE INTERCONNECTED PROCESSES PROVIDING FOR MULTIPLE ROLES OF FORESTS ON THE LANDSCAPE. WE SEEK TO UNDERSTAND HOW CHANGES IN ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS POTENTIALLY IMPACT EACH FOREST USE. SPECIFICALLY, WE WILL INVESTIGATE CAPACITY TO STORE CARBON AND OUR ABILITY TO MEASURE AND PREDICT STORAGE, SEED BANK COMPOSITION AND POTENTIAL FOR CURRENT AND FUTURE RESTORATION OF FOREST AND RANGE IN THE EVENT OF A CHANGE IN STRUCTURE, WILDLIFE RESPONSES TO TIMBER, RANGE, AND RECREATIONAL USE, AND SOCIAL RESPONSES TO FORESTS INCLUDING RECREATION AND VALUES. OUR RESEARCH ALIGNS WITH THE MANDATED RESEARCH AREAS OF THE MCINTIRE-STENNIS ACT AND IT ALSO ALIGNS WITH THE USDA STRATEGIC PLAN GOALS 1 AND 2. WE WILL LEVERAGE THE UM LUBRECHT EXPERIMENTAL FOREST IN ADDITION TO OTHER SITES AROUND THE WESTERN UNITED STATES TO BETTER UNDERSTAND THE INTERCONNECTEDNESS OF FOREST SYSTEMS. WE WILL CONTINUE THE FIRE AND FIRE SURROGATE STUDY AS A LONG-TERM LONGITUDINAL STUDY TO UNDERSTAND FIRE AND THINNING PRACTICES. WE WILL EXAMINE CARBON STORAGE MEASUREMENT AND PREDICTION TOOLS TO BETTER UNDERSTAND HOW TO PLAN FOR FOREST MANAGEMENT AS A CARBON STORAGE SYSTEM. FURTHERMORE, WE WILL EXAMINE SEED BANK RESILIENCY AND WATER RESOURCES TO BETTER UNDERSTAND HOW FORESTS CAN BE RESTORED AFTER STRUCTURAL CHANGES SUCH AS WILDFIRE AND TIMBER HARVEST. FOREST RESOURCES EXTEND BEYOND VEGETATION TO WILDLIFE AND PEOPLE WHO USE THEM. WE WILL FURTHER CONSIDER HOW MANAGEMENT FOR CARBON STORAGE CAN BE LINKED TO MANAGEMENT FOR WILDLIFE HABITAT AND RECREATION. WE WILL EXPAND METHODS FOR MEASURING WILDLIFE POPULATIONS USING REMOTELY TRIGGERED CAMERAS TO ESTIMATE WILDLIFE ABUNDANCE, DIVERSITY, AND USE. CAMERAS REPRESENT A METHOD THAT COULD BE EMPLOYED ACROSS A WIDE RANGE OF FOREST MANAGERS FROM SMALL PRIVATE FOR ESTS TO LARGE-SCALE FEDERAL LANDS. THE RESULTS OF OUR RESEARCH WILL PROVIDE GUIDANCE FOR LAND MANAGERS SEEKING TO BALANCE MULTIPLE OBJECTIVES IN THEIR FORESTS. WE WILL DEVELOP METHODS FOR MEASURING KEY FEATURES SUCH AS SEED BANK RESOURCES AND WILDLIFE. WE WILL ALSO DEVELOP INSIGHTS FOR MANAGING FOREST STANDS WITH FIRE AND THINNING AS THEY GROW WITH AN EYE TOWARD CARBON STORAGE CAPACITY. BENEFICIARIES OF OUR RESEARCH INCLUDE PRIVATE LANDOWNERS AND LAND MANAGEMENT AGENCIES CONSIDERING TIMBER AND CARBON RESOURCES OF THEIR FORESTS, RECREATIONISTS, AND WILDLIFE USERS.

THE RESEARCH CONDUCTED AT THE UNIVERSITY OF ALASKA FAIRBANKS (UAF) AGRICULTURAL AND FORESTRY EXPERIMENT STATION (AFES) WITH MCINTIRE -STENNIS FUNDING WILL ADDRESS STAKEHOLDER NEEDS FOR UNBIASED, SCIENCE-BASED INFORMATION ABOUT NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGEMENT ISSUES IN FORESTRY, MINING, WATER, RECREATION AND ALTERNATIVE, SUSTAINABLE ENERGY SOURCES. ALASKA'S FOREST AND AGRICULTURAL RESOURCE POTENTIAL FOR BIOENERGY PRODUCTION IS IMMENSE BUT REQUIRES MORE RESEARCH. THE ECONOMIC POTENTIAL OF ALASKA'S FORESTS IS UNDER-REALIZED IN TIMBER AND NON-TIMBER PRODUCTS. THE FOREST ECOSYSTEM AND AGRICULTURAL LANDS CAN PLAY A ROLE IN DIVERSIFYING THE ECONOMY OF ALASKA. CONCERN FOR THE HEALTH AND SURVIVAL OF RESOURCE BIODIVERSITY WILL CONTINUE TO BE A CENTRAL ISSUE IN RESOURCES MANAGEMENT IN ALASKA AND ELSEWHERE. AS ENERGY CONTINUES TO BECOME A GROWING CONCERN THROUGHOUT THE WORLD, THE BOREAL FOREST HAS THE POTENTIAL TO PROVIDE PRODUCTS NECESSARY FOR FUEL ALTERNATIVES TO PETROLEUM AND COAL. THE FOREST ECOSYSTEM ALSO PLAYS A CRITICAL ROLE IN THE CULTURE AND QUALITY OF LIFE OF ALASKAN CITIZENS. THE BOREAL FOREST IS EXPERIENCING ECOLOGICAL DROUGHT AND THE IMPACTS OF CLIMATE CHANGE AT A HIGHER RATE THAN MANY OTHER ECOSYSTEMS. HOW THE FOREST RESPONDS TO CLIMATE CHANGE WILL HAVE CONSEQUENCES FOR WILDFIRE VULNERABILITY, INSECT INFESTATION, AND CLIMATE-INDUCED STRESS THAT IMPACTS TREE GROWTH, WOOD PRODUCTION, WATER USE, AND WILDLIFE HABITAT. MORE RESEARCH IS NEEDED THAT FOCUSES ON THESE CRITICAL FOREST ISSUES. RESEARCH PROJECTS WILL BE IN RESPONSE TO REQUESTS FROM PRODUCERS, INDUSTRIES, AND STATE AND FEDERAL AGENCIES FOR INFORMATION ON PLANT, ANIMAL AND SOIL SCIENCES, FOREST SCIENCES AND RESOURCES MANAGEMENT. AFES PRIORITIES, LIKE NATIONAL PRIORITIES, ARE TO ENHANCE SUSTAINABILITY OF FOOD, FOREST, AND AGRICULTURAL SYSTEMS; ADAPT TO AND MITIGATE THE IMPACTS OF CLIMATE CHANGE; SUPPORT ENERGY SECURITY THROUGH THE DEVELOPMENT OF RENEWABLE NATURAL RESOURCES; ENSURE A SAFE, SECURE AND ABUNDANT FOOD SUPPLY; STRENGTHEN ENVIRONMENTAL STEWARDSHIP THROUGH THE DEVELOPMENT OF SUSTAINABLE MANAGEMENT PRACTICES; AND SUPPORT INDIVIDUAL, FAMILY AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT AND RESILIENCE. EXPERIMENT STATION RESEARCHERS WILL CONTINUE TO PUBLISH RESEARCH IN SCIENTIFIC JOURNALS, CONFERENCE PROCEEDINGS, BOOKS, AND IN EXPERIMENT STATION BULLETINS, CIRCULARS, NEWSLETTERS, RESEARCH PROGRESS REPORTS AND MISCELLANEOUS PUBLICATIONS. SCIENTISTS WILL ALSO DISSEMINATE THEIR FINDINGS THROUGH CONFERENCES, PUBLIC PRESENTATIONS, WORKSHOPS AND OTHER PUBLIC INFORMATION PROGRAMS LIKE WEBSITES AND BLOGS. AFES WILL MEET WITH AUDIENCES ON DEMAND THROUGHOUT THE STATE IN BOTH FORMAL AND INFORMAL SETTINGS EACH YEAR. EXAMPLES OF THESE AUDIENCES INCLUDE FORESTRY AND NATURAL RESOURCE ASSOCIATIONS, ALASKA NATIVE VILLAGES, TRIBAL ORGANIZATIONS AND REGIONAL CORPORATIONS, BOROUGH AND CITY GOVERNMENTS AND MUNICIPALITIES, GROWER GROUPS MEETING AT REGIONAL AND STATEWIDE CONFERENCES, INDUSTRY STAKEHOLDERS INVOLVED IN FUEL/ENERGY PRODUCTION, TRIBAL SOIL AND WATER C ONSERVATION DISTRICTS (TSWCDS) AND SOIL AND WATER CONSERVATION DISTRICTS (SWCDS), AND STATE AND FEDERAL PARTNERS INCLUDING BUT NOT LIMITED TO ALASKA DEPARTMENT OF NATURAL RESOURCES (INCLUDING THE DIVISION OF FORESTRY), USDA, NRCS, AND THE NATIONAL FOREST SERVICE. STAKEHOLDER INPUT WILL BE CONSIDERED IN PROGRAM PLANNING TO: IDENTIFY EMERGING ISSUES; REDIRECT EXTENSION AND RESEARCH PROGRAMS; GUIDE STAFF HIRING AND ACTION PLANS; SET DISTRICT AND UNIT-WIDE PRIORITIES; AND IDENTIFY UNDERSERVED POPULATIONS. AFES WILL CONTINUE TO SERVE THE NEEDS OF THE PEOPLE OF THE STATE OF ALASKA. INPUT WILL REFLECT IDEAS AND ADVICE GIVEN BY CLIENT USER GROUPS, STUDENTS, EXPERT ADVISORS, STATE AND NATIONAL PEERS AND COLLABORATORS AND UAF ADMINISTRATION. NEEDS ASSESSMENTS WILL CONTINUE TO HELP AFES FACULTY AND STAFF IDENTIFY EMERGING ISSUES. STAKEHOLDER NEEDS WILL CONTINUE TO BE A DRIVING FACTOR IN DETERMINING AFES PRIORITIES FOR RESEARCH.

THE OVERALL GOAL OF THE MCINTIRE-STENNIS PROJECT AT VIRGINIA STATE UNIVERSITY IS TO GAIN A COMPLETE UNDERSTANDING OF THE GRAZING BEHAVIOR AND PERFORMANCE OF SHEEP AND GOATS AND GENERATE INFORMATION ON THE PRIMARY MEANS BY WHICH SHEEP AND GOATS CAN BE INTEGRATED INTO AGRO FORESTRY PRODUCTION SYSTEM. SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES ARE TO: A) INTEGRATE INFORMATION ON SOIL COMPOSITION, FORAGE GROWTH, BIOMASS AND QUALITY, IN AGROFORESTRY PRODUCTION SYSTEM, B) GENERATE INFORMATION ON GRAZING BEHAVIOR USING GPS TRACKING SYSTEMS AND EVALUATE ANIMAL PERFORMANCE IN AGRO FORESTRY PRODUCTION SYSTEMS AND C) OYSTER MUSHROOM CULTIVATION ON THINNED LOGS. THE INTENTIONAL COMBINATION OF TREES, FORAGE, AND LIVESTOCK ON A PARCEL OF LAND TO MAXIMIZE MULTIPLE OUTPUTS HAS BEEN SHOWN TO HAVE BENEFITS. SUCH AGRICULTURAL PRACTICES HAVE LARGELY NOT BEEN STUDIED DESPITE A GREAT DEAL OF INTEREST. PRODUCERS WHO ARE INTERESTED IN LOCAL, NATURAL/ORGANIC FOOD, LIVESTOCK AND FORAGE AND FORESTRY PRODUCTION SYSTEMS SEE THIS FOREST-PASTURE-LIVESTOCK AS A POTENTIALLY SUSTAINABLE AND ENVIRONMENTALLY-FRIENDLY OPTION TO CONSERVE SOIL AND WATER, MAINTAIN AND INCREASE CARBON STOCKS, AND PROVIDE HABITAT FOR LIVESTOCK AND WILDLIFE. THE PURPOSE OF THIS PROJECT IS TO EVALUATE THE USE AND MANAGEMENT OF STANDS OF WOODLAND/FOREST, PASTURE AND LIVESTOCK ON THE SAME PIECE OF LAND IN A SUSTAINABLE PRODUCTION SYSTEM. THE STUDY FOCUSES ON THE GRAZING BEHAVIOR INCLUDING TEMPORAL AS WELL AS SPATIAL DISTRIBUTION OF SHEEP AND GOATS USING GPS COLLARS IN SUCH PRODUCTION SYSTEM. A GPS DATABASE LABORATORY WILL BE ESTABLISHED BY ACQUIRING GPS COLLARS AND ACCESSORIES. BASELINE INFORMATION IS ALSO COLLECTED ON FORAGE, LIVESTOCK, FOREST AND SOIL, WHICH WILL BE USED TO ESTIMATE CARRYING CAPACITY AND STOCKING DENSITY, ANIMAL PERFORMANCE FORAGE BIOMASS AND QUALITY. STAKEHOLDERS INCLUDING SMALL, TRADITIONAL AND URBAN FARMERS WILL BE TRAINED ON MUSHROOM CULTIVATION ON LOGS FROM THINNED FOREST AS AN ALTERNATIVE TO AUGMENT INCOME. RESEARCH ON INTEGRATION OF FOREST, PASTURE AND LIVESTOCK ON A PIECE OF LAND CAN BE BENEFICIAL IN INCREASING WATER AVAILABILITY, GREATER BIODIVERSITY, ENHANCED ECONOMIC OR SOCIAL RETURNS FROM FOREST LAND OWNERSHIP OR USAGE, AND DECREASED FIRE HAZARDS. STUDENTS WILL RECEIVE TRAINING AND EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING IN AGROFORESTRY. ESTABLISHMENT OF AGRO FORESTRY RESEARCH SITE FOR FUTURE STUDY.

HUMAN SOCIETIES HAVE A TENDENCY OF PLACING INCREASING VALUE ON LEISURE TIME, RESULTING IN INCREASED DEMAND FOR RECREATIONAL ACCESS TO PUBLIC LANDS. HUMAN PERCEPTIONS OF THE TANGIBLE AND INTANGIBLE BENEFITS THAT FOREST LANDSCAPES PROVIDE HAVE NOT BEEN STUDIED EXCLUSIVELY IN KENTUCKY PUBLIC LANDS. IN GENERAL, PUBLIC LANDS, SUCH AS NATIONAL FORESTS, PROVIDE IMPORTANT ECOLOGICAL, CULTURAL, AND ECONOMIC SERVICES THAT INCLUDE BIODIVERSITY, TIMBER PRODUCTION, AND RECREATIONAL OPPORTUNITIES. FOREST RECREATIONAL OPPORTUNITIES CAN CONSIST OF HUNTING, FISHING, HIKING, WALKING, CAMPING, CYCLING, HORSEBACK RIDING, SIGHTSEEING, ETC. GROWING DEMANDS FOR FOREST RECREATIONAL ACTIVITIES HAVE RESULTED IN THE NEED TO UNDERSTAND DEMOGRAPHIC AND SPATIAL DIMENSIONS OF VISITORS' ATTITUDES AND PERCEPTIONS TOWARDS VALUING RECREATIONAL RESOURCES AND ECOLOGICAL SERVICES OF PUBLIC LANDS. HIGH LEVELS OF FOREST RECREATIONAL USE CAN ENDANGER THE ECOLOGICAL STATUS OF FORESTS. A RECENT MEETING BETWEEN KENTUCKY STATE UNIVERSITY AND PERSONNEL FROM THE DANIEL BOONE NATIONAL FOREST, STATE FORESTERS, AND OTHER STATE AGENCIES SHOWED INCREASED INTEREST IN THE IMPORTANCE OF UNDERSTANDING PUBLIC PERCEPTIONS AND USE OF PUBLIC LANDS IN KENTUCKY. GEOSPATIAL CHARACTERIZATION OF RECREATION AREAS ALONG WITH SURVEYS AND ASSESSMENTS OF MANAGEMENT P RACTICES CAN HELP PROVIDE THE NEEDED INFORMATION ON TRENDS, DEMANDS, AND IMPORTANCE OF FOREST RECREATION IN KENTUCKY. THE EMERALD ASH BORER (EAB; AGRILUS PLANIPENNIS) HAS DEVASTATED THE ASH (FRAXINUS SPP.) POPULATION THROUGHOUT KENTUCKY AND ACROSS THE COUNTRY. EAB RESULTS IN DEAD STANDING ASH SNAG TREES THAT MAY HINDER FOREST RECREATION OPPORTUNITIES DUE TO THEIR POTENTIAL FOR FALLING. THE OVERALL IMPACT OF EAB ON FORESTS IS STILL UNKNOWN AS IS THE FUTURE OF THE ASH TREE. STUDIES NEED TO BE CONDUCTED TO ASSESS THE OVERALL IMPACT OF EAB ON FOREST ECOSYSTEMS AND TO DETERMINE WHICH SPECIES ARE REGENERATING IN IMPACTED AREAS, ESPECIALLY IN NORTHCENTRAL KENTUCKY WHERE BUSH HONEYSUCKLE, MULTIFLORA ROSE, GARLIC MUSTARD, AUTUMN OLIVE, AND OTHER INVASIVE SPECIES THRIVE IN DISTURBED AREAS. GROWING GINSENG MAY PROVIDE OPPORTUNITIES FOR SMALL-SCALE FOREST OWNERS AND FARMERS INCLUDING SOCIALLY DISADVANTAGED FARMERS/FOREST OWNERS IN KENTUCKY TO GENERATE INCOME WHILE IMPROVING AND MAINTAINING THE HEALTH OF THEIR FORESTS. FOREST-FARMING, AN AGROFORESTRY PRACTICE, HAS SHOWN PROMISE TO OPTIMIZE GINSENG PRODUCTION, HOWEVER, NO RESEARCH EXISTS TO ASSESS ITS POTENTIAL IN KENTUCKY. GINSENG IS GROWN FOR ITS HEALTH BENEFITS, AND MARKETS EXIST FOR THIS SPECIES; HOWEVER, FARMERS AND PRODUCERS IN KENTUCKY LACK KNOWLEDGE ABOUT GINSENG PRODUCTION UNDER VARIOUS GROWING CONDITIONS. THIS PROJECT WILL ASSESS GENSING PERFORMANCE AND PRODUCTION USING FOREST FARMING AND OTHER PRODUCTION METHODS. BEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES OF GROWING GINSENG WILL BE DEVELOPED UTILIZING THE RESULTS OF THE STUDY AND EXTENSION ACTIVITIES WILL BE OFFERED. THE BMPS WILL BE DESIGNED IN SUCH A WAY THAT KENTUCKYFARMERS CAN USE THEM TO IMPROVE THEIR LAND ECONOMIC PRODUCTION USING GINSENG PRODUCTION PRACTICES WHILE EMPLOYING SUSTAINABLE FOREST MANAGEMENT. THIS PROJECT WILL EVALUATE PARTICIPATION, TRENDS, AND DEMANDS FOR FOREST RECREATION BASED ON GEOSPATIAL CHARACTERIZATION AND SURVEYS AND TRAIL MANAGEMENT PRACTICES IN KENTUCKY. THE PROJECT WILL ALSO ASSESS THE IMPACT EAB HAS HAD ON KENTUCKY FORESTS. PROJECT INFORMATION METHODOLOGY OBJECTIVE 1: ASSESS FOREST RECREATION PREFERENCES INCLUDING GEOSPATIAL CHARACTERISTICS TO DETERMINE CURRENT DEMANDS AND TRENDS IN KENTUCKY. FOREST RECREATION SURVEYS WILL BE CONDUCTED IN THE FIELD AT POPULAR HIKING, BIKING, AND HORSE TRAILS, AS WELL AS AT CANOEING, KAYAKING, AND CAMPING SITES (TRAILHEADS FOR BACKCOUNTRY CAMPING) THROUGHOUT KENTUCKY. SURVEY FOCUS AREAS WILL CONSIST OF THE BERNHEIM ARBORETUM AND RESEARCH FOREST (BULLITT COUNTY), DANIEL BOONE NATIONAL FOREST (EASTERN KENTUCKY-APPALACHIAN REGION), BIG SOUTH FORK NATIONAL RIVER AND RECREATION AREA (EASTERN KENTUCKY), STATE PARKS AND FORESTS, AND CITY AND COUNTY PARKS IN LARGER CITIES SUCH AS LOUISVILLE, FRANKFORT, AND LEXINGTON. SURVEY QUESTIONS WILL BE RELATED TO CURRENT RECREATIONAL USE (HIKING, WATCHING BIRDS AND WILDLIFE, KAYAKING, CANOEING, HUNTING, ETC.), PREFERRED RECREATIONAL USE, FOREST MANAGEMENT IN RECREATION AREAS (PRESCRIBED BURNING, TIMBER HARVESTING, INVASIVE SPECIES REMOVAL, ETC.), AESTHETICS, SUSTAINABILITY, NON-TIMBER FOREST PRODUCTS, HOW OFTEN INDIVIDUALS USE RECREATIONAL AREAS, DISTANCE TRAVELED, DISTANCE WILLING TO TRAVEL, YOUTH PARTICIPATION, IMPROVEMENTS, AND FUTURE PLANNED USE. THE NUMBER OF SURVEY QUESTIONS WILL BE KEPT TO A MINIMUM AND QUESTIONS WILL BE SPECIFIC TO THE RECREATIONAL AREAS. RECREATION OPPORTUNITIES ON OR NEAR RECLAIMED MINE SITES WILL ALSO BE OF INTEREST. GIS CHARACTERIZATION WILL BE CONDUCTED FOR ALL RECREATION AREAS TO DETERMINE WHETHER CORRELATIONS EXIST BETWEEN USE AND RECREATION AREA CHARACTERISTICS (SLOPE, ASPECT, ACRES, VEGETATION, WATERFEATURES, ACCESS, DISTANCE FROM CITIES, ETC.). THERE WILL ALSO BE QUESTIONS RELATED TO EMERALD ASH BORER (EAB) ON THE SURVEY AND THE GEOSPATIAL ANALYSIS WILL ASSESS THE IMPACT OF EAB ON THOSE AREAS. THIS WILL RELATE TO OBJECTIVE 3 BELOW. WILDLIFE MANAGEMENT AREAS (WMAS) WILL ALSO BE TARGETED TO ASSESS FOREST USE PREFERENCES AND TRENDS ASSOCIATED WITH RECREATIONAL HUNTING. HUNTING SURVEYS WILL BE CONDUCTED AT WMA DEER AND OTHER WILDLIFE QUOTA CHECK STATIONS AS WELL AS AT LOCAL DEER PROCESSING FACILITIES TO ACCOUNT FOR HUNTERS WHO PRIMARILY HUNT ON PRIVATE LANDS. LEASE HUNTING IS BECOMING MORE POPULAR IN KENTUCKY AND WILL BE ASSESSED IN THESE SURVEYS. ALL SURVEYS WILL BE APPROVED BY KENTUCKY STATE UNIVERSITY PRIOR TO DISTRIBUTION. SURVEYS WILL BE CONDUCTED ON TABLETS (IPADS) AT THE DESIGNATED LOCATIONS USING A SOFTWARE PROGRAM SUCH AS SURVEYMONKEY OR SIMILAR PROGRAM THAT ALLOWS OFFLINE ACCESS ON TABLETS. THE MAJORITY OF THE SURVEYS WILL BE CONDUCTED BY STUDENTS. SURVEY DATA WILL BE DOWNLOADED INTO A DATABASE, SUCH AS MICROSOFT ACCESS AND EXCEL, AND WILL BE ANALYZED USING SAS, SPSS, OR R. OBJECTIVE 2: EVALUATE AND COMPARE FOREST RECREATIONAL TRAIL (HIKING, BIKING, AND HORSE TRAILS) DESIGN, IMPACT, AND MANAGEMENT ON EROSION AND SEDIMENT DELIVERY. IN ADDITION TO THE FOREST RECREATION SURVEYS, WE WILL ASSESS TRAIL DESIGN, IMPACT, AND MANAGEMENT ON WATER QUALITY AT STREAM CROSSINGS. EROSION, SEDIMENT DELIVERY, AND WATER QUALITY WILL BE THE MAIN VARIABLES ASSESSED. WILDLIFE AND PLANT SPECIES MAY ALSO BE OF INTEREST. TRAILS WILL BE DIVIDED INTO THREE CATEGORIES: HIKING, BIKING, AND HORSE TRAILS. ADDITIONALLY, EACH TRAIL WILL BE SUBDIVIDED BY WIDTH, TRAFFIC, MANAGEMENT PRACTICES, AND LOCATION. STREAM CROSSING APPROACHES WILL BE OF INTEREST AND EROSION AND SEDIMENT DELIVERY WILL BE ESTIMATED (TONS/ACRE/YEAR) USING THE UNIVERSAL SOIL LOSS EQUATION, REVISED UNIVERSAL SOIL LOSS EQUATION, AND WATER EROSION PREDICTION PROJECT (WEPP). EROSION AND SEDIMENT DELIVERY WILL BE MEASURED USING SEDIMENT TRAP AND PINS AND A TOTAL STATION TO MEASURE SEDIMENT LOSS IF VANDALISM WILL NOT BE A CONCERN. VANDALISM OF EROSION COLLECTION AND SAMPLING AREAS WILL BE A CONCERN ON PUBLIC TRAILS SO PRELIMINARY MEASUREMENTS WILL BE CONDUCTED TO DETERMINE METHODS TO REDUCE VANDALISM SUCH AS POSTING SIGNS ABOUT THE STUDY. SITE LOCATIONS WILL BE SIMILAR TO THE AREAS SELECTED IN OBJECTIVE 1. GIS CHARACTERIZATION OF THE SITE LOCATIONS WILL BE CONDUCTED AND A CORRELATION WILL BE COMPLETED BETWEEN EROSION RATES AND SITE CHARACTERISTICS. STATISTICAL ANALYSIS WILL BE CONDUCTED IN SAS, R, OR SAS-JMP. OBJECTIVE 3: ASSESS FOREST HEALTH -RELATED CANOPY GAPS, SPECIFICALLY EAB-RELATED CANOPY GAPS IN KENTUCKY, USING DRONE- BASED REMOTE SENSING AND FIELD MEASUREMENTS. STUDY AREAS WILL INCLUDE THE BERNHEIM ARBORETUM AND RESEARCH FOREST, KENTUCKY STATE UNIVERSITY'S ENVIRONMENTAL EDUCATION AND RESEARCH CENTER (EERC) LOCATED IN HENRY COUNTY, AND POSSIBLY THE DANIEL BOONE NATIONAL FOREST (ALTHOUGH THIS LOCATION HAS LIMITED ACCESS WITH APPROPRIATE LAUNCH SITES FOR DRONES). DRONES WILL BE USED TO COLLECT HIGH-RESOLUTION IMAGERY TO IDENTIFY TREES, CANOPY GAPS, AND STANDS AFFECTED BY EAB. NORMALIZED DIFFERENCE VEGETATION INDEX (NDVI) AND NORMALIZED DIFFERENCE RED EDGE (NDRE) SENSORS WILL BE USED TO DETERMINE CANOPY GAPS. CORRELATIONS WILL BE MADE TO DETERMINE ACCURACY OF NDVI FOR IDENTIFYING AREAS AFFECTED BY EAB. A RED-GREEN-BLUE (RBG) CAMERA WILL BE USED FOR AERIAL IMAGERY. AFTER COLLECTION OF AERIAL IMAGERY, EAB-IMPACTED AREAS WILL BE DOCUMENTED BY CANOPY GAP SIZE (ACRES); SURROUNDING STAND COMPOSITION: SINGLE ASH TREE, MIXED, OR ASH-DOMINATED (ASH DENSITY); AND GPS COORDINATES. THE GPS COORDINATES WILL BE USED TO LOCATE EAB-IMPACTED AREAS TO CONDUCT FIELD ASSESSMENTS. FIELD ASSESSMENTS WILL CONSIST OF THE COLLECTION OF PLOT-LEVEL DATA. FIELD DATA WILL INCLUDE: SPECIES GROWING IN EAB CANOPY GAPS (INCLUDING REGENERATION), SIZE OF SPECIES FO UND (HEIGHT, DIAMETER, CROWN WIDTH), PRESENCE/ABSENCE OF INVASIVE SPECIES, LEAF AREA INDEX (LAI), ETC. STATISTICAL ANALYSIS WILL COMPARE CANOPY GAP SIZE, SURROUNDING STAND COMPOSITION,SPECIES REGENERATING, INVASIVE SPECIES, AND LAI USING STATISTICAL SOFTWARE SUCH AS SAS, R, OR SAS-JMP. NDVI, NDRE, AND RBG IMAGERY WILL ALSO BE COMPARED WITH THE FIELD ASSESSMENTS TO DETERMINE HOW VALUES FROM THE DRONE SENSORS COMPARE TO VEGETATION GROWING IN THESE IMPACTED AREAS. THE USE OF DRONES FOR DETECTING CANOPY GAPS RELATED TO FOREST HEALTH CONCERNS WILL BE ADDRESSED. THE KENTUCKY DIVISION OF FORESTRY CURRENTLY MONITORS THE SPREAD AND STATEWIDE MORTALITY OF EAB AND THIS INFORMATION WILL BE INCORPORATED INTO THIS STUDY. OBJECTIVE 4: EVALUATE THE GROWTH, PRODUCTION, AND PERFORMANCE OF AMERICAN GINSENG (PANAX QUINQUEFOLIUS) GROWN UNDER FOREST FARMING AGROFORESTRY PRACTICE. A FACTORIAL EXPERIMENT WILL BE SET-UP AT THE EERC TO ADDRESS OBJECTIVE #4 USING THREE PRODUCTION METHODS OF GINSENG (I.E., WILD-SIMULATED, WOODS CULTIVATED, AND FIELD CULTIVATED), PLANTING DENSITY (I.E., LOW AND HIGH DENSITY), AND ASPECT (NORTH-FACING, AND SOUTH-FACING SLOPES). THE WILD-SIMULATED METHOD WILL INVOLVE SIMULATING THE GROWTH OF GINSENG GROWING IN THE WILD BY PLANTING THE SEEDS MANUALLY AFTER RAKING THE SOIL. UNDER THIS METHOD, THE SOIL WILL BE MINIMALLY DISTURBED. THE WOOD CULTIVATED METHOD WILL INVOLVE GROWING GINSENG IN FORESTED ENVIRONMENT IN TILLED BEDS UNDER NATURAL SHADE, AND THE FIELD-CULTIVATED METHOD WILL INVOLVE GROWING OF GINSENG IN RAISED BEDS IN FIELD UNDER ARTIFICIAL SHADE USING POLYPROPYLENE SHADE CLOTHES. PRIOR TO PLANTING, LIGHT AVAILABILITY IN THE WILD-SIMULATED AND WOOD-CULTIVATED PLOTS WILL BE MEASURED. THE AMOUNT OF LIGHT MEASURED WILL BE APPLIED TO GINSENG GROWING IN FIELD-CULTIVATED METHOD TO CREATE UNIFORMITY OF LIGHT TRANSMISSION AMONG TREATMENTS. POLYPROPYLENE SHADE CLOTH WILL BE USED IN FIELD-CULTIVATED METHOD. A TOTAL 40 RANDOM PLOTS WILL BE SET-UP FOR THE STUDY. EACH PLOT WILL MEASURE 5 FT X 25 FT. A LOW (25 LBS/ACRE) AND HIGH (50LBS/ACRE) PLANTING DENSITY WILL BE EMPLOYED IN THE STUDY AND PLOTS WILL BE SET-UP IN NORTH-FACING SLOPE (16 PLOTS), AND SOUTH-FACING SLOPE (16 PLOTS). SOIL ANALYSIS WILL BE ASSESSED PRIOR TO PLANTING, AND BASELINE DATA ON TREE GROWTH WILL BE ESTABLISHED. PARAMETERS TO MEASURE WILL INCLUDE SURVIVAL RATE, PHENOTYPIC CHARACTERISTICS, ROOT PRODUCTION AND QUALITY. 13

FOREST FARMING PRACTICES INVOLVE CULTIVATING HIGH-VALUE SPECIALTY CROPS IN THE FOREST UNDERSTORY WITH SPECIFIC MANAGEMENT OF THE CANOPY AND THE FOREST OVERSTORY TO PROMOTE THE GROWTH AND ESTABLISHMENT OF THE DESIRED CROP. THE UNDERSTORY OR SPECIALTY CROPS (NON-TIMBER FOREST PRODUCTS, NTFPS) CAN INCLUDE VARIOUS ITEMS FOR FOOD (MUSHROOMS AND NUTS), BOTANICALS (HERBS AND MEDICINAL), DECORATIVE (FLORAL GREENERY AND DYES), AND HANDICRAFTS (BASKETS ANN WOOD PRODUCTS). ALTHOUGH FOREST FARMING INVOLVES MODIFYING THE FOREST ECOSYSTEM, IF CORRECTLY DONE, THE PRIMARY FOREST FUNCTIONS ARE NOT NEGATIVELY IMPAIRED BUT ENHANCED. THIS STUDY IS DESIGNED TO EVALUATE THE FEASIBILITY OF FOREST FARMING OF FOUR MISSOURI NATIVE PERENNIAL HERBS BLACK COHOSH (ACTAEA RACEMOSA L.), RICHWEED (COLLINSONIA CANADENSIS L.), GOLDEN SEAL (HYDRASTIS CANADENSIS L.), AND GERANIUM (GERANIUM MACULATUM L.) AND THE IMPACT OF TIMBER STAND IMPROVEMENT (TSI) AND PRESCRIBED BURN (PB) ON FOREST ECOSYSTEM PROCESSES. THE SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES INCLUDE, I) EVALUATE THE ESTABLISHMENT AND PRODUCTIVITY OF SELECTED NATIVE HERB SPECIES IN MISSOURI WOODLANDS FOR FOREST FARMING, II) DETERMINE THE IMPACT OF ASSOCIATED FOREST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES (TIMBER STAND IMPROVEMENT AND PRESCRIBED BURN) ON PHOTOSYNTHETIC RESOURCE ALLOCATION, GREENHOUSE GAS EMISSIONS AND SOIL CHEMICAL PROPERTIES, AND III) MONITOR THE EFFECT OF FOREST FARMING ACTIVITIES ON SOIL MICROBIAL COMMUNITY AND FUNCTION. THIS PROJECT WILL BENEFIT SMALL FARMERS AND FORESTED LANDOWNERS IN MISSOURI AND THE MIDWESTERN US BY GENERATING ECONOMIC INCOME BY INCORPORATING FOREST FARMING PRACTICES. AS AN ADDED BENEFIT, FOREST HEALTH WILL ALSO IMPROVE FROM THE TSI AND PB TREATMENTS. PROJECT OUTCOMES WILL LEAD TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF BEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES FOR FOREST WOODLOTS AND PROMOTE BETTER DECISION-MAKING PROCESSES FOR FOREST LANDOWNERS, CONSERVATIONISTS, STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS, AND OTHER STAKEHOLDERS.

THE MCINTIRE-STENNIS PROGRAM IN THE UNIVERSITY OF THE VIRGIN ISLANDS STUDIES THE FORESTS OF THE USVI, BOTH ON A LAND SCAPE SCALE AND A SPECIES SCALE. IT FOCUSSES RESEARCH ON BOTH FEDERALLY ENDANGERED TREE SPECIES SUCH AS BUXUS VAHLII AND CATESBAEA MELANOCARPA AND LOCALLY ENDANGERED SPECIES SUCH AS GUAIACUM OFFICINALE AND ZANTHOXYLUM FLAVUM. IT IS NECESSARY TO STUDY SITE REQUIREMENTS SUCH AS SOIL AND CLIMATE, PHENOLOGY, AND SEED DISPERSAL IN ORDER TO PROPAGATE THESE SPECIES IN A NURSERY SETTING AND SUCCESSFULLY PLANT THEM IN THE FOREST. THE MCINTIRE-STENNIS PROGRAM ALSO PROMOTES THE PLANTING OF NATIVE TREES IN PUBLIC SPACES AS OPPOSED TO NURSERY STOCK IMPORTED INTO THE ISLANDS. SINCE THE MAJORITY LANDSCAPE OF THE US VIRGIN ISLANDS IS CONSIDERED URBAN, DUE TO NUMBERS OF INHABITANTS PER SQUARE MILE, A MAJOR CONSIDERATION IS “PLANTING THE RIGHT TREE IN THE RIGHT PLACE” TAKING IN CONSIDERATION TREE SIZE AND AVAILABLE PLANTING SPACE. THE CORRECT CARE OF TREES IN THE URBAN AND SUBURBAN ENVIRONMENT IS ALSO PROMOTED. IT ALSO ENCOURAGES THE PLANTING OF NATIVE TREES IN THE AGRICULTURAL LANDSCAPE FOR WINDBREAKS AND AS SHADE TREES FOR LIVESTOCK IN PASTURES.

THE UNIVERSITY OF PUERTO RICO AGRICULTURAL EXPERIMENT STATION MAINTAINS A SMALL BUT IMPORTANT FORESTRY RESEARCH PROGRAM FINANCED BY MCINTIRE-STENNIS FUNDS. THESE FUNDS SUPPORT RESEARCH ON USEFUL TECHNOLOGIES FOR REFORESTATION PROJECTS AND FOR THE MANAGEMENT OF WATERSHEDS RELATED TO FORESTS, ON THE ECONOMIC VIABILITY OF DEVELOPING RECREATIONAL OPPORTUNITIES IN FORESTS, AND ON ESTABLISHING USEFUL BASELINE DATA FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF MANAGEMENT PLANS OF SELECTED FORESTS. INTENDED BENEFICIARIES OF RESEARCH ACTIVITIES INCLUDE LOCAL GOVERNMENT AGENCIES SUCH AS THE DEPARTMENT OF NATURAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL RESOURCES, THE DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE AND THE PUERTO RICO PLANNING BOARD; RESIDENTS LIVING IN AREAS SURROUNDING THE FORESTS SELECTED FOR RESEARCH ACTIVITIES; THE SCIENTIFIC AND ACADEMIC COMMUNITY; AND PRIVATE AND PUBLIC ENTITIES INTERESTED IN REFORESTATION PROJECTS IN AREAS WITH LIMITED WATER SUPPLY. ACTIVITIES PLANNED INCLUDE: EXPERIMENTS WITH TECHNOLOGIES FOR OVERCOMING DROUGHT MORTALITY OF JUVENILE TREES IN REFORESTATION PROJECTSNALYSES OF SEDIMENT IN THREE RESERVOIRS CONSTRUCTED PRIOR TO 1950 TO RECONSTRUCT THE ECOLOGICAL EVOLUTION (>70 YR) OF THEIR WATERSHEDS AND ULTIMATELY USE THE INFORMATION TO DEVELOP A LOCAL FRAMEWORK FOR THE PLANNING OF SUSTAINABLE MULTIFUNCTIONAL LANDSCAPES IN PUERTO RICO.  CHOICE EXPERIMENTS TO EXAMINE RESIDENTS' WILLINGNESS TO PAY FOR RECREATIONAL OPPORTUNITIES IN SELECTED FORESTS AND COST-BENEFIT ANALYSES OF DEVELOPING THE INTENDED RECREATIONAL ACTIVITIES. THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A LONG-TERM, ECOLOGICAL RESEARCH STATION FOR THE STUDY OF LAND COVER CHANGE, CARBON AND BIODIVERSITY LINKAGES ON SERPENTINE SOILS, AS WELL AS THE BENEFITS NEIGHBORING COMMUNITIES MAY GAIN FROM THEIR INVOLVEMENT IN THE DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION OF A MANAGEMENT PLAN FOR THE STATION. DELIVERABLES FROM PROJECTS' ACTIVITIES INCLUDE PUBLICATION IN PEER REVIEWED JOURNALS AND POPULAR MEDIA OUTLETS (NEWSPAPERS, PODCASTS, SOCIAL MEDIA), POSTERS AND ORAL PRESENTATIONS ATSCIENTIFIC MEETINGS DEPICTING PROJECT RESULTS; AN UPDATED GEOGRAPHICAL INFORMATION SYSTEM CONTAINING LAND COVER, SOIL, AND GEOLOGICAL INFORMATION LAYERS OF THE THREE MAJOR WATERSHEDS OF PUERTO RICO; PROOF OF- CONCEPT OF UPSCALED EARTH-WATER DISTILLATION TECHNOLOGY FOR JUVENILE TREE IRRIGATION AND HUMAN CONSUMPTION IN REMOTE ARID AND SEMIARID ENVIRONMENTS; AND INCREASED DOCUMENTATION OF INTERACTIONS BETWEEN LAND COVER CHANGE, CARBON STORAGE CAPACITY AND BIODIVERSITY OF SERPENTINE SOILS IN THE CARIBBEAN. EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE AN INCREASED AWARENESS OF THE VALUE OF FORESTS ON THE ISLAND; THE INCORPORATION OF ECOLOGICAL TRADE-OFFS AS PART OF THE PLANNING PROCESS FOR SUSTAINABLE MULTIFUNCTIONAL LANDSCAPES IN PUERTO RICO; INCREASED PUBLIC AWARENESS AND USE OF SMALL COMMERCIALLY AVAILABLE WATER-VAPOR CONDENSATION DEVICES FOR MORE EFFECTIVE REFORESTATION IN ARID ENVIRONMENTS; AND INCREASED INFORMATION ON THE BENEFITS FROM CONSERVATION AND ECOSYSTEM SERVICES THAT FOREST LANDS CAN PROVIDE TONEIGHBORING RESIDENTS AND ACADEMIC COMMUNITIES.

negativeFlows.title: FORESTS HAVE PROVEN TO BE QUITE FLEXIBLE IN COMPARISON TO MANY OTHER LAND USE DESIGNATIONS AND CAN PROVIDE FOR A WIDE RANGE OF USES WHILE PROVIDING SOCIAL, ECONOMIC AND ENVIRONMENTAL BENEFITS. SPECIFICALLY, FOREST WATERSHEDS PROVIDE FOR A WEALTH OF PROVISIONING, REGULATING, AND SUSTAINING ECOSYSTEM SERVICES AND ARE A NEGLIGIBLE CONTRIBUTOR OF NON-POINT SOURCE POLLUTION AND CAUSES OF STREAM IMPAIRMENT. THE  FORESTED LANDSCAPE IN THE NATION FACES IMMENSE CHALLENGES WHICH DEMAND SCIENTIFIC INVESTIGATIONS TO PROVIDE APPROPRIATE SOLUTIONS TO THE CHALLENGES. AMONG THE CHALLENGES INCLUDE CLIMATE CHANGE, SUSTAINABILITY, LAND USE PRESSURE, APPROPRIATE FOREST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES, SOCIAL FACTORS AND WILDFIRES. ALABAMA IS THE FIFTH MOST FORESTED STATE IN THE UNITED STATES, WITH AN ESTIMATED 23,069,432 ACRES OF FOREST LAND, ACCOUNTING FOR 71% OF THE TOTAL LAND AREA. ALABAMA FOREST INDUSTRY JOB CONCENTRATION IS 2.57 TIMES THE NATIONAL JOB CONCENTRATION AND RANKED 3RD NATIONALLY IN THE FOREST PRODUCTS SECTOR'S CONTRIBUTION TO THE STATE ECONOMY.  FAMILY OWNERS CONTROL 71% OF THE PRIVATE FORESTLAND. MINORITY LANDOWNERS REPRESENT A RELATIVELY SMALL PROPORTION OF FOREST LANDOWNERS AND FORESTLAND (4.2% AND 1.4%, RESPECTIVELY). FORESTLAND OCCUPIES A SIGNIFICANT PART OF THE MINORITY FARMER LANDSCAPE, OFTEN REPRESENTING HALF OR MORE OF AGRICULTURAL LAND. HOWEVER, ONLY 3% OF OWNERS ACROSS THE SOUTH HAVE A MANAGEMENT PLAN. THERE IS THE NEED TO DEVELOP SUSTAINABLE AND BEST PRACTICES FOR FOREST MANAGEMENT ALTERNATIVES FOR LIMITED RESOURCE LANDOWNERS IN THE BLACK BELT REGION BY EXPLORING AND PRESENTING POTENTIAL STREAMS OF INCOME FOR THESE LANDOWNERS WHILE PROVIDING A PLATFORM FOR ENHANCED RESEARCH, EDUCATION, AND OUTREACH FOR STUDENTS AND STAKEHOLDERS. MANAGING FOR MULTIPLE USES CAN RANGE FROM TIMBER PRODUCTION, TO MANAGING FOR WILDLIFE HABITAT AND ASSOCIATED RECREATION ACTIVITIES, E.G., WILD GAME HUNTING. THESE USES ALSO INCLUDE WATER RESOURCES, SOIL HEALTH, AND OTHERS SERVICES. FURTHER, MANAGING FOR MULTIPLE USES IN A LESS CONVENTIONAL MANNER MAY TAKE THE FORM OF AGROFORESTRY SCHEMES THAT PRODUCE HIGH QUALITY TIMBER WHILE PROVIDING AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTS OR OPPORTUNITIES TO FORAGE FOR NON-TIMBER FOREST PRODUCTS. FOREST SYSTEMS ARE MULTI-FUNCTIONAL AND CAPABLE OF SUPPLYING A WIDE ARRAY OF SERVICES AND OUTPUTS; YET, LIMITED RESOURCE LANDOWNERS TYPICALLY HAVE SCANT KNOWLEDGE OF EITHER THE OPERATIONAL REQUIREMENTS FOR MAXIMIZING THESE OPPORTUNITIES OR THE FINANCIAL AND ECONOMIC BENEFITS ASSOCIATED WITH THEIR LANDS. OUR EFFORTS ARE THEREFORE  FOCUSED ON DEVELOPING RESEARCH PROGRAMS THAT ADDRESS THE NEEDS OF THIS SEGMENT OF THE FOREST AND LANDOWNERS. SPECIFICALLY, WE WILL CONDUCT RESEARCH ON: ADVANCING SUSTAINABILITY AND PROFITABILITY FOR SMALL-SCALE UNDER-REPRESENTED MINORITY FORESTRY LANDOWNERS; SUSTAINABLE FOREST MANAGEMENT AND RECREATIONAL USE FOR LIMITED RESOURCE LANDOWNERS IN THE BLACK BELT REGION;  AND ENHANCING THE GRAZING AND FEEDING OPPORTUNITY FOR LIVESTOCK BY EXPANDING SILVOPASTURE AND WOODLAND-GRAZING PRACTICES FOR LIMITED RESOURCE FOREST LANDOWNERS IN ALABAMA BLACK BELT REGION

IN 1962, PRESIDENT JOHN F. KENNEDY SIGNED THE MCINTIRESTENNIS COOPERATIVE FORESTRY ACT, 16 U.S.C 582A, ET SEQ., CREATING PUBLIC LAW 87788. THIS LEGISLATION PROVIDES A FEDERALLY SUPPORTED BASE FOR FORESTRY RESEARCH AND GRADUATE EDUCATION PROGRAMS AT STATECERTIFIED SCHOOLS OF FORESTRY ACROSS THE UNITED STATES. THE UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON HAS RECEIVED AN AWARD EACH YEAR FOR ALL 59 YEARS OF THE PROGRAM. THESE ARE FORMULA FUNDS; A VARIETY OF DATA POINTS, INCLUDING THE LEVEL OF ACTIVITY IN THE STATES TIMBER INDUSTRY, DETERMINE THE ANNUAL AMOUNT THAT OUR UNIVERSITY RECEIVES. RECIPIENTS CAN USE THIS FUNDING AS DIRECT SUPPORT FOR SPECIFIC RESEARCH PROJECTS OR INDIRECTLY TO PROVIDE ADMINISTRATIVE SUPPORT FOR FORESTRELATED RESEARCH. AREAS CURRENTLY SUPPORTED INCLUDE ANALYSIS OF FOREST ECOSYSTEMS; MANAGEMENT OF THREATENED AND ENDANGERED MAMMALIAN SPECIES ON HUMANALTERED LANDSCAPES; CLIMATE CHANGE MITIGATION; AND NOVEL APPROACHES TO ECOLOGICAL RESTORATION. THE UW SCHOOL OF ENVIRONMENTAL AND FOREST SCIENCES AWARDS NEW PROJECTS COMPETITIVELY TO MEMBERS OF ITS FACULTY. ITS RESEARCH COMMITTEE SELECTS PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATORS WITH A GOAL OF ENCOURAGING HIGHLY IMPACTFUL RESEARCH THAT WILL PROVIDE TRAINING OPPORTUNITIES FOR GRADUATE STUDENTS AND HAVE A LONGTERM, POSITIVE EFFECT ON FORESTS AND NATURAL RESOURCES NATIONWIDE. SCOPE OF WORK 2023 MCINTIRESTENNIS A183946 IN 1962, PRESIDENT JOHN F. KENNEDY SIGNED THE MCINTIRESTENNIS COOPERATIVE FORESTRY ACT, 16 U.S.C 582A, ET SEQ., CREATING PUBLIC LAW 87788. THIS LEGISLATION PROVIDES A FEDERALLY SUPPORTED BASE FOR FORESTRY RESEARCH AND GRADUATE EDUCATION PROGRAMS AT STATECERTIFIED SCHOOLS OF FORESTRY ACROSS THE UNITED STATES. THE UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON HAS RECEIVED AN AWARD EACH YEAR FOR ALL 58 YEARS OF THE PROGRAM. THESE ARE FORMULA FUNDS; A VARIETY OF DATA POINTS, INCLUDING THE LEVEL OF ACTIVITY IN THE STATES TIMBER INDUSTRY, DETERMINE THE ANNUAL AMOUNT THAT OUR UNIVERSITY RECEIVES. RECIPIENTS CAN USE THIS FUNDING AS DIRECT SUPPORT FOR SPECIFIC RESEARCH PROJECTS OR INDIRECTLY TO PROVIDE ADMINISTRATIVE SUPPORT FOR FORESTRELATED RESEARCH. THE ACT SEEKS TO PROMOTE FORESTRY EDUCATION, SO MOST MCINTIRESTENNIS FUNDING GOES TOWARD STUDENT SUPPORT. THE MCINTIRESTENNIS PROGRAM CURRENTLY FUNDS 2 RESEARCH PROJECTS AT THE UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON SCHOOL OF ENVIRONMENTAL AND FOREST SCIENCES: 1. PRODUCTION OF BIODEGRADABLE PLASTIC COMPOSITES USING FOREST SOURCED MATERIALS (ACCESSION #7003635, PD RICK GUSTAFSON) NANO CELLULOSE IS A REMARKABLE MATERIAL THAT CAN HAVE MULTIPLE USES; A MAJOR ONE BEING TO IMPROVE THE BIODEGRADABILITY OF POLYMER PRODUCTS. CURRENTLY IT HAS LIMITED USE BECAUSE OF THE HIGH COST. TECHNOLOGY DEVELOPED IN SEFS LOWERS THE COST BY TWO ORDERS OF MAGNITUDE. AT $10/KG THERE WILL BE MANY USES OF NANO CELLULOSE AND A LARGE DEMAND FOR RAW MATERIALS TO PRODUCE NANO CELLULOSE, SUCH AS FOREST RESIDUALS. IN THE PRODUCTION OF NANO CELLULOSE WE STRIP THE BIOMASS DOWN TO THE CELLULOSE FIBRILS; THEREFORE, RESIDUAL MATERIALS AREGOOD STARTING MATERIALS BECAUSE THEY ARE CHEAP AND ALREADY PARTIALLY DEGRADED. RESIDUALS CANNOT BE USED FOR PRODUCTS SUCH AS PULP BECAUSE THE FIBERS ARE TOO DEGRADED. LOWCOST NANO CELLULOSE HAS THE POTENTIAL TO TOTALLY REINVIGORATE THE DOMESTIC FOREST PRODUCTS INDUSTRY. THIS PROJECT WILL TRAIN A GRADUATE STUDENT WHO CAN HELP DEVELOP THIS NEW FOREST PRODUCTS MARKET. THE WORK WITH SQUAXIN ISLAND TRIBE WILL FORGE A NEW RELATIONSHIP THAT WE CAN BUILD ON WITH FUTURE RESEARCH INITIATIVES AND THE WHOLE PROJECT WILL DEMONSTRATE THE IMPORTANCE OF MCINTIRESTENNIS FUNDING TO DEVELOP NEW TECHNOLOGIES IN CLOSE COLLABORATION WITH OUR TRIBAL PARTNERS. 2. MODELBASED COUPLING OF WINTER HARDINESS AND SPRING PHENOLOGY IN PACIFIC NORTHWEST CONIFERS (ACCESSION #7003636, PD SOOHYUNG KIM) AS DOUGLASFIR IS A CULTURALLY, ECONOMICALLY, AND ECOLOGICALLY IMPORTANT SPECIES, THIS WORK WILL IMPACT BROAD AUDIENCE INCLUDING STAKEHOLDERS SUCH AS WA DEPARTMENT OF NATURAL RESOURCES (DNR) AND US FOREST SERVICE (USFS). THIS PROPOSED WORK CAN LEVERAGE EXISTING RELATIONSHIPS WITHIN EACH OF THESE AGENCIES TO ACCESS PLANT MATERIALS FOR ASSESSMENT, DISSEMINATE RESULTS, AND PROVIDE IMPLEMENTATION SUPPORT. THE KEY OUTCOME OF THIS PROJECT WILL BE A PREDICTIVE MODEL THAT WILL IMPROVE THE UNDERSTANDING OF COLD HARDINESS AND SPRING PHENOLOGY OF CONIFERS, IDENTIFY THE DRIVING FACTORS OF THESE TRAITS, IMPROVE THE APPLICATION OF PHENOLOGY TO SPECIES DISTRIBUTION MODELS, AND DETERMINE SENSITIVITY OF POPULATIONS TO ADVERSE EFFECTS. THE RESULTS OF THIS MODEL WILL QUANTIFY THE RISK OF NEGATIVE OUTCOMES ON FOREST HEALTH, FOREST PRODUCTIVITY, AND POTENTIAL FAILURE OF FOREST REFORESTATION AND RESTORATION. THE DRIVING FACTORS OF POPULATION ADAPTATION AND INDIVIDUAL ACCLIMATION OF COLD HARDINESS AND BUD BURST WILL BE DETERMINED BY USING PHYSIOLOGYDRIVEN MODEL AUGMENTED BY MACHINE LEARNING (ML) METHODS. OUR MODELING APPROACH CAN SERVE AS A POTENTIAL TEMPLATE FOR FUTURE INVESTIGATION OF PHENOLOGICAL TRAITS

PROJECT SUMMARY PROJECT PURPOSE: COUSINS/KOST: BEECH LEAF DISEASE (BLD) IS A DAMAGING NOVEL DISEASE RAPIDLY SPREADING THROUGH FORESTS IN EASTERN NORTH AMERICA. THE FIRST CASES OF BLD WERE CONFIRMED IN MICHIGAN IN 2022. WE WILL 1) BEGIN DESCRIBING THE CURRENT AND EXPECTED IMPACTS OF BLD ON FORESTS AND ECOSYSTEM SERVICES IN THE REGION AND 2) BUILD RESPONSE CAPACITY BY TRAINING PRACTITIONERS IN FOREST ECOLOGY, INVASION BIOLOGY, AND MANAGEMENT APPROACHES, AND BY INCREASING REGIONAL BLD PREPAREDNESS. IBANEZ/CLASSEN: TO QUANTIFY THE CAPACITY OF FORESTS TO RECOVER (RESILIENCE) FROM EXTREME WATER OR PRODUCTIVITY LOSSES ACROSS THE BOR EAL-TEMPERATE ECOTONE IN MICHIGAN'S UPPER LOWER AND EASTERN UPPER PENINSULAS. WANG/ALOFS: THIS PROJECT AIMS TO INVESTIGATE THE EFFECT OF FOREST CHARACTERISTICS IN MITIGATING CLIMATE CHANGE INFLUENCE ON WATER QUALITY AND FISH. WE WILL DERIVE THE INTERACTION EFFECTS BETWEEN FOREST CHARACTERISTICS (E.G., FOREST SPECIES COMPOSITION, DIVERSITY, FOREST SPATIAL FRAGMENTATION, CHANNEL WOOD COUNT, RIPARIAN VEGETATION QUALITY) AND CLIMATE FACTORS ON STREAM PH, NITROGEN, PHOSPHORUS, SUSPENDED SOLID CONCENTRATION, AND FISH DIVERSITY INDICES. WE WILL ALSO EXPLORE THE POTENTIAL MECHANISMS ON HOW FOREST AND CLIMATE JOINTLY AFFECT FISH COMMUNITY COMPOSITION WITH PHYSICAL-BASED MODELS. BERGEN/ALLAN/BRINES: THIS PROJECT IS FOCUSED ON GEOSPATIAL DATA AND ANALYSES TO SUPPORT FOREST HEALTH AND SUSTAINABILITY PLANNING WITHIN THE NEWLY RE-ENVISIONED OBR). THE PROJECT STRIVES TO ANSWER: 1) WHAT IS THE SPATIAL DISTRIBUTION OF FOREST AND OTHER LAND STEWARDSHIP OF THE OBR REGION ACROSS ALL OWNERSHIP AND MANAGEMENT TYPES? 2) WHAT ARE THE SPATIAL DISTRIBUTIONS AND MAGNITUDES OF FOREST BIOMASS/CARBON PLUS OTHER KEY FOREST CHARACTERISTICS OF THE OBR REGION? 3) WHERE ARE SUSTAINABILITY OPPORTUNITIES IN THE OBR FOR FOREST CARBON-RELATED MARKETS, AS WELL AS SUSTAINABILITY RISKS FROM DEVELOPMENT AND FOREST HEALTH STRESSORS? WHYTE/FISCHER: THIS PROPOSAL SEEKS SUPPORT FOR RESEARCH TO DEVELOP MODELS FOR RESTITUTING FIRE STEWARDSHIP BACK TO TRIBES AND ELEVATING TRIBAL PRIORITIES FOR NATIVE FIRE STEWARDSHIP IN FEDERAL LAND MANAGEMENT. NATIVE FIRE RESTITUTION HAS BEEN RECOGNIZED AS AN IMPORTANT STRATEGY FOR IMPROVING MANAGEMENT OF FORESTS FOR GAME AND WILDLIFE; PROTECTION OF FORESTS AGAINST FIRE, INSECTS, DISEASES, OR OTHER DESTRUCTIVE AGENTS; AND DEVELOPMENT OF SOUND POLICIES FOR THE MANAGEMENT OF FOREST LANDS FOR ECOLOGICAL RESTORATION, CATASTROPHE MANAGEMENT, CLIMATE CHANGE ADAPTATION, AND IMPROVED HEALTH. HOWEVER, MODELS FOR FIRE RESTITUTION ARE LACKING IN THE SCHOLARLY AND POLICY LITERATURES. ACTIVITIES TO BE PERFORMED: COUSINS/KOST: THIS PROJECT WILL EXAMINE THE DISTRIBUTION AND PROGRESSION OF BLD IN VULNERABLE MICHIGAN FORESTS BY ESTABLISHING A SURVEY AND MONITORING NETWORK. THE COLLECTED INFORMATION WILL CONTRIBUTE TO NEW RESEARCH INVESTIGATING THE ANTICIPATED PATTERNS OF FOREST CHANGE THAT BLD COULD REALISTICALLY DRIVE; IT WILL ALSO INFORM EARLY-RESPONSEACTIONS IN THE REGION. AS PART OF THIS EFFORT, WE WILL ALSO CREATE OPPORTUNITIES FOR MENTORED PROFESSIONAL DEVELOPMENT AND ON-THE-JOB TRAINING IN ENVIRONMENTAL MANAGEMENT FOR GRADUATE STUDENTS AT THE UNIVERSITY OF MICHIGAN AND INTERNS AT MATTHAEI BOTANICAL GARDENS AND NICHOLS ARBORETUM. 11/15 IBANEZ/CLASSEN: I) IDENTIFY STRESSORS OF CONCERN TO WATER AND PRODUCTIVITY LOSSES FOR THE FOREST ECOSYSTEM TYPES IN OUR STUDY REGION AND ASSESS VULNERABILITY TO THOSE STRESSORS. II) INFORM RESISTANCE AND RESILIENCE STRATEGIES VIA MANAGEMENT ASSESSMENT TOOLS BY ASSESSING A PRIORI THE OUTCOMES OF DIFFERENT PRACTICES (E.G., CONVENTIONAL: PLANTING, THINNING, HARVESTING; TRADITIONAL: PRESCRIBED BURNING, PRESERVING CULTURALLY SIGNIFICANT SPECIES, PROVIDING WILDLIFE HABITAT). WANG/ALOFS: WE WILL CARRY OUT THE STUDY IN THE GREAT LAKES BASIN, INCLUDING PARTS OF MICHIGAN, WISCONSIN, MINNESOTA, NEW YORK, OHIO, PENNSYLVANIA, ILLINOIS, AND INDIANA. USING THE DATA FROM THE NATIONAL RIVER AND STREAM ASSESSMENT (NRSA) AND OTHER OPEN-SOURCE CLIMATE AND FOREST DATASETS, WE WILL FIRST PERFORM STATISTICAL ANALYSIS TO IDENTIFY THE MOST IMPORTANT CLIMATE AND FOREST CHARACTERISTICS FACTORS TO PREDICT WATER QUALITY AND FISH COMMUNITY COMPOSITION. WE WILL ALSO USE SOIL <(>&<)> WATER ASSESSMENT TOOL (SWAT) TO INVESTIGATE HOW WATER QUALITY REACTS TO THE CHANGING CLIMATE AND FOREST MANAGEMENT, AS WELL AS PREDICT THE IMPACT ON FISH DIVERSITY WITH THE DERIVED STATISTICAL RELATIONSHIP FROM THE FIRST STEP. BERGEN/ALLAN/BRINES: GEOSPATIAL DATA AND VISUALIZATION, OBR-WIDE STATISTICS, AND SCIENTIST-STEWARD CO-CREATED RASTER GIS SUITABILITY/RISK MODELS WILL FORM AN INTEGRATIVE APPROACH TO ADDRESSING OBR START-UP NEEDS. THE PROJECT WILL: 1) COMPILE MULTIPLE REGIONAL-SCALE GEOSPATIAL DATASETS CUSTOMIZED TO THE NEWLY RE-ENVISIONED OBR; 2) ANALYZE GEOSPATIAL DATA TO PRODUCE OBR-WIDE MAPS AND STATISTICS; DEVELOP CO-CREATED GIS SUITABILITY/RISK MODELS FOR SELECTED FOREST CARBON OPPORTUNITIES AND DEVELOPMENT/HEALTH RISKS. WHYTE/FISCHER: THIS PROPOSAL SEEKS SUPPORT FOR QUALITATIVE RESEARCH TO DEVELOP MODELS FOR RESTITUTING FIRE STEWARDSHIP BACK TO TRIBES AND ELEVATING TRIBAL PRIORITIES FOR NATIVE FIRE STEWARDSHIP IN FEDERAL LAND MANAGEMENT. WE WILL USE A CASE STUDY APPROACH TO PURSUE OUR RESEARCH OBJECTIVES. THE CASE STUDY METHOD REFERS TO EMPIRICAL INVESTIGATION OF A CONTEMPORARY PHENOMENON IN ITS REAL-WORLD CONTEXT USING MULTIPLE SOURCES OF DATA THAT WILL BE ANALYZED QUALITATIVELY. DELIVERABLES AND EXPECTED OUTCOMES: COUSINS/KOST: WE WILL PRODUCE: 1) CURRENT INFORMATION ON THE DISTRIBUTION AND SEVERITY OF BLD IN VULNERABLE SE MICHIGAN FORESTS AND 2) A MANSUSCRIPT EXAMINING EXPECTED STRUCTURAL AND ECOLOGICAL CHANGES IN FORESTS IMPACTED BY BLD. ADDITIONALLY, WE WILL CREATE AND INSTALL 3) INTERPRETIVE EXHIBITS AND/OR EDUCATIONAL MATERIALS FOR DISTRIBUTION TO THE PUBLIC AND DEVELOP 4) A GRANT PROPOSAL FOR CONTINUED WORK. THESE ACTIONS WILL CONTRIBUTE NEW, VALUABLE INFORMATION TO NASCENT SCIENTIFIC UNDERSTANDING OF BLD AND BOLSTER PROTECTION OF FOREST ECOSYSTEMS AGAINST BOTH THIS DISEASE AND OTHER DESTRUCTIVE AGENTS. IBANEZ/CLASSEN: PROVIDE PROJECTIONS OF BOTH RESILIENCE METRICS FOR THE LATE 21 ST CENTURY BASED ON AN ARRAY OF FUTURE CLIMATE SCENARIOS AND MANAGEMENT PRACTICES. OUTCOMES FROM THESE ANALYSES WILL BRING CRUCIAL INSIGHTS ON HOW FOREST PRODUCTIVITY AND WATER ECOSYSTEM SERVICES PROVIDED BY FORESTS MIGHT BE IMPACTED BY CLIMATE CHANGE AND HOW DIFFERENT MANAGEMENT APPROACHES COULD MODIFY THOSE RESPONSES. WANG/ALOFS: WE HAVE TWO EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDING (1) THE LEVERAGED NRSA DATASET WITH FOREST CHARACTERISTICS AND CLIMATE FACTORS (INCLUDING CLIMATE NORMAL, EXTREME, AND SEASONALITY VARIABLES). THIS OPEN DATASET WILL ENABLE FUTURE STUDIES TO EXPLORE THE FUNCTIONAL RELATIONSHIP BETWEEN FOREST, CLIMATE, AND WATER QUALITY. (2) THE PREDICTED WATER QUALITY AND FISH COMPOSITION UNDER DIFFERENT FOREST MANAGEMENT AND CLIMATE CHANGE SCENARIOS. ACCORDING TO THE PREDICTION, WE WILL PROPOSE GUIDELINES FOR ECOLOGICAL RESTORATION POLICY THAT MITIGATES CLIMATE CHANGE EFFECTS ON STREAM CONTAMINATION AND BIODIVERSITY DEGRADATION WITH FOREST MANAGEMENT APPROACHES. BERGEN/ALLAN/BRINES: THE PROJECT WILL PROVIDE A BROAD SET OF GIS DATABASES ON OBR FORESTS, LAND STEWARDSHIP, FOREST HEALTH AND FOREST PRODUCTIVITY CUSTOMIZED TO THE OBR. DELIVERABLES WILL ALSO INCLUDE STATISTICAL AND MODELED SUMMARIES RESULTING FROM GIS MODELING. THE PROJECT WILL ALSO PRODUCE REPORTS AND PUBLICATIONS. WE WILL ALSO SOLICIT STEWARD-PARTNER INPUT AND FEEDBACK ON FUTURE DIRECTIONS. WHYTE/FISCHER: THE MAJOR DELIVERABLE WILL BE A REPORT AND SET OF PUBLISHED PEER REVIEWED ARTICLES FLOWING FROM THE REPORT THAT WILL FURNISH MODELS OF PROVEN STRATEGIES, BEST PRACTICES, AND POLICY OPPORTUNITIES REGARDING NATIVE FIRE STEWARDSHIP AND NATIVE FIRE RES TITUTION.  INTENDED BENEFICIARIES: COUSINS/KOST: BENEFICIARIES OF THE PROJECT INCLUDE LAND MANAGERS AND FOREST STEWARDS AT ORGANIZATIONS, AGENCIES, LOCAL/REGIONAL GOVERNMENTS, AND PRIVATE HOLDINGS, AS WELL AS THE MICHIGAN DEPARTMENT OF NATURAL RESOURCES FOREST HEALTH PROGRAM. MANAGERS OF BEECH (FAGUS GRANDIFOLIA) TREES AND FORESTS WILL ESPECIALLY BENEFIT. TRAINEES WILL ALSO GAIN THE ADVANTAGES OF HANDS-ON EXPERIENCE IN ASSESSING TREE HEALTH, MEASURING FOREST ECOSYSTEMS, AND EXAMINING EFFECTIVE INVASIVE SPECIES MANAGEMENT. IBANEZ/CLASSEN: WE WILL ENGAGE IN ITERATIVE DISCUSSIONS WITH SAULT TRIBE AND OTHER LAND MANAGERS TO DEFINE NEEDS THAT SHOULD BE ADDRESSED, THE VALIDITY AND USABILITY OF THE RESEARCH PRODUCTS (ACTIONABLE SCIENCE), SYNERGY WITH ANISHINAABE KNOWLEDGES AND FOREST RELATIONS, AS WELL AS THE PLAUSIBILITY OF THE OUTPUTS AND POTENTIAL USE BY NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGERS MORE BROADLY (APPLICABILITY). BERGEN/ALLAN/BRINES: THE PRIMARY BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE THE CORE UMBS,PLUS THE DIVERSE LAND STEWARDS OF THE BROADER OBR. THE LATTER ARE COMPRISED OF LOCAL, STATE, AND FEDERAL LAND MANAGEMENT ENTITIES; LAND CONSERVANCIES; TRIBAL LANDS AND LEADERSHIP; LARGE INDUSTRIAL AND INVESTMENT LANDOWNERS; AND SMALL NON-INDUSTRIAL PRIVATE LANDOWNERS. BENEFICIARIES ALSO INCLUDE RESEARCHERS AND GRADUATE STUDENTS WHO WILL WORK ON THIS FOREST HEALTH AND SUSTAINABILITY PROJECT. WHYTE/FISCHER: THESE MODELS WILL GUIDE FUTURE FIRE AND LAND MANAGEMENT, HELPING SOCIETY ADDRESS THE GROWING NEED FOR ECOLOGICAL RESTORATION, CLIMATE CHANGE ADAPTATION, AND MITIGATION OF CATASTROPHIC WILDFIRE RISK IN ECOLOGICALLY AND CULTURALLY IMPORTANT FORESTS OF THE UPPER MIDWEST AND ELSEWHERE. THE MODELS WILL DEMONSTRATE THE IMPORTANCE OF TRIBAL SELF-DETERMINATION IN FIRE STEWARDSHIP.
