negativeFlows.title: THE OBJECTIVE OF THE MCINTIRE-STENNIS (M-S) COOPERATIVE FORESTRY RESEARCH PROGRAM IN THE WARNELL SCHOOL OF FORESTRY AND NATURAL RESOURCES AT THE UNIVERSITY OF GEORGIA (UGA) IS TO ASSIST THE STATE IN CARRYING OUT AN APPLIED RESEARCH PROGRAM WHOSE OUTCOMES SUPPORT THE SUSTAINABLE MANAGEMENT OF OUR FOREST LANDS TO PROVIDE MULTIPLE BENEFITS FOR PEOPLE AND NATURE. IN DOING SO, AN ADDITIONAL PRIMARY OBJECTIVE IS TO DEVELOP A POOL OF WELL-TRAINED FOREST SCIENTISTS TO SUPPORT RESEARCH AND PRACTICE. THE M-S PROGRAM AT UGA SUPPORTS RESEARCH IN ALL THE FEDERAL PROGRAM'S FOCUS AREAS. IN THE AREA OF (1) REFORESTATION AND MANAGEMENT OF LAND FOR TIMBER PRODUCTION AND OTHER RELATED FOREST PRODUCTS, ONE SUB-PROJECT WILL EVALUATE GENETICALLY IMPROVED PLANTATIONS RELATIVE TO UNIMPROVED PLANTATIONS IN TERMS OF STAND DYNAMICS, WOOD QUALITY, AND GROWTH AND YIELD. TARGET AUDIENCES INCLUDE FORESTLAND MANAGERS, FOREST INDUSTRY PLANNERS, AND PRIVATE FORESTLAND OWNERS. A SECOND SUBPROJECT IN THIS AREA ADVANCESOPERATIONS RESEARCH METHODOLOGY THAT CAN IMPROVE FOREST PLANNING PROCESSES, LEADING TO FOREST PLANS THAT ARE FEASIBLE, EFFICIENT, AND SUSTAINABLE. ACTIVITIES INCLUDE THE DEVELOPMENT OF A NEW MODEL FOR HARVEST SCHEDULING. TARGET AUDIENCES INCLUDE FOREST MANAGERS, ANALYSTS, LANDOWNERS AND LAND MANAGEMENT PLANNERS. FINALLY, A THIRD SUBPROJECT EVALUATES HOW WATER USE EFFICIENCY AND SOIL ORGANIC CARBON RESPOND TO ENVIRONMENTAL FACTORS, DISTURBANCES, AND SILVICULTURAL TECHNIQUES OVER TIME PERIODS RELEVANT TO FOREST ROTATIONS. TARGET AUDIENCES INCLUDE OF LANDOWNERS, LAND MANAGERS, STUDENTS, AND SCIENTISTS FROM A VARIETY OF DISCIPLINES INTERESTED IN THE SUSTAINABILITY OF FOREST PRODUCTION. IN THE AREA OF (2) MANAGEMENT OF FOREST AND RELATED WATERSHED LANDS TO IMPROVE CONDITIONS OF WATER FLOW AND TO PROTECT RESOURCES AGAINST FLOODS AND EROSION, A SUBPROJECT IS FOCUSED ON THE EFFECTIVENESS OF ENHANCED FORESTRY BEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES (EBMPS) THAT HELP TO ENSURE THAT PRIVATE AND INDUSTRIAL FORESTLANDS IN THE SOUTHEAST PROVIDE A WIDE RANGE OF ECOSYSTEM SERVICES IN ADDITION TO WOOD PRODUCTS, INCLUDING TERRESTRIAL AND AQUATIC HABITATS FOR NATIVE SPECIES, RECREATION, CLEAN AIR AND WATER, AND MITIGATION AGAINST FLOODS AND DROUGHTS. THIS PROJECT WILL INVESTIGATE THE WATER QUANTITY AND QUALITY BENEFITS OF EBMPS AND DEVELOP STRATEGIES TO COMPENSATE AND ENCOURAGE FOREST LANDHOLDERS TO IMPLEMENT THESE PRACTICES. TASKS INCLUDE EVALUATION OF EBMP EFFECTIVENESS, ESTABLISHMENT OF A MULTISTAKEHOLDER COLLABORATION FOR OUTREACH/EDUCATION PROGRAMMING, AND IMPLEMENTATION OF A DEMONSTRATION PROJECT TO SHOW THE VALUE OF IMPROVED FOREST MANAGEMENT TO WATER SUPPLY AND QUALITY. IN THE AREA OF (3) MANAGEMENT OF FOREST AND RELATED RANGELAND FOR PRODUCTION OF FORAGE FOR DOMESTIC LIVESTOCK AND GAME AND IMPROVEMENT OF FOOD AND HABITAT FOR WILDLIFE, SEVERAL SUBPROJECTS INVESTIGATE HOW FOREST LANDS CAN BE BEST MANAGED TO SUPPORT DIVERSE WILDLIFE AND FISHERY RESOURCES. BY MONITORING DEER, COYOTES, REPTILES, AMPHIBIANS, BIRDS, AND FISH, AND MODELING THEIR RESPONSES TO FOREST MANAGEMENT AND OTHER ENVIRONMENTAL FACTORS, THESE PROJECTS WILL BE ABLE TO MAKE SPECIFIC RECOMMENDATIONS TO LAND MANAGERS TO IMPROVE HABITAT FOR NATIVE SPECIES, ENSURE RECREATIONAL OPPORTUNITIES SUCH AS HUNTING, FISHING, AND BIRD WATCHING, AND PROJECT HOW ENVIRONMENTAL CHANGE MAY IMPACT INDIVIDUAL SPECIES AND COMMUNITIES. TARGET AUDIENCES INCLUDE STATE AND FEDERAL AGENCIES AND OTHER LAND MANAGERS, INCLUDING PRIVATE LANDOWNERS AND NGO PARTNERS. IN THE AREA OF (4) MANAGEMENT OF FOREST LANDS FOR OUTDOOR RECREATION, ONE SUBPROJECT SEEKS TO ASSESS VISITATION TO TENNESSEE VALLEY AUTHORITY'S (TVA'S) STREAM ACCESS SITES, THE RECREATIONAL ACTIVITIES CONDUCTED ON-SITE BY VISITORS, AND THE ASSOCIATED ECONOMIC IMPACTS THAT VISITORS TO THESE STREAM ACCESS SITES HAVE ON LOCAL COMMUNITIES ACROSS TWO DIFFERENT REGIONS OF THE TENNESSEE VALLEY. THE PRIMARY METHODS INCLUDE RANDOM STRATIFIED EXIT SURVEYS AT STREAM ACCESS POINTS. USING SURVEY RESULTS COMBINED WITH VISITATION ESTIMATES, IT WILL BE POSSIBLE TO CALCULATE THE DIRECT, INDIRECT, AND INDUCED ECONOMIC IMPACTS OF THE STREAM ACCESS SITES, THUS RESULTING IN AN ESTIMATE OF THE TOTAL ECONOMIC IMPACT OF ALL TVA STREAM ACCESS SITES IN GEORGIA AND NORTH CAROLINA. THE INTENDED AUDIENCES WILL INCLUDE TVA OFFICIALS AND NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGERS AT THE FEDERAL AND STATE LEVEL. IN THE AREA OF (5) PROTECTION OF FOREST LAND AND RESOURCES AGAINST FIRE, INSECTS, DISEASES, OR OTHER DESTRUCTIVE AGENTS, ONE SUBPROJECT IS FOCUSED ON PROTECTION AND RESTORATION OF NORTH AMERICAN ASH SPECIES WHICH ARE UNDER THREAT OF EXTIRPATION FROM THEIR NATIVE RANGES BY THE EMERALD ASH BORER (EAB). THE PROJECT WILL INITIATE EMBRYOGENIC CULTURES FROM A VARIETY OF SPECIES AND SOURCES, PRODUCE SEEDLINGS FROM EMBRYOGENIC CULTURES, AND OPTIMIZE RECOVERY AND STORAGE PROTOCOLS FOR CONSERVATION PURPOSES. TARGET AUDIENCES INCLUDE OTHER EAB RESEARCHERS, USDA FOREST SERVICE, STATE FORESTRY AGENCIES, AND NGOS SUCH AS TREES ATLANTA. A SECOND SUBPROJECT IN THIS AREA INVESTIGATES THE BIOLOGY AND ECOLOGY OF NATIVE AND EXOTIC BARK AND WOODBORING INSECTS AND EVALUATES BEST MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES TO ACHIEVE SUSTAINABLE FOREST MANAGEMENT UNDER VARYING THREAT FROM THESE PESTS. A VARIETY OF EXPERIMENTAL AND OBSERVATIONAL APPROACHES WILL BE USED TO ASSESS THE EFFECTS OF FOREST MANAGEMENT FOREST CONDITION ON SUSCEPTIBILITY TO OUTBREAKS OF BARK AND WOODBORING INSECTS. TARGET AUDIENCES INCLUDE PRIVATE, STATE, AND FEDERAL AGENCIES, LANDOWNERS, AND FORESTERS. IN THE AREA OF (6) UTILIZATION OF WOOD AND OTHER FOREST PRODUCTS, ONE SUBPROJECT ADDRESSES THE STRUCTURE, PROFITABILITY, AND EFFICIENCY OF SMALL, INDEPENDENT LOGGING BUSINESSES, AND TO HELP THESE BUSINESSES BE MORE EFFICIENT AND PROFITABLE. THE SOUTHERN FOREST INDUSTRY IS RESPONSIBLE FOR $230 BILLION IN ECONOMIC OUTPUT OVER 1 MILLION JOBS. THE FOREST INDUSTRY DEPENDS ON THOUSANDS OF SMALL, INDEPENDENT LOGGING BUSINESSES TO HARVEST AND DELIVER TIMBERTO THEIR MILLS. VERY LITTLE IS KNOWN ABOUT THE STRUCTURE, PROFITABILITY, AND EFFICIENCY OF THESE BUSINESSES. THIS STUDY WILL CONDUCT A SURVEY OF GEORGIA AND SOUTH CAROLINA LOGGERS TO DETERMINE THEIR BUSINESS STRUCTURE, CAPITAL INVESTMENT, AND CHALLENGES FACED. THE STUDY WILL ALSO INVESTIGATE TRANSPORTATION SAFETY AND COST OF HARVESTING WOOD FOR ENERGY. RESULTS WILL ENABLE LOGGING BUSINESS OWNERS TO MAKE INFORMED DECISIONS THAT HELP THEM OPERATE MORE PROFITABLY AND DELIVER THE TIMBER NECESSARY TO SUPPORT THE FOREST PRODUCTS INDUSTRY. TARGET AUDIENCES INCLUDE FORESTERS, FOREST PRODUCTS INDUSTRY REPRESENTATIVES, AND RESEARCHERS. FINALLY, IN THE AREA OF (7) DEVELOPMENT OF SOUND POLICIES FOR THE MANAGEMENT OF FOREST LANDS AND THE HARVESTING AND MARKETING OF FOREST PRODUCTS, ONE SUBPROJECT WILL EVALUATE THE ROLE OF FARM REAL ESTATE IN A MIXED ASSET PORTFOLIO AND INVESTIGATE RISKS FOR TIMBERLAND INVESTMENTS. TARGET AUDIENCES INCLUDE FOREST LANDOWNERS, INVESTORS, TIMBERLAND INVESTMENT MANAGEMENT ORGANIZATIONS, REAL ESTATE INVESTMENT TRUSTS, AND OTHER RESEARCHERS. ANOTHER SUBPROJECT WILL ADDRESS THE NEED FOR A TIMELY ASSESSMENT OF FACTORS AFFECTING FOREST RESOURCES, MARKETS, AND ENVIRONMENTAL VALUES. THIS PROJECT WILL PROVIDE INFORMATION ON THE PROVISION OF FOREST ECOSYSTEM SERVICES, CLIMATE CHANGE MITIGATION, DEVELOPMENT OF INVESTMENT OPPORTUNITIES, AND NEEDS OF FAMILY FOREST OWNERS. A FINAL SUBPROJECT WILL USE IN-DEPTH CASE STUDIES, REPURPOSING OF EXISTING PERFORMANCE DATA, AND REMOTELY SENSED LAND COVER DATA TO EVALUATE THE DYNAMICS AND LANDSCAPE OUTCOMES OF COLLABORATIVE, CROSS-BOUNDARY FOREST MANAGEMENT POLICIES. COLLECTIVELY, THESE OUTCOMES WILL HELP TO IMPROVE THE DESIGN, IMPLEMENTATION, AND MONITORING OF POLICIES AND PROGRAMS DESIGNED TO BETTER MANAGE FORESTS FOR ECOLOGICAL, ECONOMIC, AND SOCIAL GOALS.

PROPOSALS AT SUNY ESF FUNDED UNDER THE MCINTIRE STENNIS FORESTRY PROGRAM WILL ADDRESS ONE OF THE SIX FORESTRY RESEARCH MANDATED AREAS AS DEFINED BY MCINTIRE STENNIS FORESTRY LEGISLATION: 1. REFORESTATION AND MANAGEMENT OF LAND FOR THE PRODUCTION OF CROPS OF TIMBER AND OTHER RELATED PRODUCTS OF THE FOREST; 2. MANAGEMENT OF FOREST AND RELATED WATERSHED LANDS TO IMPROVE CONDITIONS OF WATER FLOW AND TO PROTECT RESOURCES AGAINST FLOODS AND EROSION; 3. MANAGEMENT OF FOREST AND RELATED RANGELAND FOR PRODUCTION OF FORAGE FOR DOMESTIC LIVESTOCK AND GAME AND IMPROVEMENT OF FOOD AND HABITAT FOR WILDLIFE; MANAGEMENT OF FOREST LANDS FOR OUTDOOR RECREATION; 4. PROTECTION OF FOREST LAND AND RESOURCES AGAINST FIRE, INSECTS, DISEASES, OR OTHER DESTRUCTIVE AGENTS; 5. UTILIZATION OF WOOD AND OTHER FOREST PRODUCTS; AND 6. DEVELOPMENT OF SOUND POLICIES FOR THE MANAGEMENT OF FOREST LANDS AND THE HARVESTING AND MARKETING OF FOREST PRODUCTS; AND SUCH OTHER STUDIES AS MAY BE NECESSARY TO OBTAIN THE FULLEST AND MOST EFFECTIVE USE OF FOREST RESOURCES. IN ADDITION, AWARDED PROPOSALS WILL ALSO ADDRESS THE FOLLOWING GOALS: 1. CREATE THE FUTURE GENERATION OF FORESTRY EDUCATORS, SCIENTISTS, AND PRACTITIONERS THROUGH GRADUATE EDUCATION; 2. BUILD AND SUSTAIN STRATEGIC RELATIONSHIPS THAT ENHANCE OVERALL PROGRAM EFFECTIVENESS AND SUPPORT; AND 3. COMMUNICATE AND EDUCATE THE IMPORTANCE, IMPACT, AND SUCCESSES OF THE MCINTIRE-STENNIS PROGRAM. FUNDING WILL BE UTILIZED TO SUPPORT FACULTY INVESTIGATORS AND THEIR GRADUATE STUDENTS IN PURSUIT OF THESE RESEARCH GOALS AND OBJECTIVES. EXPECTED OUTCOMES SUNY ESF USES ITS MCINTIRE-STENNIS (M-S) FUNDING TO PRIMARILY SUPPORT EARLY CAREER FACULTY. ONLY NON-TENURED FACULTY MEMBERS CAN APPLY FOR FUNDING (GENERALLY FOR 2-YEAR PROJECTS) AND ALL PROPOSALS GO THROUGH A RIGOROUS REVIEW PROCESS PRIOR TO SELECTION. THE INTERNAL RFP THAT WE USE IS DESIGNED TO ENCOURAGE THE RECRUITMENT OF PH.D. STUDENTS BY OFFERING AN ADDITIONAL YEAR OF FUNDING FOR NEW, RECRUITED STUDENTS. AS A RESULT OF THIS CONSCIOUS DECISION TO SUPPORT JUNIOR FACULTY, WE ARE PREPARING OUR FACULTY TO COMPETE FOR LARGER OUTSIDE FUNDING IN THE FUTURE. WE ENCOURAGE FACULTY TO LEVERAGE THEIR M-S FUNDING WITH OTHER GRANT OPPORTUNITIES AND TO DEVELOP INITIAL DATASETS TO BETTER COMPETE IN THE FUTURE. WE GENERALLY HAVE SUFFICIENT FUNDING FOR 2-4 NEW PROJECTS EACH YEAR AT AROUND THE $100,000 LEVEL. OUR PROJECT PORTFOLIO INCLUDES PROJECTS OF SPECIFIC IMPORTANCE TO THE STATE OF NEW YORK, BUT WE HAVE ALSO FUNDED PROJECTS OF INTEREST TO BROADER AUDIENCES. OVER THE PAST DECADE, WE HAVE FUNDED OVER 100 GRADUATE STUDENTS AT BOTH THE MASTERS AND PH.D. LEVEL. IN ADDITION TO THE BULK OF OUR FUNDING GOING TO PEER-REVIEWED PROJECTS, WE HAVE ALWAYS MADE ADDITIONAL FUNDS AVAILABLE AS SEED FUNDING FOR RESEARCHERS WORKING ON EMERGING TOPICS. THESE SMALL GRANTS, GENERALLY AROUND $10,000, ALLOW FACULTY MEMBERS TO RESPOND TO NEW OPPORTUNITIES AND REGIONAL CONCERNS IN AN EXPEDITED MANNER. INTENDED BENEFICIARIES AS ISEXPECTED FOR THESE TYPES OF FORMULA FUNDS, THE PRIMARY BENEFICIARIES OF THE M-S FUNDED RESEARCH ARE THE PEOPLE OF THE STATE OF NEW YORK AND THE COUNTRY AS A WHOLE. OUR RESEARCH IS GENERALLY SPECIFIC TO THE NEEDS OF THE STATE AND REGION AND HAVE SERVED TO INCREASE OUR KNOWLEDGE OF THE TRIPLE BOTTOM LINE OF THE FOREST SECTOR, INCLUDING THE ECOLOGICAL, ECONOMIC, AND SOCIAL FACTORS INFLUENCING THE STATE'S FOREST SECTOR.

negativeFlows.title: CURRENTLY WE HAVE FIVE ACTIVE PROJECTS AND TWO PENDING PROJECTS THAT THIS WILL BE FUNDED AND TEN PROFESSORS ARE WORKING ON THESE APPROVED OR PENDING PROJECTS TO THE USDA. THESE PROJECTS HAVE ALREADY INVOLVED 14 UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS AND ONE GRADUATE STUDENT. THE PROJECTS INCLUDE THE FOLLOWING PROJECTS: 1) EVALUATING THE ROLE OF FUNGI IN FOREST HEALTH IN LOUISIANA THE OBJECTIVES ARE TO EXAMINE AND MAP TREE MORTALITY AND CANOPY STRUCTURE USING DRONE FLEETS TO IMPROVE UNDERSTANDING AND BETTER DESCRIBE THE HEALTH DIFFERENTIAL OF 'HEALTHY' AND 'UNHEALTHY' FORESTS AND TREES CONSIDERING HUMAN, CLIMATIC, AND BIOTIC DRIVERS. SECONDLY, WE WILL EVALUATE THE PARAMETERS ASSOCIATED WITH DECLINE/DISEASE AND PRESENCE OF PATHOGENS, INCLUDING THE ROLE OF FUNGI IN THE FORMATION OF CANOPY OPENINGS, TREE COMPETITION, AND CANOPY STRUCTURE. FINALLY, WE WILL CONDUCT PATHOGENICITY TESTS ON SPECIES CORRELATED WITH DISEASE OUTBREAKS. A "BIG PICTURE" APPROACH WILL BE USED TO CREATE A REALISTIC AND LOGISTICALLYFEASIBLE APPROACH AS THEY RELATE TO RISK PRIORITIES FOR ANY INVOLVED AGENCIES TO DEVELOP BEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES AND TO HELP AVOID INTRODUCTION AND MOVEMENT OF KEY PATHOGENIC FUNGAL SPECIES. A REVIEW OF ANY EXISTING BMPS CAN BE DONE TO USE AS BASELINE DOCUMENTS AND THEN BUILD AND IMPROVE FROM THERE BASED ON THE CONDITION OF EXISTING SITES, NEEDS AND PRIORITIES. IDENTIFICATION OF PATHOGENS AND POTENTIAL VECTORS WILL BE MADE, AND CORRELATED RISK ANALYSES WILL BE DONE. FIELDWORK BEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES INCLUDING WEED CONTROL, REVEGETATION, WATERING, SEED COLLECTION, AND INFRASTRUCTURE (TRAILS, ROADS, AND CONSTRUCTION) AND MAINTENANCE AS APPROPRIATE WILL BE TAKEN INTO ACCOUNT, DEVELOPED AND MODIFIED AS NECESSARY. PROCEDURES FOR EQUIPMENT AND MATERIALS MOVEMENT WILL ALSO BE TAKEN INTO ACCOUNT, DEVELOPED, AND MODIFIED AS NECESSARY. SAMPLING AND MONITORING PROTOCOLS WILL BE OUTLINED. BASED ON EXISTING KNOWLEDGE AND INFORMATION GLEANED, DEVELOP CORRESPONDING PROTOCOLS FOR IMPROVED SITE SELECTION AND PRACTICE. THESE WILL BE MODIFIED AND ADAPTED TO MANAGE FOR THE PATHOGENS FOUND, ASSOCIATED HOSTS, AND LANDSCAPE AND ECOSYSTEM CHARACTERISTICS. 2) OPTIMIZATION OF GENETICALLY IMPROVED SEEDLINGS FOR SOUTHERN FORESTS THROUGH THIS PROJECT, I PROPOSE TO USE EXISTING KNOWLEDGE AS WELL AS TO BROADEN THE KNOWLEDGE BASE OF IMPORTANT SPECIES TO INCREASE YIELD OF DESIRED PRODUCTS. I WILL USE NEW TECHNOLOGIES IN GENOMICS AND TRADITIONAL FOREST TECHNIQUES TO DEVELOP BETTER PROTOCOLS FOR LANDOWNERS TO INCREASE FOREST CROP PRODUCTION. THE FIRST AIM IS TO USE TRADITIONAL SELECTION: WE WILL USE INFORMATION FROM PROGENY TESTS WITH NEW YEAR MEASUREMENTS TO FURTHER INFORM SELECTION OF SUPERIOR GENOTYPES. PROJECT INFORMATION METHODOLOGY THE PRIMARY MEANS OF ANALYSIS WILL BE VIA INPUT-OUTPUT TABLES AND SOCIAL ACCOUNTING MATRIXES. AN INPUT-OUTPUT TABLE QUANTIFIES TRANSACTIONS BY HOW MANY DOLLARS EACH SECTOR PROCESSES TOSELL AND PURCHASES FOR USE. THE TABLE SEPARATES PROCESSING SECTORS BY ROWS AND PURCHASING SECTORS BY COLUMNS; EVERY SECTOR IS CONSIDERED TO BE BOTH A PROCESSOR AND PURCHASER. SUMMING EACH ROW QUANTIFIES AN INDUSTRY'S OUTPUT, WHICH INCLUDES SALES TO OTHER PRODUCTION SECTORS ALONG WITH THOSE TO FINAL USERS. BEYOND THE INPUT-OUTPUT FRAMEWORK ARE THE NONMARKET INCOME FLOWS OCCURRING IN A REGION, SUCH AS HOUSEHOLDS RECEIVING WAGES AND BENEFITS FROM INDUSTRIES, DIVIDENDS FROM CORPORATIONS, AND/OR TRANSFER PAYMENTS FROM GOVERNMENT. A SOCIAL ACCOUNTING MATRIX DETAILS THESE ECONOMIC RELATIONSHIPS VIA CONSTRUCTION OF SUBMATRICES IN ADDITION TO THAT CHARACTERIZING THE TRADITIONAL INTER-INDUSTRY FLOWS FOUND IN AN INPUT-OUTPUT TABLE. 4) PRELIMINARY EVALUATION OF WILDLIFE RESPONSE TO CATTLE GRAZING IN A LONGLEAF PINE THE SOUTHWESTERN LOUISIANA/SOUTHEASTERN TEXAS REGION HAS BEEN IDENTIFIED BY USDA NRCS AS A PRIORITY AREA FOR LONGLEAF PINE RESTORATION, AND THERE ARE SEVERAL OPPORTUNITIES FOR IMPROVING RESTORATION EFFORTS IN THE REGION BY INTEGRATING GRAZING INTO LONGLEAF PINE MANAGEMENT. IN 2022-23, THE CAL POLY HUMBOLDT MCINTIRE-STENNIS GRANT WILL FUND THE FOLLOWING PROJECTS: 1) MCINTIRE-STENNIS RESEARCH PLANNING AND ADMINISTRATION, 2) YEAR-5 ASSESSMENT OF REPLICATED UNEVEN-AGED DOUGLAS-FIR/TANOAK SILVICULTURE EXPERIMENT ALONG NORTHERN CALIFORNIA'S COAST RANGE, 3) TREE RESPONSES TO WILDFIRE AND DROUGHT IN A CONIFER DIVERSITY HOTSPOT, 4) CLIMATE CHANGE IMPACTS ON FOREST AND WATER RESOURCES OF NORTHERN CALIFORNIA, 5) RECOVERY OF HUMAN COMMUNITIES AFTER WILDFIRE: BUILDING SOCIAL-ECOLOGICAL RESILIENCE, AND 6) THE CAPACITY OF NONSEROTINOUS SEEDS TO SURVIVE FIRE WITHIN MATURE CONES. 1) MCINTIRE-STENNIS RESEARCH PLANNING AND ADMINISTRATION PROJECT DIRECTOR: JEFFREY KANE THE GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO FACILITATE RESEARCH PLANNING AND ADMINISTRATIVE ACTIVITIES FOR THE MCINTIRE-STENNIS RESEARCH PROGRAM AT CAL POLY HUMBOLDT. THE BUDGET ITEMS FOR THIS PROJECT INCLUDE STAFF SALARY AND BENEFITS, TRAVEL TO ATTEND MEETINGS, SUPPLIES, EQUIPMENT, AND PUBLICATION CHARGES. 2) YEAR-5 ASSESSMENT OF REPLICATED UNEVEN-AGED DOUGLAS-FIR/TANOAK SILVICULTURE EXPERIMENT ALONG NORTHERN CALIFORNIA'S COAST RANGE PROJECT DIRECTOR: PASCAL BERRILL THE PROPOSED RESEARCH AND DEMONSTRATION PROJECT WILL COMPARE DIFFERENT METHODS OF CONVERTING DEGRADED TIMBERLANDS INTO HEALTHY, VIGOROUS, AND RESILIENT FORESTS THAT SEQUESTER MORE CARBON PER ACRE ANNUALLY AND AVOID LOSS OF STORED CARBON FROM CATASTROPHIC WILDFIRE. DRY FORESTS OF CALIFORNIA'S COAST RANGE WERE LOGGED THROUGHOUT THE 1900S AND LEFT TO REGENERATE NATURALLY WITH HARDWOOD (MAINLY TANOAK) AND CONIFER (MAINLY DOUGLAS-FIR) SEEDLINGS. ONCE DOMINATED BY LARGE CONIFERS, THE DRY FORESTS NOW HAVE AN OVER-ABUNDANCE OF HARDWOODS. MANY OF THESE FORESTS HAVE BECOME CROWDED WHICH POSES A RISK OF CATASTROPHIC WILDFIRE WHERE CO2 GAS IS RELEASED TO THE ATMOSPHERE BY BURNING OF CARBONSTORED IN WOOD AND DECAY OF UNBURNED WOOD IN FIRE-KILLED TREES. COAST RANGE DRY FORESTS CONTAIN MANY OF THE STATE'S "COMMUNITIES AT RISK FROM WILDFIRE" (FRAP.FIRE.CA.GOV). CURRENT OWNERSHIP PATTERNS AND FOREST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES INCLUDE SMALL UNMANAGED PRIVATE HOLDINGS, INDUSTRIAL FORESTRY COMPANIES HARVESTING CONIFERS AND USING HERBICIDE TO CONTROL HARDWOODS, AND NOT-FOR-PROFIT OWNERS SUCH AS THE CONSERVATION FUND, REDWOOD FOREST FOUNDATION, AND SUSTAINABLE CONSERVATION INC. WHO MANAGE FORESTS FOR ECOSYSTEM AND COMMUNITY VALUES AND BENEFITS INCLUDING TIMBER PRODUCTION, TRANSPORTATION, AND PROCESSING. VERY LITTLE IS KNOWN ABOUT HOW SUSTAINABLE FOREST MANAGEMENT AFFECTS POTENTIAL WILDFIRE BEHAVIOR IN THIS IMPORTANT WIDESPREAD CALIFORNIA FOREST TYPE. FIVE YEARS AGO, MY RESEARCH GROUP DESIGNED AND IMPLEMENTED A REPLICATED FIELD EXPERIMENT ACROSS 120+ ACRES AT FOUR SITES LOCATED ALONG A NORTH-SOUTH GRADIENT THROUGHOUT THE COAST RANGE OF NORTHERN CALIFORNIA. OUR GOAL WAS TO DEMONSTRATE ANDQUANTIFY GREENHOUSE GAS (GHG) REDUCTIONS ACHIEVED BY FOREST RESTORATION. WE ARE TESTING DIFFERENT COMBINATIONS OF RESTORATION TREATMENT OPTIONS THAT ENHANCE CARBON SEQUESTRATION BY FAVORING FAST-GROWING CONIFERS OVER HARDWOODS, AND REMOVE OR MODIFY THE ARRANGEMENT OF FLAMMABLE HARVEST RESIDUES (SURFACE FUELS). TREATMENT COMBINATIONS TESTED IN THIS LARGE, LONG-TERM EXPERIMENT INCLUDE A SILVICULTURAL TREATMENT IMPLEMENTED BY PARTIAL HARVESTING, WITH AND WITHOUT HERBICIDE TREATMENT OF HARDWOODS, COMBINED WITH A VIABLE FUELS REDUCTION TREATMENT (I.E., LOP+SCATTER, BIOMASS REMOVAL) THAT DISPOSES OF - OR REARRANGES - FUELS TO MITIGATE EXTREME WILDFIRE BEHAVIOR. SUBSEQUENT UNDERPLANTING WITH CONIFER SEEDLINGS CREATES A NEW AGE-CLASS OF TREES IN THE RESTORED FOREST. IN THIS PROJECT, WE PROPOSE TO RE-VISIT THE EXPERIMENT AFTER 5 YEARS AND RE-MEASURE TREES AND FUELS TO QUANTIFY GROWTH OF TREES AND SEEDLINGS, AND THE ARRANGEMENT AND DECAY RATE OF FUELS, AND HOW THIS HAS CHANGED OVER TIME FOR EACH TREATMENT COMBINATION. THESE DATA WILL ALLOW US TO SEEK FUNDING TO CONDUCT A FOLLOW-ON STUDY WHERE WE SIMULATE THE POTENTIAL IMPACTS OF WILDFIRE WITH THE GOAL OF IDENTIFYING FOREST AND FUELS TREATMENTS THAT MITIGATE WILDFIRE IMPACTS WHILE ALSO SUSTAINING TIMBER PRODUCTION AND VIABLE REGENERATION OF A NEW AGE CLASS OF TREE SEEDLINGS. ONE GRADUATE STUDENT AND MULTIPLE UNDERGRADUATE STUDENT ASSISTANTS WILL BE ACTIVELY ENGAGED IN THIS APPLIED RESEARCH PROJECT OF INTEREST TO STUDENTS, SMALL PRIVATE TIMBERLAND LANDOWNERS, FOREST MANAGERS, FOREST AND FIRE SCIENTISTS, AND POLICYMAKERS. 3) TREE RESPONSES TO WILDFIRE AND DROUGHT IN A CONIFER DIVERSITY HOTSPOT PROJECT DIRECTOR: LUCY KERHOULAS AND ROSEMARY SHERRIFF WILDFIRES AND DROUGHT HAVE INCREASED DRAMATICALLY OVER RECENT DECADES IN THE WESTERN U.S., CREATING SUBSTANTIAL FOREST MORTALITY WITH WIDE-REACHING IMPACTS AFFECTING RURAL ECONOMIES, NATURAL ENVIRONMENTS, WATER RESOURCES, AND THE HEALTH OF RURAL AND URBAN COMMUNITIES. IMPACTS ON OTHER HIGH PRIORITY AREAS INCLUDE HELPING TO REDUCE UNCERTAINTY AND INFORM DECISION-MAKING. 5) RECOVERY OF HUMAN COMMUNITIES AFTER WILDFIRE: BUILDING SOCIAL-ECOLOGICAL RESILIENCE PROJECT DIRECTOR: ERIN KELLY FOREST FIRE ACTIVITY HAS DRAMATICALLY INCREASED THROUGHOUT MUCH OF THE WESTERN US OVER THE PAST FEW DECADES, POSING SERIOUS CHALLENGES TO MANY HUMAN COMMUNITIES. IN CALIFORNIA, SEVEN OF THE TEN LARGEST FIRES, FIVE OF THE TEN MOST DESTRUCTIVE FIRES, AND THREE OF THE TEN DEADLIEST FIRES IN RECORDED HISTORY OCCURRED WITHIN THE PAST FOUR YEARS. AS HUMAN COMMUNITIES RECOVER FROM THESE WILDFIRES, THEY WILL GO THROUGH PHASES, FROM AN EMERGENCY PERIOD (OF RESCUE AND RELOCATION) TO REHABILITATION (WHEN ESSENTIAL INFRASTRUCTURE IS RE-BUILT) TO RECONSTRUCTION, WHEN LONG-TERM PHYSICAL AND SOCIAL NEEDS OF RESIDENTS ARE ADDRESSED AND THE COMMUNITY ATTEMPTS TO REBUILD IN A WAY THAT INCREASES ITS RESILIENCE. THIS LAST PHASE MAY ALSO BE TERMED LONG-TERM RECOVERY, AND OCCURS 2-3 YEARS AFTER DISASTER, AS COMMUNITY CAPACITY IS RE-BUILT AND LONG-TERM PLANS ARE PUT IN PLACE. POST-WILDFIRE RECOVERY IS MULTIFACETED, AND INCLUDES REBUILDING PHYSICAL INFRASTRUCTURE; RESUMING MUNICIPAL, SOCIAL, AND ECONOMIC ACTIVITIES; AND PROMOTING PSYCHOLOGICAL HEALING AND RECOVERY, AS RESIDENTS STRUGGLE WITH "LOSSES AND PROLONGED DISTRESS". THERE HAS BEEN VERY LITTLE RESEARCH ON COMMUNITY RECOVERYSEVERAL YEARS AFTER WILDFIRE. THE TIMELINE OF OUR PROPOSED RESEARCH, 3-4 YEARS AFTER WILDFIRE, WILL ALLOW US TO ASSESS BOTH IMMEDIATE POST-DISASTER COMMUNITY RESPONSES AND MORE LONG-TERM COMMUNITY RECOVERY. RATHER THAN FOCUSING NARROWLY ON THE "AFTERSHOCK" SOCIAL AND ECONOMIC FACTORS, WE WILL CONSIDER THE DIRECTION OF RECOVERY WITH SEVERAL YEARS' WORTH OF LESSONS LEARNED. THE TIMELINE OF POST-DISASTER RECOVERY IS IMPORTANT: SOON AFTER DISASTER THERE MAY BE A SENSE OF COMMUNITY COHESION AND WORKING TOGETHER TOWARD COMMON CAUSE , DESCRIBED AS A "HONEYMOON" PHASE. THIS SUGGESTS THAT RECOVERY EFFORTS MAY LAG, OR MAY RUN INTO COMMUNITY CONFLICTS, AFTER SOME TIME. BUT WITHIN COMMUNITIES, NEW ACTORS AND LEADERS MAY ALSO EMERGE TO FACILITATE RECOVERY EFFORTS, CONTRIBUTING TO RENEWED SOCIAL COHESION AND COMMUNITY AGENCY. PRIOR RESEARCH FOUND THAT 9 MONTHS AFTER A FIRE IN SWEDEN, THERE WAS STILL INCREASED SOCIAL COHESION AND PEOPLE DESCRIBED THEIR COMMUNITY AS "STRONGER" AFTER THE FIRE. IN ONE OF THE FEW STUDIES TO ASSESS COMMUNITY RECOVERY SEVERAL YEARS AFTER THE FIRE, THEY FOUND THAT FIVE YEARS AFTER THE RODEO- CHEDISKI FIRE, NEARBY COMMUNITIES HAD BOTH MAINTAINED A "COMING TOGETHER" SPIRIT THAT SPURRED COMMUNITY ACTION, AND HAD DEVELOPED POST-FIRE CONFLICT, DISTRUST, AND DISAGREEMENTS. THIS FUNDING WILL HELP US TO BUILD PARTNERSHIPS WITH COMMUNITY NON-PROFIT ORGANIZATIONS THAT ARE FACILITATING IN THE RECOVERY EFFORT, AND TO EXPAND THEIR UNDERSTANDING OF WHAT IS NEEDED (WHAT IS WORKING, WHAT IS NOT WORKING) IN TERMS OF WILDFIRE RECOVERY. WE ARE CREATING CASE STUDIES IN THREE COMMUNITIES AND WILL USE FUNDING TO SUPPORT ACTIVITIES IN ALL THREE. 6) THE CAPACITY OF NON-SEROTINOUS SEEDS TO SURVIVE FIRE WITHIN MATURE CONES PROJECT DIRECTOR: DAVID GREENE SUMMARY: THE FOREST DENSIFICATION AND WARMING OF THE 20TH CENTURY HAS LED TO INCREASINGLY FREQUENT, LARGE, AND SEVERE PATCHES IN WESTERN FORESTS OF THE US. OWING TO THE PREVIOUS LOW INTENSITY FIRE REGIME CHARACTERISTIC OF THE LAST FEW MILLENNIA, OUR CURRENT SPECIES MIX IS POORLY ADAPTED TO A STANDREPLACING FIRE REGIME (E.G. SEROTINOUS SPECIES PRESENTLY COMPRISE A TINY FRACTION OF THE TREE BIOMASS IN THE FAR WESTERN STATES). IN PARTICULAR, RECENT STUDIES HAVE SHOWN POOR POST-FIRE REGENERATION IN LARGE SEVERE PATCHES, ESPECIALLY AT LOWER ELEVATIONS. IF SO, THEN THE TRANSITION TO A PREDOMINANTLY SEROTINOUS FOREST MAY BE SLOWER THAN WE MIGHT EXPECT. THE PROPOSED RESEARCH WILL BUILD ON EARLIER WORK, MUCH OF IT UNPUBLISHED, ADVANCING THIS IDEA. IN ADDITION TO ALIGNING WITH THE MAIN RESEARCH AREA ("REFORESTATION AND MANAGEMENT. . ."). THE PROPOSED PROJECT ADDRESSES THE HIGH PRIORITY ISSUE OF "CONFLICT, UNCERTAINTY, AND DECISION-MAKING" AS IT IS FOCUSED ON DELINEATING THE JOINT PROBABILITIES GOVERNING SEXUAL RECRUITMENT BY CONIFERS IN RECENT BURNS. negativeFlows.title: DR. PAUL M. LUKACS, MCINTIRE-STENNIS ADMINISTRATIVE-TECHNICAL REPRESENTATIVE (A-TR) W.A. FRANKE COLLEGE OF FORESTRY AND CONSERVATION, UNIVERSITY OF MONTANA, MISSOULA, MT 59812 THE UNIVERSITY OF MONTANA'S PROGRAM OF RESEARCH IN FY2023 CONSISTS OF SIX CONTINUING PROJECTS AND ONE NEW TRANSDISCIPLINARY PROJECT - THAT ADVANCE SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE ACROSS THE RANGE OF TOPICAL AREAS TARGETED BY THE MCINTIRE-STENNIS COOPERATIVE FORESTRY PROGRAM. FORESTS IN THE WESTERN UNITED STATES SERVE MULTIPLE ROLES ON THE LANDSCAPE. FORESTS STORE CARBON, PRODUCE TIMBER, SUPPORT BIODIVERSITY, PROVIDE RECREATIONAL OPPORTUNITIES, AND SERVE AS RANGE FOR LIVESTOCK. BALANCING ALL THESE OPPORTUNITIES REQUIRES AN UNDERSTANDING OF THE PROCESSES SUPPORTING EACH AND, PERHAPS MORE IMPORTANTLY, THE INTERACTIONS AMONG THE VARIOUS USES. OUR RESEARCH PROJECTS AIM TO UNDERSTAND THE INTERCONNECTED PROCESSES PROVIDING FOR MULTIPLE ROLES OF FORESTS ON THE LANDSCAPE. WE SEEK TO UNDERSTAND HOW CHANGES IN ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS POTENTIALLY IMPACT EACH FOREST USE. SPECIFICALLY, WE WILL INVESTIGATE 1) CAPACITY TO STORE CARBON AND OUR ABILITY TO MEASURE AND PREDICT STORAGE, 2) SEED BANK COMPOSITION AND POTENTIAL FOR CURRENT AND FUTURE RESTORATION OF FOREST AND RANGE IN THE EVENT OF A CHANGE IN STRUCTURE, 3) WILDLIFE RESPONSES TO TIMBER, RANGE, AND RECREATIONAL USE, AND 4) SOCIAL RESPONSES TO FORESTS INCLUDING RECREATION AND VALUES. OUR RESEARCH ALIGNS WITH THE MANDATED RESEARCH AREAS OF THE MCINTIRE-STENNIS ACT AND IT ALSO ALIGNS WITH THE USDA STRATEGIC PLAN GOALS 1 AND 2. WE WILL LEVERAGE THE UM LUBRECHT EXPERIMENTAL FOREST IN ADDITION TO OTHER SITES AROUND THE WESTERN UNITED STATES TO BETTER UNDERSTAND THE INTERCONNECTEDNESS OF FOREST SYSTEMS. WE WILL CONTINUE THE FIRE AND FIRE SURROGATE STUDY AS A LONG-TERM LONGITUDINAL STUDY TO UNDERSTAND FIRE AND THINNING PRACTICES. WE WILL EXAMINE CARBON STORAGE MEASUREMENT AND PREDICTION TOOLS TO BETTER UNDERSTAND HOW TO PLAN FOR FOREST MANAGEMENT AS A CARBON STORAGE SYSTEM. FURTHERMORE, WE WILL EXAMINE SEED BANK RESILIENCY AND WATER RESOURCES TO BETTER UNDERSTAND HOW FORESTS CAN BE RESTORED AFTER STRUCTURAL CHANGES SUCH AS WILDFIRE AND TIMBER HARVEST. FOREST RESOURCES EXTEND BEYOND VEGETATION TO WILDLIFE AND PEOPLE WHO USE THEM. WE WILL FURTHER CONSIDER HOW MANAGEMENT FOR CARBON STORAGE CAN BE LINKED TO MANAGEMENT FOR WILDLIFE HABITAT AND RECREATION. WE WILL EXPAND METHODS FOR MEASURING WILDLIFE POPULATIONS USING REMOTELY TRIGGERED CAMERAS TO ESTIMATE WILDLIFE ABUNDANCE, DIVERSITY, AND USE. CAMERAS REPRESENT A METHOD THAT COULD BE EMPLOYED ACROSS A WIDE RANGE OF FOREST MANAGERS FROM SMALL PRIVATE FORESTS TO LARGE-SCALE FEDERAL LANDS. THE RESULTS OF OUR RESEARCH WILL PROVIDE GUIDANCE FOR LAND MANAGERS SEEKING TO BALANCE MULTIPLE OBJECTIVES IN THEIR FORESTS. WE WILL DEVELOP METHODS FOR MEASURING KEY FEATURES SUCH AS SEED BANK RESOURCES AND WILDLIFE. WE WILL ALSO DEVELOP INSIGHTS FOR MANAGING FOREST STANDS WITH FIRE AND THINNING AS THEY GROW WITH AN EYE TOWARD CARBON STORAGE CAPACITY.

positiveFlows.title: THE PROPOSED PROJECT WILL HELP OSU COLLEGE OF FORESTRY CARRY OUT RESEARCH PROJECTS IMPORTANT TO THE STATE OF OREGON. SUPPORTED PROJECTS WILL SUPPORT TRAINED FOREST SCIENTISTS IN THE FOLLOWING RESEARCH TOPICS: REFORESTATION; FOREST, WATERSHED, AND RANGELAND MANAGEMENT; FOREST RECREATION; PROTECTION AGAINST FIRE, INSECTS, DISEASES, AND OTHER DESTRUCTIVE AGENTS; FOREST PRODUCTS UTILIZATION; AND FOREST POLICY. PROJECTS FUNDED BY OSU INCLUDE UNDERSTANDING CONTEXT OF, BARRIERS TO, AND IMPACTS OF ACTIVE FOREST MANAGEMENT IN THE FIRE-ADAPTED WEST, REVIEWING AND DEVELOPING SOUND POLICIES FOR THE MANAGEMENT OF FOREST LANDS, HARVESTING PRACTICES, AND MARKETING OF FOREST PRODUCTS, MANAGEMENT OF FOREST AND RELATED WATERSHED LANDS TO IMPROVE WATER FLOW AND PROTECT AGAINST FLOODS AND EROSION, RESEARCH ON ADVANCED WOOD PRODUCTS IN MASS TIMBER BUILDINGS, IMPROVEMENT OF SCIENTIFIC TOOLS FOR MANAGING FORESTED WATERSHEDS, USE OF REMOTE SENSING TECHNOLOGIES TO ESTIMATE DIMENSIONS AND DIFFERENT QUALITIES OF TREES, AND UNDERSTANDING THE CONNECTIONS BETWEEN FOREST GOVERNANCE AND LANDSCAPE PATTERN AND PROCESS, AND THE WAYS IN WHICH PUBLIC PERCEPTIONS AND VALUATIONS OF FEDERAL FOREST LANDSCAPES AND SCIENCE INFLUENCE THOSE CONNECTIONS. DELIVERABLES INCLUDE RESEARCH PAPERS, CONFERENCE PRESENTATIONS, DATASETS, MANAGEMENT GUIDES, AND THE LIKE. INTENDED BENEFICIARIES INCLUDE STATE AND FEDERAL AGENCIES, POLICYMAKERS, FOREST AND LANDOWNERS, AND GENERAL PUBLIC WHO RECREATE IN PRIVATE, STATE, OR FEDERAL FOREST AND RANGELANDS.

THROUGH INTEGRATED RESEARCH AND EXTENSION PROGRAMS, NC STATE IS SOLVING CHALLENGES RELATED TO THE PRODUCTIVITY AND PROFITABILITY OF BOTH LARGE- AND SMALL-SCALE FARMS. RESEARCHERS AND EXTENSION EDUCATORS ARE ALSO DEVELOPING AND DISSEMINATING KNOWLEDGE AND TECHNOLOGY TO IMPROVE LANDSCAPING AND GARDENING. RESEARCH AND EXTENSION PROGRAMS IN ANIMAL SYSTEMS ARE FOCUSED ON DEVELOPING AND DISSEMINATING KNOWLEDGE AND METHODS FOR ANIMAL BREEDING, REPRODUCTION, NUTRITION, GENETICS AND GENOMICS, PHYSIOLOGY, ENVIRONMENTAL STRESS, PRODUCT QUALITY, AND HEALTH AND WELL-BEING. THESE INTEGRATED RESEARCH AND EXTENSION EFFORTS ALSO AIM TO TACKLE THE CRITICAL ISSUES IMPACTING THE QUALITY OF OUR SOIL, WATER AND AIR BY PROVIDING SCIENTIFIC SOLUTIONS FOR ANIMAL WASTE MANAGEMENT, WASTEWATER TREATMENT, NUTRIENT MANAGEMENT, SEPTIC SYSTEMS, WETLAND MANAGEMENT, SOIL PROPERTIES, AND FISHERY AND POND MANAGEMENT. NC STATE'S RESEARCH AND EXTENSION EFFORTS TO ENHANCE FOOD SAFETY, NUTRITION AND HEALTH AND TO KEEP AMERICAN'S HEALTHY AND FREE FROM FOODBORNE ILLNESS NECESSITATE A FOCUS ON PREVENTING FOOD SAFETY PROBLEMS RATHER THAN TAKING A REACTIONARY APPROACH. NC STATE'S INTEGRATED RESEARCH AND EXTENSION EFFORTS FOCUS ON PROTECTING THE SAFETY OF FOODS ALONG THE ENTIRE SUPPLY CHAIN, FROM PRODUCTION TO CONSUMPTION. TO MEET THE GROWING  NEED FOR HEALTHY FOOD, RESEARCHERS ARE DEVELOPING AND PRODUCING NEW FOOD PRODUCTS THAT PROMOTE HEALTH AND PREVENT DISEASE. AT THE SAME TIME, EXTENSION PROVIDES NUTRITION EDUCATION PROGRAMMING TO ENSURE THAT INDIVIDUALS, FAMILIES, AND COMMUNITIES HAVE THE KNOWLEDGE THEY NEED TO MAKE INFORMED CHOICES ABOUT FOOD AND HEALTHY LIFESTYLES. IMPROVING PLANT AND ANIMAL AGRICULTURAL SYSTEMS: WITHIN THIS AREA, WE WILL WORK TO ADDRESS CROSS-CUTTING AND EMERGING ISSUES OF ANIMAL AND PLANT HEALTH AND PRODUCTION. IN ANIMAL SYSTEMS, RESEARCHERS WILL STUDY THE EFFICIENCY OF DIFFERENT FEEDING SOURCES TO IMPROVE ANIMAL PRODUCTIVITY AND GUT HEALTH. IN PLANT SYSTEMS, THE FOCUS WILL BE IN SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE, ALTERNATIVE AND HIGH VALUE CROP PRODUCTION, SEASON EXTENSION, ENVIRONMENTAL ADAPTATION, VALUE ADDED AGRICULTURE, DIGITAL AGRICULTURE, SOIL HEALTH, PEST CONTROL, AND AGRO ECONOMICS. EXTENSION WILL CONTINUE TO EXPAND ITS WORK WITH LIVESTOCK PRODUCERS, PLACING SPECIAL INTEREST ON COMPACTED RESOURCES, SMALL- SCALE MINORITY FARMERS. THE FARM PAVILION WILL FOCUS ON SUSTAINABLE AGRICULTURE AND LOCAL AND COMMUNITY FOOD SYSTEMS, HOUSING ITS APPLIED RESEARCH AND DEMONSTRATION PROGRAMS' STAFF AND PROVIDING SPACE FOR MEETINGS, FORUMS AND CONFERENCES

THE OBJECTIVE OF THE MCINTIRE-STENNIS (M-S) COOPERATIVE FORESTRY RESEARCH PROGRAM AT THE UNIVERSITY OF GEORGIA (UGA) IS TO CARRY OUT APPLIED RESEARCH WHOSE OUTCOMES SUPPORT SUSTAINABLE MANAGEMENT OF FOREST LANDS FOR MULTIPLE BENEFITS TO PEOPLE AND NATURE IN GEORGIA, AND TO TRAIN FOREST SCIENTISTS TO SUPPORT RESEARCH AND PRACTICE. OUR PROGRAM SUPPORTS RESEARCH IN ALL M-S FOCUS AREAS. IN THE AREA OF REFORESTATION AND MANAGEMENT OF LAND FOR TIMBER PRODUCTION AND OTHER RELATED FOREST PRODUCTS, ONE SUB-PROJECT WILL EVALUATE GENETICALLY IMPROVED PLANTATIONS IN TERMS OF WOOD QUALITY, GROWTH, AND YIELD. A SECOND SUBPROJECT ADVANCES OPERATIONS RESEARCH, SUPPORTING FOREST PLANS THAT ARE FEASIBLE, EFFICIENT, AND SUSTAINABLE. A THIRD SUBPROJECT EVALUATES HOW WATER USE AND SOIL CARBON RESPOND TO ENVIRONMENTAL FACTORS AND SILVICULTURAL TECHNIQUES OVER TIME. IN THE AREA OF MANAGEMENT OF FOREST AND RELATED WATERSHED LANDS TO IMPROVE CONDITIONS OF WATER FLOW AND TO PROTECT RESOURCES AGAINST FLOODS AND EROSION, ONE SUBPROJECT WILL ASSESS EFFECTIVENESS OF ENHANCED BEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES TO ENSURE THAT FORESTLANDS IN THE SOUTHEAST PROVIDE A RANGE OF ECOSYSTEM SERVICES IN ADDITION TO WOOD PRODUCTS, INCLUDING HABITAT FOR NATIVE SPECIES, RECREATION, CLEAN AIR AND WATER, AND MITIGATION AGAINST FLOODS AND DROUGHTS. IN THE AREA OF MANAGEMENT OF FOREST AND RELATED RANGELAND FOR PRODUCTION OF FORAGE FOR DOMESTIC LIVESTOCK AND GAME AND IMPROVEMENT OF FOOD AND HABITAT FOR WILDLIFE, SEVERAL SUBPROJECTS INVESTIGATE HOW FOREST LANDS CAN BE MANAGED TO SUPPORT WILDLIFE AND FISHERY RESOURCES. BY MONITORING DEER, COYOTES, REPTILES, AMPHIBIANS, BIRDS, AND FISH, AND MODELING RESPONSES TO FOREST MANAGEMENT AND ENVIRONMENTAL FACTORS, THESE PROJECTS WILL INFORM PRACTICES THAT IMPROVE HABITAT FOR NATIVE SPECIES, ENSURE RECREATIONAL OPPORTUNITIES SUCH AS HUNTING, FISHING, AND BIRD WATCHING, AND INCREASE RESILIENCE TO ENVIRONMENTAL CHANGE. IN THE AREA OF MANAGEMENT OF FOREST LANDS FOR OUTDOOR RECREATION, ONE SUBPROJECT USES RANDOM STRATIFIED EXIT SURVEYS ALONG WITH VISITATION ESTIMATES TO CALCULATE ECONOMIC IMPACTS OF TENNESSEE VALLEY AUTHORITY'S (TVA'S) STREAM ACCESS SITES. IN THE AREA OF PROTECTION OF FOREST LAND AND RESOURCES AGAINST FIRE, INSECTS, DISEASES, OR OTHER DESTRUCTIVE AGENTS, ONE SUBPROJECT IS FOCUSED ON PROTECTION AND RESTORATION OF NORTH AMERICAN ASH SPECIES UNDER THREAT BY THE EMERALD ASH BORER. A SECOND SUBPROJECT INVESTIGATES THE BIOLOGY AND ECOLOGY OF NATIVE AND EXOTIC INSECT PESTS AND EVALUATES BEST MANAGEMENT STRATEGIES TO SUSTAIN FORESTS UNDER THREAT FROM THESE PESTS. IN THE AREA OF UTILIZATION OF WOOD AND OTHER FOREST PRODUCTS, ONE SUBPROJECT ADDRESSES THE STRUCTURE, PROFITABILITY, AND EFFICIENCY OF SMALL, INDEPENDENT LOGGING BUSINESSES, AND AIMS TO HELP THESE BUSINESSES BE MORE EFFICIENT AND PROFITABLE. THE SOUTHERN FOREST INDUSTRY IS RESPONSIBLE FOR $230 BILLION IN ECONOMIC OUTPUT AND OVER 1 MILLION JOBS, AND DEPENDS ON THOUSANDS OF SMALL, INDEPENDENT LOGGING BUSINESSES TO HARVEST AND DELIVER TIMBER. RESULTS WILL HELP THEM OPERATE MORE PROFITABLY AND DELIVER THE TIMBER NECESSARY TO SUPPORT THE FOREST PRODUCTS INDUSTRY. FINALLY, IN THE AREA OF DEVELOPMENT OF SOUND POLICIES FOR THE MANAGEMENT OF FOREST LANDS AND THE HARVESTING AND MARKETING OF FOREST PRODUCTS, ONE SUBPROJECT WILL EVALUATE RISKS TO TIMBERLAND INVESTMENTS FROM MIXED ASSET PORTFOLIOS. ANOTHER WILL USE IN-DEPTH CASE STUDIES, EXISTING PERFORMANCE DATA, AND REMOTELY SENSED LAND COVER DATA TO EVALUATE OUTCOMES OF CROSS-BOUNDARY FOREST MANAGEMENT POLICIES. COLLECTIVELY, THESE OUTCOMES WILL HELP TO IMPROVE THE DESIGN, IMPLEMENTATION, AND MONITORING OF POLICIES AND PROGRAMS TO BETTER MANAGE FORESTS FOR ECOLOGICAL, ECONOMIC, AND SOCIAL GOALS. TARGET AUDIENCES FOR ALL M-S WORK INCLUDE FOREST MANAGERS, INDUSTRY PLANNERS, PRIVATE OWNERS, STUDENTS, SCIENTISTS, AGENCY AND NGO PARTNERS, INVESTORS, AND MORE

AGRICULTURE IS THE PRIMARY INDUSTRY IN SOUTH CAROLINA, WITH 25,000 FARMS ACROSS 4.7 MILLION ACRES THAT CONTRIBUTE OVER $46 BILLION TO THE STATE'S ANNUAL ECONOMY AND PROVIDE OVER 247,000 JOBS. FORESTRY IS ALSO AN IMPORTANT ECONOMIC DRIVER IN SC, CONTRIBUTING OVER $21.2 BILLION ANNUALLY. WITH DIVERSE NATURAL RESOURCES ACROSS THE STATE, TOURISM IS AN ADDITIONAL ECONOMIC FORCE, ACCOUNTING FOR EXPENDITURES OF $24.4 BILLION ANNUALLY. SUPPORTING AND IMPROVING THE LIVELIHOOD AND QUALITY OF LIFE FOR SC RESIDENTS ARE WHAT DRIVE THE PROGRAMMING AND RESEARCH FOCUS FOR CLEMSON UNIVERSITY. THE PLAN OF WORK REFLECTS RESEARCH ACTIVITIES TO BENEFIT AGRIBUSINESS, COMMUNITIES, AND CITIZENS OF SC. THE RESEARCH IS CONDUCTED ON THE MAIN CAMPUS OF CLEMSON UNIVERSITY AND IN EACH OF THE SIX RESEARCH AND EDUCATION CENTERS (RECS) LOCATED ACROSS THE STATE. FOCUS AREAS INCLUDE ADVANCING THE COMPETITIVENESS OF THE AGRICULTURE AND FORESTRY, ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT, SAFEGUARDING THE FOOD SUPPLY, PRESERVING NATURAL RESOURCES, AND PREPARING YOUNGER GENERATIONS TO BECOME PRODU CTIVE CITIZENS. RESEARCH PROGRAMS TO SUSTAIN CONSERVATION OF NATURAL RESOURCES INCLUDE: 1) REMOTE CLIMATIC DATA COLLECTION AND DATA MANAGEMENT ON FORESTS, 2) TECHNIQUES TO ENHANCE FOREST GROWTH AND QUALITY (SILVICULTURE, HARVESTING OPERATIONS, FOREST MANAGEMENT, AND FOREST HEALTH), 3) HYDROLOGIC AND FOREST PRODUCTIVITY PROCESSES ALONG HYDROPERIODS AND SALINITY GRADIENTS. WILDLIFE MANAGEMENT RESEARCH FOCUSES ON THE PRACTICES AND POLICIES THAT AFFECT THE ANIMALS OF THE STATE, EXAMINING THE HEALTH, ENVIRONMENTAL AND ECOLOGICAL RISKS OF WILDLIFE SPECIES WITH DECLINING POPULATION AND OVERPOPULATION

VAES IS COMMITTED TO DEVELOPING AND IMPLEMENTING RESEARCH THAT ADDRESSES SOCIETAL NEEDS,  EXPECTATIONS, AND FUTURE PRESSURES AND OPPORTUNITIES. VAES IS FOCUSED ON CREATING KNOWLEDGE,  INTEGRATING ADVANCED TECHNOLOGICAL AND SCIENTIFIC INNOVATIONS TO CREATE EFFICIENCIES AND ECONOMIC  GROWTH, AND TRANSLATING KNOWLEDGE INTO PRACTICE TO ENHANCE AGRICULTURAL AND FOOD SYSTEMS, INCLUDING  AGRICULTURE AND FOOD, NATURAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL RESOURCES, AND LIFE SCIENCES. RESEARCH ENCOMPASSES  NEAR- AND LONG-TERM ISSUES AND OPPORTUNITIES PERTAINING TO INVASIVE PESTS AND ORGANISMS, INFECTIOUS  DISEASE, HEALTH AND WELLNESS, QUALITY, SOCIAL INTERACTIONS, AND ECONOMICS IN ANIMAL, PLANT, HUMAN,  NATURAL RESOURCES, ENVIRONMENT AND CLIMATE, ADVANCED TECHNOLOGY AND COMPUTER-HUMAN INTERACTIONS. THE AGRICULTURAL VIABILITY, PROFITABILITY, AND SUSTAINABILITY CRITICAL ISSUE WILL DEVELOP LOW INPUT AND  PROFITABLE INDOOR AGRICULTURAL PRODUCTION SYSTEMS; IMPROVE THE SUSTAINABILITY AND PROFITABILITY OF SMALL  RUMINANT PRODUCTION; ASSESS LABOR AND ECONOMIC EFFICIENCIES ASSOCIATED WITH ADVANCED TECHNOLOGICAL  AND SCIENTIFIC INNOVATIONS. THE BIOTECHNOLOGY, BIOMATERIALS, AND BIOENERGY CRITICAL ISSUE WILL IDENTIFY  NOVEL GENES THAT CAN BE USED TO IMPROVE CROP TOLERANCES TO ENVIRONMENTAL STRESSES, ESPECIALLY DROUGHT,  HEAT AND METAL TOXICITY; USE GENETIC AND GENOME APPROACHES FOR BREEDING NEW CROPS TO ADDRESS GLOBAL  ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS; DESIGN SUSTAINABLE VA LUE-ADDED ALTERNATIVES FOR AGRICULTURAL, FOOD, AND MATERIAL WASTE;  AND CREATE CELLULAR-BASED ALTERNATIVES FOR ADDRESSING ENVIRONMENTAL CHALLENGES, INCREASED AGRICULTURAL  PRODUCTION, AND EXPANDING FOOD RESOURCES. THE FOOD, NUTRITION AND HEALTH CRITICAL ISSUE WILL DEVELOP  AND DESIGN INNOVATIVE APPROACHES AND PROCESSES FOR MAINTAINING AND IMPROVING QUALITY, NUTRITIONAL  VALUE, AND SHELF-LIFE OF FOOD; AND IDENTIFY, DEVELOP, AND EVALUATE NOVEL BIOLOGICAL AND CHEMICAL  RESOURCES FOR ENHANCING HEALTH AND WELLNESS FOR PLANTS, ANIMALS, AND HUMANS. THE NATURAL RESOURCES,  ENVIRONMENT, AND CLIMATE CHANGE CRITICAL ISSUE WILL DEVELOP A RESILIENT FARMING SYSTEM THAT CAN COPE  WITH THE ADVERSE IMPACTS OF CLIMATE CHANGE; MINIMIZE THE EFFECTS OF CHANGING ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS ON LOW-INCOME  COMMUNITIES; AND EVALUATE CARBON SEQUESTRATION AND METHANE EMISSIONS RELATED TO NATURAL RESOURCES,  AGRICULTURAL PRACTICES, AND FOOD PROCESSING.

IN 2024, FOREST LANDS TOTALING NEARLY 20 MILLION ACRES PROVIDED $1.48 BILLION IN PRODUCTION FOR 130,000 MISSISSIPPI FOREST LANDOWNERS AND GENERATED MORE THAN $19 BILLION IN ECONOMIC IMPACT. THE FOREST INDUSTRY SUPPORTED 84,024 MISSISSIPPI JOBS WITH A $4.42 BILLION PAYROLL. THE MISSION OF THE COLLEGE OF FOREST RESOURCES (CFR) AND THE FOREST AND WILDLIFE RESEARCH CENTER (FWRC) IS TO FOSTER THE MANAGEMENT, CONSERVATION, AND SUSTAINABLE USE OF FOREST, WILDLIFE, AND AQUATIC RESOURCES TO BENEFIT THE PEOPLE OF MISSISSIPPI, THE NATION, AND THE WORLD. THROUGH TRANSFORMATIVE TEACHING AND LEARNING, RESEARCH AND DISCOVERY, OUTREACH, AND ENGAGEMENT, WE PREPARE FUTURE LEADERS, ENHANCE THE RESTORATION AND SUSTAINABLE USE OF RENEWABLE NATURAL RESOURCES, AND TRANSFER TECHNOLOGY INTO APPLICATION TO SOLVE THE GRAND CHALLENGES IN FORESTRY, FOREST PRODUCTS, AND WILDLIFE CONSERVATION. OUR RESEARCH INFORMS MANAGEMENT PRACTICES THAT MAKE OUR FOREST LANDOWNERS MORE PRODUCTIVE, PROFITABLE, AND ECOLOGICALLY SUSTAINABLE. THE GRADUATE EDUCATION PROGRAMS OF THE CFR TRAIN AND EQUIP THE NEXT GENERATION OF NATURAL RESOURCES PROFESSIONALS AND LEADERS. OUTREACH AND TECHNOLOGY TRANSFER PROGRAMS FACILITATE COORDINATION AMONG SCIENTISTS, AGENCIES, AND INDUSTRY STAKEHOLDERS. MISSISSIPPI FOREST LANDS PRODUCE MYRIAD FOREST PRODUCTS INCLUDING DIMENSIONAL LUMBER, VENEER, ENGINEERED WOOD PRODUCTS, FURNITURE, PALLETS, AND PAPER PRODUCTS. SCIENTISTS IN THE FWRC ARE DEVELOPING NEW SUSTAINABLE BIOPRODUCTS INCLUDING; MASS TIMBER ENGINEERED WOOD PRODUCTS, ADHESIVES, PRESERVATIVES, GRAPHENE-BASED COMPOSITE MATERIALS, AND LIGNIN-BASED NANOPARTICLES. THESE NEW VALUE-ADDED WOOD PRODUCTS WILL EXPAND MARKETS, SUPPORT ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT, AND INCREASE PROFITABILITY FOR FOREST LANDOWNERS. FWRC RESEARCH PROGRAMS SUPPORT ECONOMIC DEVELOPMENT. AS AN ILLUSTRATION, SOFTWARE AND METHODOLOGY DEVELOPED BY FWRC ARE USED BY THE MISSISSIPPI FORESTRY COMMISSION AND MISSISSIPPI DEVELOPMENT AUTHORITY TO INFORM SIT ING OF SAWMILLS, OSB/PLYWOOD AND PELLET PLANTS AND ATTRACT NEW INDUSTRIES TO THE STATE. THESE TOOLS DETERMINE THE IDEAL LOCATION TO BUILD A FACILITY, BASED ON AVAILABILITY OF THE RESOURCE AND ACCESS TO MARKETS AND TRANSPORTATION NETWORKS. EMERGING CARBON MARKETS PROVIDE AN OPPORTUNITY FOR MISSISSIPPI FOREST LANDOWNERS TO MONETIZE ENVIRONMENTAL SERVICES THAT PROVIDE A PUBLIC GOOD. FWRC SCIENTISTS ARE DEVELOPING DECISION SUPPORT TOOLS AND OUTREACH PRODUCTS TO HELP FOREST LANDOWNERS UNDERSTAND THESE MARKETS AND WEIGH THE COSTS AND BENEFITS OF HARVEST DEFERRAL FOR CARBON CREDITS. FWRC RESEARCH ON SHORT-ROTATION WOODY BIOMASS CROPS REDUCES OFF-SITE NUTRIENT TRANSPORT FROM AGRICULTURAL LANDS, SEQUESTERS CARBON, AND PROVIDES A CARBON-NEUTRAL ENERGY FEEDSTOCK. EMERGING WILDLIFE DISEASES THREATEN WILDLIFE POPULATIONS, HUMAN HEALTH, AND ASSOCIATED RECREATION AND ECONOMIC ACTIVITY. MISSISSIPPI IS ON THE GEOGRAPHIC SOUTHEASTERN LEADING EDGE OF THE SPREADING CHRONIC WASTING DISEASE (CWD) EPIDEMIC. SCIENTISTS IN THE FOREST AND WILDLIFE RESEARCH CENTER HAVE PARTNERED WITH THE MISSISSIPPI DEPARTMENT OF WILDLIFE, FISHERIES AND PARKS, AND THE MSU COLLEGE OF VETERINARY MEDICINE DIAGNOSTIC LAB SYSTEM TO RESPOND TO THIS NEW THREAT WITH SURVEILLANCE, DIAGNOSTICS, RESEARCH, AND POLICY DEVELOPMENT. DETECTION OF THIS EPIDEMIC WHILE GEOGRAPHICALLY LIMITED AND AT LOW PREVALENCE, PROVIDES A UNIQUE OPPORTUNITY TO APPLY A SCIENCE-BASED RESPONSE AND PROACTIVELY GET OUT IN FRONT WITH; DEVELOPMENT AND TESTING OF CONTAINMENT STRATEGIES, REGULATORY POLICIES, HUNTER EDUCATION, AND HUMAN HEALTH GUIDELINES. MCINTIRE-STENNIS FUNDING IN THE FWRC/CFR SUPPORTS 37 INDIVIDUAL ACTIVE M-S PROJECTS. MCINTIRE-STENNIS FUNDING IS LEVERAGED WITH $7.2 MILLION IN STATE APPROPRIATED FUNDS THAT COLLECTIVELY SUPPORT RESEARCH AND EDUCATION PROGRAMS TO ADVANCE MANAGEMENT, CONSERVATION AND UTILIZATION OF FOREST RESOURCES. STATE-LEVERAGED FUNDING SUPPORTS 31 M.S. AND PH.D. STUDENTS WORKING ON ACTIVE MCINTIRE-STENNIS PROJECTS.

ANNUAL APPROPRIATIONS UNDER THE MCINTIRE-STENNIS ACT OF 1962, IN COMBINATION WITH STATE APPROPRIATED FUNDING, ALLOW FACULTY TO CONDUCT FUNDAMENTAL AND APPLIED RESEARCH TO ADDRESS ISSUES AND DEVELOP OPPORTUNITIES FOR THE PEOPLE OF MAINE AND THE NATION. THE RESEARCH CAPACITY PROVIDED BY BASE FUNDING LEVERAGES ADDITIONAL FUNDING FROM COMPETITIVE GRANTS AND CONTRACTS AND INDUSTRY SUPPORT. UNIVERSITY OF MAINE FACULTY LEAD 25 RESEARCH PROJECTS IN THE MCINTIRE-STENNIS PROGRAM. MCINTIRE-STENNIS FUNDS ARE USED AT THE MAINE AGRICULTURAL AND FOREST EXPERIMENT STATION TO SUPPORT RESEARCH IN FOREST RESOURCES SPANNING A RANGE OF CURRENT ISSUES IN SILVICULTURE AND FOREST MANAGEMENT, WOOD SCIENCE AND FOREST PRODUCT DEVELOPMENT AND MARKETING, TO WILDLIFE HABITAT, OUTDOOR RECREATION, AND LAND USE POLICY. THE MAINE AGRICULTURAL AND FOREST EXPERIMENT STATION WILL USE ADMINISTRATIVE MCINTIRE-STENNIS FUNDS TO SUPPORT THE RESEARCH PROGRAM ADMINISTRATION AND FINANCIAL RECORDKEEPING AND REPORTING ACTIVITIES REQUIRED BY THE FEDERAL REGULATIONS THAT GOVERN THE EXPENDITURE OF MCINTIRE-STENNIS FUNDS. TYPICALLY, EACH MCINTIRE-STENNIS PROJECT WILL HAVE SEVERAL ASSOCIATED PROJECT ACTIVITIES SUPPORTED BY COMPETITIVE GRANTS OR OTHER SOURCES.

THE RESEARCH MISSION OF UF/IFAS, CONDUCTED UNDER THE AUSPICES OF THE FLORIDA AGRICULTURAL EXPERIMENT STATION (FAES), IS TO DISCOVER NEW SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE, ENCOURAGE INNOVATIVE STUDY, AND CREATE APPLICATIONS BASED ON SOUND SCIENCE THAT ADDRESS CHALLENGES FACING AGRICULTURE, NATURAL RESOURCES, AND INTERRELATED HUMAN SYSTEMS IN FLORIDA, OUR COUNTRY, AND THE WORLD. THE STATE HAS EXTENSIVE NATURAL AND PLANTED PINE AND HARDWOOD FORESTS THAT ARE OFTEN UTILIZED FOR THE COMMERCIAL PRODUCTION OF A WIDE VARIETY OF WOOD BUILDING MATERIALS, CONSUMER PAPER AND PACKAGING PRODUCTS, CHEMICALS, AND RENEWABLE BIOMASS FUELS. CONCURRENTLY MAINTAINING TREMENDOUS POPULATION GROWTH AND SIGNIFICANT AREA OF FORESTED LAND INCREASES THE NEED FOR NEW INFORMATION AND TECHNOLOGY RELATED TO FOOD AND FIBER PRODUCTION, WATER CONSERVATION, NATURAL RESOURCE PROTECTION, ALTERNATIVE ENERGY AND CONSERVATION, COMMUNITY RESOURCE DEVELOPMENT, AND INDIVIDUAL AND FAMILY WELL?BEING. UF/IFAS PROGRAMS IN FORESTRY, NATURAL RESOURCES, AND CONSERVATION ADDRESS THE ECOLOGICAL, SOCIAL, AND ECONOMIC ASPECTS OF MANAGING TERRESTRIAL NATURAL RESOURCES. WITHIN THIS BROAD FIELD, FACULTY AND STAFF WITH A VARIETY OF TECHNICAL AND ACADEMIC SPECIALTIES CONDUCT INNOVATIVE BASIC AND APPLIED SCIENCE; EDUCATE SOCIETY ON THE VALUE AND PROPER MANAGEMENT OF NATURAL RESOURCES, DEVELOP THE NEXT GENERATION OF PROFESSIONAL NATURAL RESOURCE MANAGERS AND WORK TO IMPROVE OUR NATURAL RESOURCES THROUGH OUTREACH TO THE PUBLIC, LANDOWNERS, AND RESOURCE STEWARDS. OUR WORK ON THE ECOLOGY OF TERRESTRIAL NATURAL RESOURCES INCLUDES SUCH SUBFIELDS AS THE ROLE OF DISTURBANCE/SUCCESSIONAL FORCES SUCH AS FIRES, STORMS, TIMBER HARVESTING, AND INSECT/DISEASE OUTBREAKS; THE CARBON AND WATER CYCLES OF FORESTS; AND BASIC TREE PHYSIOLOGY AND GENETICS. FACULTY AND STAFF STUDYING THE SOCIAL ASPECTS OF TERRESTRIAL ECOSYSTEMS ADDRESS THE VALUE OF RECREATIONAL OPPORTUNITIES, INCLUDING MANAGING ECOSYSTEMS TO BALANCE RECREATIONAL USE WITH RESOURCE PROTECTION; HOW THE PUBLIC UNDERSTANDS ENVIRONMENTAL ISSUES, AND HOW EDUCATORS CAN BETTER DISSEMINATE NEW INFORMATION ON ENVIRONMENTAL ISSUES; AND HOW PUBLIC POLICIES IMPACT THE WAY TERRESTRIAL ECOSYSTEMS ARE MANAGED. FORESTS CONTINUE TO HAVE A SIGNIFICANT ROLE IN SOCIETY FROM AN ECONOMIC PERSPECTIVE: IDENTIFYING NEW MARKETS FOR TIMBER PRODUCTS AND ECOSYSTEM SERVICES; HOW LANDOWNERS CHOOSE TO MANAGE THEIR LAND TO PRODUCE FINANCIAL RETURNS; AND HOW POLICY CHANGES INFLUENCE THE MARKETS FOR LAND, TIMBER, AND ECOSYSTEM SERVICES. THE PURPOSE OF THE MCINTIRE?STENNIS CAPACITY PROGRAM IS TO INCREASE FORESTRY RESEARCH IN THE PRODUCTION, UTILIZATION, AND PROTECTION OF FORESTLAND, TO TRAIN FUTURE FORESTRY SCIENTISTS, AND TO INVOLVE OTHER DISCIPLINES IN FORESTRY RESEARCH. AT THE TIME OF APPLICATION, UF/IFAS HAS 42 ACTIVE MCINTIRE?STENNIS CAPACITY PROJECTS THAT LEVERAGE PROGRAM FUNDS TO CONDUCT A WIDE RANGE OF INTERDISCIPLINARY RESEARCH ON TOPICS COVERED BY THE PROGRAM'S LEGISLATIVELY MANDATED RESEARCH TOPICS: 1) REFORESTATION AND MANAGEMENT OF LAND FOR THE PRODUCTION OF CROPS OF TIMBER AND OTHER RELATED PRODUCTS OF THE FOREST. 2) MANAGEMENT OF FOREST AND RELATED WATERSHED LANDS TO IMPROVE CONDITIONS OF WATER FLOW AND TO PROTECT RESOURCES AGAINST FLOODS AND EROSION. 3) MANAGEMENT OF FOREST AND RELATED RANGELAND FOR PRODUCTION OF FORAGE FOR DOMESTIC LIVESTOCK AND GAME AND IMPROVEMENT OF FOOD AND HABITAT FOR WILDLIFE. 4) MANAGEMENT OF FOREST LANDS FOR OUTDOOR RECREATION. 5) PROTECTION OF FOREST LAND AND RESOURCES AGAINST FIRE, INSECTS, DISEASES, OR OTHER DESTRUCTIVE AGENTS. 6) UTILIZATION OF WOOD AND OTHER FOREST PRODUCTS. 7) DEVELOPMENT OF SOUND POLICIES FOR THE MANAGEMENT OF FOREST LANDS AND THE HARVESTING AND MARKETING OF FOREST PRODUCTS. RESEARCH GENERATED BY THESE PROJECTS WILL BENEFIT SCIENTISTS, STUDENTS, GOVERNMENTAL AGENCIES, RANCHERS AND OTHER AGRICULTURAL PRODUCERS, INDUSTRY, NON?GOVERNMENTAL ORGANIZATIONS (NGOS), NON?PROFIT GROUPS, LANDOWNERS, LAND MANAGERS AND THE GENERAL PUBLIC

MOST PROJECTS FUNDED WITHIN THESE FOCUS AREAS ARE INTERDISCIPLINARY IN NATURE, BR INGING TOGETHER  DIVERSE TEAMS OF FACULTY, STAFF, AND STUDENTS ACROSS THE COLLEGE OF NATURAL RESOURCES AND THE  UNIVERSITY OF IDAHO TO FIND SOLUTIONS TO THE COMPLEX ISSUES FACING IDAHO'S FORESTS AND  RANGELANDS. negativeFlows.title: THE OVERARCHING GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO CREATE A PILOT-SCALE YEAR-ROUND INDOOR SPECIALTY MUSHROOM (SHIITAKE) CULTIVATION FACILITY ON FORESTRY PRODUCTS LIKE SAWDUST AND WOOD CHIPS AT ALCORN STATE AGRICULTURAL EXPERIMENT STATION. ACCORDINGLY, THE PROJECT WOULD ADDRESS ONE OF THE SEVEN LEGISLATIVELY MANDATED FORESTRY RESEARCH AREAS NAMELY UTILIZATION OF WOOD AND OTHER FOREST PRODUCTS. IN 2018, THERE WERE 19.7 MILLION ACRES OF FOREST LAND IN MISSISSIPPI, WITH 125,000 FOREST LANDOWNERS, AND FORESTRY CONTRIBUTING TO $1,250 MILLION. FORESTRY CONTINUES TO BE THE SECOND LARGEST REVENUE CONTRIBUTOR IN MISSISSIPPI. FOREST COVER IS SEEN IN MORE THAN 60% OF THE STATE AND 72% OF THIS LAND IS PRIVATELY OWNED. AT LEAST 25% OF THE WORKFORCE IS EMPLOYED IN THE FORESTRY SECTOR. WOOD SHAVINGS, SAWDUST, WOOD CHIPS AND BARK ARE PRODUCTS OF MILLING AND IN 2011 MISSISSIPPI MILLS PRODUCED 203 MILLION CUBIC FEET OF WOOD RESIDUE, WITH WOOD CHIPS ACCOUNTING FOR 41 PERCENT OF RESIDUES, 25% SAWDUST AND 7% WOOD SHAVINGS, RESPECTIVELY. MISSISSIPPI UTILIZES ALL THE FORESTRY RESIDUES AND IN 2011, 77% OF SAWDUST AND SHAVINGS WERE USED AS INDUSTRIAL FUEL. ANNUALLY THREE POUNDS OF FRESH MUSHROOMS ARE CONSUMED BY AMERICANS. MUSHROOM SALES REACHED A SECOND ALL-TIME HIGH IN 2017 WITH $1.2 BILLION. SPECIALTY MUSHROOMS ACCOUNTED FOR 2.7% OF THE SALES OF WHICH 1.1% OR 10.98 MILLION POUNDS OF SHIITAKE MUSHROOMS WERE SOLD. SHIITAKE WAS SOLD FOR $3.89/POUND AND RESULTED IN $40.7 MILLION SALES. SPECIALTY MUSHROOM SALES INCREASED BY 4% FROM THE PREVIOUS YEARS. MOST OF THE MUSHROOMS IN THE U.S. IN 2017 AS IN PREVIOUS YEARS WERE PRODUCED BY PENNSYLVANIA (64%) AND CALIFORNIA (11%). MISSISSIPPI IS NOT A CONTRIBUTOR TO THE NATIONAL MUSHROOM PRODUCTION AND/OR SALES STATISTICS. FOR A STATE ENDOWED WITH FORESTRY RESOURCES, AND AGRICULTURE INCLUDING FORESTRY RANKED THE LARGEST EMPLOYER, MUSHROOM CULTIVATION ON FORESTRY PRODUCTS OR AGRICULTURE RESIDUES IS NOT CONSIDERED AS AN INDUSTRY TO AUGMENT FARM INCOME. SINCE SHIITAKE CAN BE PRODUCED INDOORS IN ARTIFICIAL GROW BLOCKS YEAR-ROUND USING A COMBINATION OF SAWDUST, WOOD CHIPS, GRAIN AND BRAN, AND SINCE THE PRIMARY SUBSTRATES LIKE SAWDUST AND WOOD SHAVINGS ARE USED PRIMARILY AS FUEL IN MISSISSIPPI, THIS PROJECT AIMS TO DEVELOP A PILOT-SCALE INDOOR SHIITAKE CULTIVATION FACILITY AT THE ALCORN AGRICULTURAL EXPERIMENT STATION. THE INDOOR CULTIVATION OF SHIITAKE MUSHROOM BLOCKS IS SIMPLE, AND WE WILL UTILIZE THE WELL-PUBLISHED RECIPES. THE RECIPE WILL BE TAILORED TO INCLUDE A LARGER PROPORTION OF FORESTRY PRODUCTS AND THE MOST EFFICIENT SHIITAKE STRAIN WILL BE UTILIZED. FIVE POUND GROW BLOCKS PER BAG WILL BE INOCULATED WITH SHIITAKE STRAIN AND 20 BAGS WILL BE MADE PER BATCH. MUSHROOM QUALITATIVE AND QUANTITATIVE ANALYSES WILL BE CON DUCTED PER BATCH AND COMPARED TO THE USDA STANDARDS. AS A LAND-GRANT UNIVERSITY WITH A ROBUST EXTENSION PORTFOLIO SERVING A LARGE NUMBER OF SMALL FOREST LAND OWNERS AND FARMERS, A PILOT-SCALE SHIITAKE CULTIVATION FACILITY IS EXPECTED TO I) PROMOTE MUSHROOM CULTIVATION TO LAND OWNERS AS SOURCE TO AUGMENT FARM INCOME, II) PROMOTE ALTERNATIVE AND SUSTAINABLE USE OF FORESTRY PRODUCTS LIKE SAWDUST AND WOODCHIPS, III) EDUCATE STAKEHOLDERS OF SHIITAKE HEALTH BENEFITS AND DEMONSTRATE INDOOR CULTIVATION, AND IV) SERVE AS A PLATFORM TO CONDUCT BASIC RESEARCH ON INDOOR MUSHROOM CULTIVATION. IN THE LONG-TERM, THE GOAL IS ENSURING LARGE-SCALE ADOPTION OF SHIITAKE CULTIVATION AND CONTRIBUTE TO NATIONAL MUSHROOM SALES.

THE OVERALL GOAL OF THE MCINTIRE-STENNIS PROJECT AT VIRGINIA STATE UNIVERSITY IS TO GAIN A COMPLETE UNDERSTANDING OF THE GRAZING BEHAVIOR AND PERFORMANCE OF SHEEP AND GOATS AND GENERATE INFORMATION ON THE PRIMARY MEANS BY WHICH SHEEP AND GOATS CAN BE INTEGRATED INTO AGRO FORESTRY PRODUCTION SYSTEM. SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES ARE TO: A) INTEGRATE INFORMATION ON SOIL COMPOSITION, FORAGE GROWTH, BIOMASS AND QUALITY, IN AGROFORESTRY PRODUCTION SYSTEM, B) GENERATE INFORMATION ON GRAZING BEHAVIOR USING GPS TRACKING SYSTEMS AND EVALUATE ANIMAL PERFORMANCE IN AGRO FORESTRY PRODUCTION SYSTEMS AND C) OYSTER MUSHROOM CULTIVATION ON THINNED LOGS. THE INTENTIONAL COMBINATION OF TREES, FORAGE, AND LIVESTOCK ON A PARCEL OF LAND TO MAXIMIZE MULTIPLE OUTPUTS HAS BEEN SHOWN TO HAVE BENEFITS. SUCH AGRICULTURAL PRACTICES HAVE LARGELY NOT BEEN STUDIED DESPITE A GREAT DEAL OF INTEREST. PRODUCERS WHO ARE INTERESTED IN LOCAL, NATURAL/ORGANIC FOOD, LIVESTOCK AND FORAGE AND FORESTRY PRODUCTION SYSTEMS SEE THIS FOREST-PASTURE-LIVESTOCK AS A POTENTIALLY SUSTAINABLE AND ENVIRONMENTALLY-FRIENDLY OPTION TO CONSERVE SOIL AND WATER, MAINTAIN AND INCREASE CARBON STOCKS, AND PROVIDE HABITAT FOR LIVESTOCK AND WILDLIFE. THE PURPOSE OF THIS PROJECT IS TO EVALUATE THE USE AND MANAGEMENT OF STANDS OF WOODLAND/FOREST, PASTURE AND LIVESTOCK ON THE SAME PIECE OF LAND IN A SUSTAINABLE PRODUCTION SYSTEM. THE STUDY FOCUSES ON THE GRAZING BEHAVIOR INCLUDING TEMPORAL AS WELL AS SPATIAL DISTRIBUTION OF SHEEP AND GOATS USING GPS COLLARS IN SUCH PRODUCTION SYSTEM. A GPS DATABASE LABORATORY WILL BE ESTABLISHED BY AC QUIRING GPS COLLARS AND ACCESSORIES. BASELINE INFORMATION IS ALSO COLLECTED ON FORAGE, LIVESTOCK, FOREST AND SOIL, WHICH WILL BE USED TO ESTIMATE CARRYING CAPACITY AND STOCKING DENSITY, ANIMAL PERFORMANCE FORAGE BIOMASS AND QUALITY. STAKEHOLDERS INCLUDING SMALL, T RADITIONAL AND URBAN FARMERS WILL BE TRAINED ON MUSHROOM CULTIVATION ON LOGS FROM THINNED FOREST AS AN ALTERNATIVE TO AUGMENT INCOME. RESEARCH ON INTEGRATION OF FOREST, PASTURE AND LIVESTOCK ON A PIECE OF LAND CAN BE BENEFICIAL IN INCREASING WATER AVAILABILITY, GR EATER BIODIVERSITY, ENHANCED ECONOMIC OR SOCIAL RETURNS FROM FOREST LAND OWNERSHIP OR USAGE, AND DECREASED FIRE HAZARDS. STUDENTS WILL RECEIVE TRAINING AND EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING IN AGROFORESTRY. ESTABLISHMENT OF AGRO FORESTRY RESEARCH SITE FOR FUTURE STUDY.

THE UNIVERSITY OF PUERTO RICO AGRICULTURAL EXPERIMENT STATION MAINTAINS A SMALL BUT IMPORTANT FORESTRY RESEARCH PROGRAM FINANCED BY MCINTIRE-STENNIS FUNDS. THESE FUNDS SUPPORT RESEARCH ON USEFUL TECHNOLOGIES FOR REFORESTATION PROJECTS AND FOR THE MANAGEMENT OF WA TERSHEDS RELATED TO FORESTS, ON THE ECONOMIC VIABILITY OF DEVELOPING RECREATIONAL OPPORTUNITIES IN FORESTS, AND ON ESTABLISHING USEFUL BASELINE DATA FOR THE DEVELOPMENT OF MANAGEMENT PLANS OF SELECTED FORESTS. INTENDED BENEFICIARIES OF RESEARCH ACTIVITIES INCLUDE LOCAL GOVERNMENT AGENCIES SUCH AS THE DEPARTMENT OF NATURAL AND ENVIRONMENTAL RESOURCES, THE DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE, AND THE PUERTO RICO PLANNING BOARD; RESIDENTS LIVING IN AREAS SURROUNDING THE FORESTS SELECTED FOR RESEARCH ACTIVITIES; THE SCIENTIFIC AND ACADEMIC COMMUNITY; AND PRIVATE AND PUBLIC ENTITIES INTERESTED IN REFORESTATION PROJECTS IN AREAS WITH LIMITED WATER SUPPLY. ACTIVITIES PLANNED INCLUDE: (1) EXPERIMENTS WITH TECHNOLOGIES FOR OVERCOMING DROUGHT MORTALITY OF JUVENILE TREES IN REFORESTATION PROJECTS; (2)ANALYSES OF SEDIMENT IN THREE RESERVOIRS CONSTRUCTED PRIOR TO 1950 TO RECONSTRUCT THE ECOLOGICAL EVOLUTION (>70 YR) OF THEIR WATERSHEDS AND ULTIMATELY USE THE INFORMATION TO DEVELOP A LOCAL FRAMEWORK FOR THE PLANNING OF SUSTAINABLE MULTIFUNCTIONAL LANDSCAPES IN PUERTO RICO; (3) CHOICE EXPERIMENTS TO EXAMINE RESIDENTS' WILLINGNESS TO PAY FOR RECREATIONAL OPPORTUNITIES IN SELECTED FORESTS AND COST-BENEFIT ANALYSES OF DEVELOPING THE INTENDED RECREATIONAL ACTIVITIES; AND (4) THE ESTABLISHMENT OF A LONG-TERM, ECOLOGICAL RESEAR CH STATION FOR THE STUDY OF LAND COVER CHANGE, CARBON AND BIODIVERSITY LINKAGES ON SERPENTINE SOILS, AS WELL AS THE BENEFITS NEIGHBORING COMMUNITIES MAY GAIN FROM THEIR INVOLVEMENT IN THE DEVELOPMENT AND IMPLEMENTATION OF A MANAGEMENT PLAN FOR THE STATION. DELIVERABLES FROM PROJECTS' ACTIVITIES INCLUDE PUBLICATION IN PEER REVIEWED JOURNALS AND POPULAR MEDIA OUTLETS (NEWSPAPERS, PODCASTS, SOCIA L MEDIA), POSTERS AND ORAL PRESENTATIONS AT SCIENTIFIC MEETINGS DEPICTING PROJECT RESULTS; AN UPDATED GEOGRAPHICAL INFORMATION SYSTEM CONTAINING LAND COVER, SOIL, AND GEOLOGICAL INFORMATION LAYERS OF THE THREE MAJOR WATERSHEDS OF PUERTO RICO; PROOF-OF-CONCEPT OF UPSCALED EARTH-WATER DISTILLATION TECHNOLOGY FOR JUVENILE TREE IRRIGATION AND HUMAN CONSUMPTION IN REMOTE ARID AND SEMIARID ENVIRONMENTS; AND INCREASED DOCUMENTATION OF INTERACTIONS BETWEEN LAND COVER CHANGE, CARBON STORAGE CAPACITY AND BIODIVERSITY OF SERPENTINE SOILS IN THE CARIBBEAN. EXPECTED OUTCOMES INCLUDE AN INCREASED AWARENESS OF THE VALUE OF FORESTS ON THE ISLAND; THE INCORPORATION OF ECOLOGICAL TRADE-OFFS AS PART OF THE PLANNING PROCESS FOR SUSTAINABLE MULTIFUNCTIONAL LANDSCAPES IN PUERTO RICO; INCREASED PUBLIC AWARENESS AND USE OF SMALL COMMERCIALLY AVAILABLE WATER-VAPOR CONDENSATION DEVICES FOR MORE EFFECTIVE REFORESTATION IN ARID ENVIRONMENTS; AND INCREASED INFORMATION ON THE BENEFITS FROM CONSERVATION AND ECOSYSTEM SERVICES THAT FOREST LANDS CAN PROVIDE TO NEIGHBORING RESIDENTS AND ACADEMIC COMMUNITIES.

THE OBJECTIVES ARE TO EXAMINE AND MAP TREE MORTALITY AND CANOPY STRUCTURE USING DRONE FLEETS TO IMPROVE UNDERSTANDING AND BETTER DESCRIBE THE HEALTH DIFFERENTIAL OF 'HEALTHY' AND 'UNHEALTHY' FORESTS AND TREES CONSIDERING HUMAN, CLIMATIC, AND BIOTIC DRIVERS. SECONDLY, WE WILL EVALUATE THE PARAMETERS ASSOCIATED WITH DECLINE/DISEASE AND PRESENCE OF PATHOGENS, INCLUDING THE ROLE OF FUNGI IN THE FORMATION OF CANOPY OPENINGS, TREE COMPETITION, AND CANOPY STRUCTURE. FINALLY, WE WILL CONDUCT PATHOGENICITY TESTS ON SPECIES CORRELATED WITH DISEASE OUTBREAKS. OPTIMIZATION OF GENETICALLY IMPROVED SEEDLINGS FOR SOUTHERN FORESTS. WOOD UTILIZATION IN A CHANGING ECONOMIC ENVIRONMENT RECOGN IZING INTRICATE, AND POTENTIALLY MESSY, INTERACTIONS BETWEEN THE ENVIRONMENT, SOCIETY, AND ECONOMY IN THIS POST-RECESSIONAL ERA REQUIRES NOVEL LEVELS OF UNDERSTANDING. THIS IS CRITICAL TO TRANSFORMING CHALLENGES INTO OPPORTUNITIES. THIS WORK WILL EXPLORE THREE PRIMARY AVENUES BY WHICH PRODUCTION FORESTRY CURRENTLY CONTRIBUTES TO, AND CAN POTENTIALLY INCREASE ITS IMPACTS ON, REGIONAL ECONOMIES: BY BRINGING NEW MONEY INTO THE REGION VIA EXPORTS, NEXT BY DEVELOPING NEW OR SUBSTITUTING LOCALLY PRODUCED GOODS AND SERVICES FOR IMPORTED INPUTS, AND FINALLY ATTRACTING VALUE ADDED MANUFACTURING THAT CAN INCREASE REGIONAL PRODUCT. 3.
