THE URI COLLEGE OF THE ENVIRONMENT AND LIFE SCIENCES (CELS) IS THE HOME OF RHODE ISLAND'S AGRICULTURAL EXPERIMENT STATION (AES) AND COOPERATIVE EXTENSION (EXTENSION). URI'S LAND GRANT PROGRAMS ADDRESS A WIDE RANGE OF NATIONAL AND INTERNATIONAL ISSUES, WITH AN EMPHASIS ON THE NEEDS OF OUR STATE. OUR RESEARCH AND EXTENSION PROGRAMS SEEK TO IMPROVE RHODE ISLANDERS' QUALITY OF LIFE, THEIR LIVELIHOODS, AND THE HEALTH OF OUR NATURAL ENVIRONMENT, WITH SPECIAL ATTENTION TO LOCAL PROBLEMS. LOCAL TO GLOBAL ENVIRONMENTAL CHANGE - INCREASE OUR ABILITY TO RESPOND AND ADAPT TO LOCAL, REGIONAL, AND GLOBAL ENVIRONMENTAL CHANGES. HUMAN AND ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH - INCREASE OUR ABILITY TO RECOGNIZE AND MANAGE EMERGENT HUMAN AND ENVIRONMENTAL HEALTH CHALLENGES. YOUTH, FAMILY, AND COMMUNITY DEVELOPMENT - INCREASE OUR ABILITY TO UNDERSTAND, RESPOND, AND ADAPT TO SOCIAL, ENVIRONMENTAL, AND ECONOMIC CHALLENGES FACING RI YOUTH, FAMILIES, AND COMMUNITIES. OUTCOMES/DELIVERABLES - MCINTIRE STENNIS COOPERATIVE FORESTRY RESEARCH: MAXIMIZE THE CAPACITY OF MANAGED ENVIRON MENTS TO PROVIDE ECOSYSTEM SERVICES SUCH AS NUTRIENT MANAGEMENT, WATER QUALITY AND HABITAT. UNDERSTAND HOW THE COUPLING BETWEEN HUMAN AND NATURAL SYSTEMS CAN ENHANCE AND PRESERVE BIODIVERSITY, ENHANCE RESILIENCE, IMPROVE THE MANAGEMENT OF AQUACULTURE, FISHERIES, AND WILDLIFE POPULATIONS AND HABITATS, AND PROMOTE A VIBRANT, SUSTAINABLE ENVIRONMENT. STRENGTHEN OUR ABILITY TO DEVELOP THE REGION'S BLUE ECONOMY IN A MORE JUST, EQUITABLE MANNER THROUGH INTERDISCIPLINARY APPROACHES AND COMMUNITY ENGAGED SCHOLARSHIP. UNDERSTAND AND ADDRESS THE DISTRIBUTION AND IMPACTS OF HUMAN AND ENVIRONMENTAL CHALLENGES ACROSS COMMUNITIES, WHICH HAVE IMPLICATIONS FOR SOCIAL AND ECONOMIC SUSTAINABILITY. INCREASE THE CAPACITY OF PLANNERS TO IMPROVE URBAN, FARM, PARK, COASTAL AND OPEN SPACE DEVELOPMENT BY ADDRESSING COMMUNITY NEEDS WITHIN THE CONTEXT OF CLIMATE CHANGE.

MANY UNDERSERVED GEORGIA LANDOWNERS LACK ACCESS TO PROPER KNOWLEDGE ABOUT SUSTAINABLE LAND MANAGEMENT PRACTICES. UNDERSERVED FOREST OWNERS FROM RACIAL AND ETHNIC MINORITIES HAVE MARKED DIFFERENCES FROM OTHER OWNERS. THE BIGGEST DIFFERENCES ARE IN TERMS OF PARTICIPATION IN TECHNICAL ASSISTANCE PROGRAMS AND FOREST-MANAGEMENT PRACTICES. THIS HAS IMPORTANT IMPLICATIONS FOR THOSE INTERESTED IN FOREST MANAGEMENT AND POLICY ISSUES. UNDERSTANDING THE ECONOMIC BENEFITS OF WELL MANAGED FORESTS WILL ALLOW UNDERSERVED FORESTERS AND LANDOWNERS TO BETTER GENERATE INCOME THROUGH SUSTAINABLE TIMBER HARVESTING, NON-TIMBER FOREST PRODUCTS, AGROFORESTRY, AND THE USE OF TECHNOLOGY. TARGET AUDIENCES FOR THIS M-S PROJECT ARE SMALL AND MEDIUM (OWNING LESS THAN 10 ACRES) FORESTRY LANDOWNERS NOT GENERALLY SERVED BY CURRENT FEDERAL, STATE, AND LOCAL PROGRAMS. THIS PROJECT'S LONG-TERM GOAL IS TO FACILITATE SMALL, MEDIUM, AND UNDERSERVED FOREST LANDOWNERS' UNDERSTANDING OF PRECISION FORESTRY, ECOSYSTEM SERVICES, AND SOCIAL AND ECONOMIC BENEFITS THROUGH USE OF INNOVATIVE TECHNOLOGY. THE SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES OF THE PROPOSED STUDY ARE AS FOLLOWS; 1) IDENTIFY SMALL, MEDIUM, AND UNDERSERVED FORESTRY LANDOWNERS IN GEORGIA AND DETERMINE ATTITUDES AND PERCEPTIONS IN FORESTRY ACTIVITIES USING A MIXED-METHOD PILOT SURVEY. 2) PROVIDE TWO WORKSHOPS ANNUALLY FOR SMALL, MEDIUM, AND UNDERSERVED FORESTRY LANDOWNERS TO COMMUNICATE THE CONCEPTS AND APPROACHES OF SUSTAINABLE FOREST MANAGEMENT USING INNOVATIVE TECHNOLOGY UNDER FORT VALLEY STATE UNIVERSITY'S COOPERATIVE EXTENSION PROGRAM. 3) IDENTIFY A FORESTRY LOCATION AT FORT VALLEY STATE UNIVERSITY AND DEVELOP A REFORESTATION SITE WITH HARDWOOD TO SERVE AS A DEMONSTRATION AND TRAINING SITE FOR SMALL, MEDIUM, AND UNDERSERVED FORESTRY LANDOWNERS. 4) INCORPORATE TECHNOLOGY TO MONITOR AND AID THE GROWTH PARAMETERS AND HEALTH CONDITIONS OF PINE TREES. DRONES AND REMOTE SENSORS WILL SERVE AS INPUTS FOR PRECISION FORESTRY FOR OPEN-SOURCE DATA COLLECTION. COMPUTER TECHNOLOGY (LMS, GIS) WILL SERVE AS COMMUNICATION OUTPUTS. THE GOALS AND OBJECTIVES OF THIS PROJECT WILL ENHANCE THE SUSTAINABLE MANAGEMENT OF FORESTLAND OWNED BY UNDERSERVED LANDOWNERS IN GEORGIA.

ABSTRACT: THE OUTLINED MCINTIRE-STENNIS (M-S) PROPOSAL ADDRESSES ONE OF THE SEVEN LEGISLATIVELY MANDATED FORESTRY RESEARCH AREAS NAMELY 6) UTILIZATION OF WOOD AND OTHER FOREST PRODUCTS. THE STATE OF MISSISSIPPI HAS 19.7 MILLION ACRES OF FOREST LAND, WITH 125,000 FOREST LANDOWNERS, AND FORESTRY CONTRIBUTING TO $1393 MILLION IN 2017. FORESTRY CONTINUES TO BE THE SECOND LARGEST REVENUE CONTRIBUTOR, NEXT ONLY TO POULTRY PRODUCTION IN MISSISSIPPI. FOREST COVER IS SEEN IN MORE THAN 60% OF THE STATE AND 72% OF THIS LAND IS PRIVATELY OWNED. HARDWOODS ACCOUNT FOR MORE THAN 50% OF MISSISSIPPI'S LIVE TREE VOLUME AND LOBLOLLY PINE (PINUS TAEDA), SWEETGUM (LIQUIDAMBAR STYRACIFLUA) AND WATER OAK (QUERCUS NIGRA) ARE MOST ABUNDANT IN MISSISSIPPI. WOOD SHAVINGS, SAWDUST, WOOD CHIPS AND BARK ARE PRODUCTS OF MILLING AND IN 2011 MISSISSIPPI MILLS PRODUCED 203 MILLION CUBIC FEET OF WOOD RESIDUE, WITH WOOD CHIPS ACCOUNTING FOR 41 PE RCENT OF RESIDUES, 25% SAWDUST AND 7% WOOD SHAVINGS RESPECTIVELY. MISSISSIPPI UTILIZES ALL THE FORESTRY RESIDUES AND IN 2011, 77% OF SAWDUST AND SHAVINGS WERE USED AS INDUSTRIAL FUEL. MISSISSIPPI IS NOT A CONTRIBUTOR TO THE NATIONAL MUSHROOM PRODUCTION AND/OR SALES STATISTICS. MUSHROOM PRODUCTION INCLUDING SPECIALTY MUSHROOMS THAT CAN BE CULTIVATED YEAR-ROUND ON SAWDUST/WOOD CHIPS IS NOT POPULAR IN MISSISSIPPI DESPITE THE ABUNDANT AVAILABILITY OF FOREST PRODUCTS. OVERALL, MISSISSIPPI HAS ABUNDANT OAK AND SWEETGUM TREES AND THEIR HARDWOOD RESIDUES CAN EASILY SUPPORT THE CULTIVATION OF SPECIALTY MUSHROOMS TO I) MAKE INROADS INTO THE EVER-INCREASING U.S. SPECIALTY MUSHROOM MARKET (SPECIALTY MUSHROOMS PER POUND SELL THREE TO FOUR TIMES THE PRICE OF REGULAR MUSHROOMS), II) SUSTAINABLE UTILIZATION OF FORESTRY RESOURCES (AS MENTIONED ABOVE MOST OF THE SAWDUST IS BURNED AS FUEL; A PORTION OF THIS CAN BE UTILIZED FOR INDOOR SHIITAKE PRODUCTION), III) AUGMENT FARM/FORESTRY INCOME SINCE AGRICULTURE IS THE LARGEST EMPLOYER IN MISSISSIPPI (WITH THE SUCCESSFUL UTILIZATION OF SAWDUST/WOOD CHIPS FOR YEAR-ROUND SHIITAKE CULTIVATION, IN THE LONG-TERM FOREST OWNERS CAN CONTRIBUTE TO LARGE-SCALE SHIITAKE CULTIVATION), AND IV) PROMOTE THE INCLUSION OF MUSHROOMS AS A LOW-CALORIE HEALTHY FOOD CHOICE (MUSHROOMS ARE NOT A PART OF THE DIET, AND AS THE SHIITAKE INDOOR CULTIVATION BECOMES POPULAR INCLUDING MUSHROOMS AS A FOOD CHOICE MAY GAIN MOMENTUM).  THE OVERARCHING GOAL OF THIS PROJECT IS TO CONDUCT INDOOR CULTIVATION OF SPECIALTY MUSHROOM (SHIITAKE; LENTINUS EDODES) ON FORESTRY PRODUCTS LIKE SAWDUST AND WOOD CHIPS. SPECIFICALLY, THE PROJECT AIMS ARE I) TO DEVELOP A YEAR-ROUND, PILOT SCALE INDOOR SHIITAKE CU LTIVATION ON GROW- BLOCKS (SYNTHETIC LOGS) AT THE MUSHROOM FACILITY AT THE ALCORN AGRICULTURE EXPERIMENT STATION, LORMAN, MS FOR DEMONSTRATION TO OUR STAKEHOLDERS MAINLY SMALL AND RESOURCE LIMITED FARMERS AND LANDOWNERS; II) TO EVALUATE THE YIELD AND NUTRITIONAL C OMPOSITION OF SHIITAKE CULTIVATED ON TRADITIONAL RECIPE OF SAWDUST/WHOLE-LOG CHIP, GRAIN AND/OR BRAN AND COMPARE THEM TO THE USDA NUTRIENT DATABASE; AND III) TO CALIBRATE THE PILOT-SCALE SHIITAKE CULTIVATION BASED ON LOCAL AVAILABILITY OF FORESTRY PRODUCTS FOR SUS TAINED SHIITAKE PRODUCTION.

GIVEN THE DECLINING NUMBERS OF MINORITIES WHO ENROLLED IN FORESTRY AND NATURAL RESOURCE PROGRAMS NATIONWIDE, THE COLLEGE OF AGRICULTURE AND FOOD SCIENCES (CAFS) IS IN AN OPPORTUNE POSITION TO ASSIST IN REVERSING THIS TREND BECAUSE OF ITS HISTORICAL RECORD OF RECRUITING, INSTRUCTING, AND GRADUATING MINORITY STUDENTS IN AGRICULTURAL AND RELATED SCIENCES. STRENGTHENING THE PROGRAM IN CAFS IS EXPECTED TO BRING ABOUT THE FOLLOWING BENEFITS: STRENGTHEN THE OVERALL TEACHING AND RESEARCH CAPACITY OF CAFS AND THE UNIVERSITY; PROMOTE AND STIMULATE RESEARCH IN FORESTRY AND NATURAL RESOURCES AND INCREASE THE NUMBER OF GRADUATES IN THESE AREAS, INCREASE THE POOL OF GRADUATES FOR THE UNITED STATES DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE (USDA) WORKFORCE DIVERSITY GOALS, ATTRACT AND RECRUIT QUALITY STUDENTS FROM 1862 AND 1890 INSTITUTIONS FOR CAREERS IN FORESTRY AND NATURAL RESOURCE CONSERVATION, STRENGTHEN AND EXPAND LINKAGES AND RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN THE CAFS, THE USDA AND STAKEHOLDER GROUPS, PROMOTE THE GOALS OF THE MCINTIRE-STENNIS COOPERATIVE FORESTRY RESEARCH PROGRAM. STUDENTS WILL PARTICIPATE IN THE MULTIDISCIPLINARY RESEARCH PROJECTS AND WORK UNDER THE SUPERVISION OF PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATORS/PROGRAM DIRECTORS. THE MCINTIRE-STENNIS SCHOLARS WILL ALSO BE PROVIDED WITH EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING ACTIVITIES TO WORK WITH OTHER RES EARCHERS IN THE COLLEGE OR OTHER INSTITUTIONS AND COLLABORATING PARTNERS. THIS APPROACH IS EXPECTED TO FURTHER IMPROVE THEIR TRAINING, PREPARATION, AND DESIRE TO ATTAIN ADDITIONAL KNOWLEDGE AND PURSUE ADVANCED DEGREES.

FOREST FARMING PRACTICES INVOLVE CULTIVATING HIGH-VALUE SPECIALTY CROPS IN THE FOREST UNDERSTORY WITH SPECIFIC MANAGEMENT OF THE CANOPY AND THE FOREST OVERSTORY TO PROMOTE THE GROWTH AND ESTABLISHMENT OF THE DESIRED CROP. THE UNDERSTORY OR SPECIALTY CROPS (NON-TIMBER FOREST PRODUCTS, NTFPS) CAN INCLUDE VARIOUS ITEMS FOR FOOD (MUSHROOMS AND NUTS), BOTANICALS (HERBS AND MEDICINAL), DECORATIVE (FLORAL GREENERY AND DYES), AND HANDICRAFTS (BASKETS ANN WOOD PRODUCTS). ALTHOUGH FOREST FARMING INVOLVES MODIFYING THE FOREST ECOSYSTEM, IF CORRECTLY DONE, THE PRIMARY FOREST FUNCTIONS ARE NOT NEGATIVELY IMPAIRED BUT ENHANCED. THIS STUDY IS DESIGNED TO EVALUATE THE FEASIBILITY OF FOREST FARMING OF FOUR MISSOURI NATIVE PERENNIAL HERBS BLACK COHOSH (ACTAEA RACEMOSA L.), RICHWEED (COLLINSONIA CANADENSIS L.), GOLDEN SEAL (HYDRASTIS CANADENSIS L.), AND GERANIUM (GERANIUM MACULATUM L.) AND THE IMPACT OF TIMBER STAND IMPROVEMENT (TSI) AND PRESCRIBED BURN (PB) ON FOREST ECOSYSTEM PROCESSES. THE SPECIFIC OBJECTIVES INCLUDE, I) EVALUATE THE ESTABLISHMENT AND PRODUCTIVITY OF SELECTED NATIVE HERB SPECIES IN MISSOURI WOODLANDS FOR FOREST FARMING, II) DETERMINE THE IMPACT OF ASSOCIATED FOREST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES (TIMBER STAND IMPROVEMENT AND PRESCRIBED BURN) ON PHOTOSYNTHETIC RESOURCE ALLOCATION, GREENHOUSE GAS EMISSIONS AND SOIL CHEMICAL PROPERTIES, AND III) MONITOR THE EFFECT OF FOREST FARMING ACTIVITIES ON SOIL MICROBIAL COMMUNITY AND FUNCTION. THIS PROJECT WILL BENEFIT SMALL FARMERS AND FOREST LANDOWNERS IN MISSOURI AND THE MIDWESTERN US BY GENERATING ECONOMIC INCOME BY INCORPORATING FOREST FARMING PRACTICES. AS AN ADDED BENEFIT, FOREST HEALTH WILL ALSO IMPROVE FROM THE TSI AND PB TREATMENTS. PROJECT OUTCOMES WILL LEAD TO THE DEVELOPMENT OF BEST MANAGEMENT PRACTICES FOR FOREST WOODLOTS AND PROMOTE BETTER DECISION-MAKING PROCESSES FOR FOREST LANDOWNERS, CONSERVATIONISTS, STATE AND LOCAL GOVERNMENTS, AND OTHER STAKEHOLDERS.

GIVEN THE DECLINING NUMBERS OF MINORITIES WHO ENROLLED IN FORESTRY AND NATURAL RESOURCE PROGRAMS NATIONWIDE, THE COLLEGE OF AGRICULTURE AND FOOD SCIENCES (CAFS) IS IN AN OPPORTUNE POSITION TO ASSIST IN REVERSING THIS TREND BECAUSE OF ITS HISTORICAL RECORD OF RECRUITING, INSTRUCTING, AND GRADUATING MINORITY STUDENTS IN AGRICULTURAL AND RELATED SCIENCES. STRENGTHENING THE GRADUATE PROGRAM IN CAFS IS EXPECTED TO BRING ABOUT THE FOLLOWING BENEFITS: STRENGTHEN THE OVERALL TEACHING AND RESEARCH CAPACITY OF CAFS AND THE UNIVERSITY.  PROMOTE AND STIMULATE RESEARCH IN FORESTRY AND NATURAL RESOURCES AND INCREASE THE NUMBER OF GRADUATES IN THESE AREAS.  INCREASE THE POOL OF GRADUATES FOR THE UNITED STATES DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE (USDA) WORKFORCE DIVERSITY GOALS.  ATTRACT AND RECRUIT QUALITY STUDENTS FROM 1862 AND 1890 INSTITUTIONS FOR CAREERS IN FORESTRY AND NATURAL RESOURCE CONSERVATION. STRENGTHEN AND EXPAND LINKAGES AND RELATIONSHIPS BETWEEN THE CAFS, THE USDA AND STAKEHOLDER GROUPS.  PROMOTE THE GOALS OF THE MCINTIRESTENNIS COOPERATIVE FORESTRY RESEARCH PROGRAM. THE COLLEGE HAS A TRACK RECORD OF TRAINING GRADUATE AND UNDERGRADUATE AFRICAN AMERICAN STUDENTS WHO HAVE EARNED TOP HONORS AND OUTSTANDING AWARDS IN ACADEMIA AND IN THE PROFESSIONAL ARENA AT THE STATE, REGIONAL, AND NATIONAL LEVELS. THE EXISTING GRADUATE PROGRAMS HAVE BEEN FUNDED FROM A WIDE RANGE OF SOURCES, NAMELY, THE CAPACITY BUILDING GRANTS, NATIONAL INSTITUTE OF FOOD AND AGRICULTURE  NIFA GRANTS, NATIONAL SCIENCE FOUNDATION GRANTS, FLORIDA DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE VITICULTURE GRANTS, FLORIDA DEPARTMENT OF AGRICULTURE  SPECIALTY CROP GRANTS, AND FAMUS GRADUATE ASSISTANTSHIPS. HOWEVER, TO SUSTAIN AND BUILD ON CURRENT EFFORTS, MORE SECURED SOURCES OF FUNDING ARE REQUIRED SUCH AS THE MCINTIRESTENNIS PROGRAM TO STRENGTHEN AND GROW THE GRADUATE PROGRAM TO ITS FULL POTENTIAL; THIS IS PARTICULARLY THE CASE FOR THE FORESTRY AND NATURAL RESOURCES AREA. THE COLLEGE, AS PREVIOUSLY STATED, IS A PARTICIPANT IN THE MCINTIRESTENNIS PROGRAM WHICH PROVIDES AN EXCELLENT OPPORTUNITY TO STABILIZE, SUSTAIN AND GROW OUR EXISTING FORESTRY AND NATURAL RESOURCES RESEARCH PROGRAMS THROUGH GREATER GRADUATE STUDENT PARTICIPATION. THE FUNDS WILL BE USED TO SUPPORT OUTSTANDING GRADUATE AND UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS WHO WILL CONDUCT RESEARCH UNDER THE MENTORSHIP AND SUPERVISION OF THE GRADUATE FACULTY. THE PROPOSED ESTABLISHMENT OF THE MCINTIRE STENNIS ASSISTANTSHIP PROGRAM (MISAP) WILL ENABLE CAFS TO RECRUIT QUALITY STUDENTS AND CANDIDATES FOR PROFESSIONAL DEGREES FROM ITS STUDENT BODY AND PREPARE THEM FOR PROFESSIONAL / DOCTORAL DEGREES AS WELL AS THE COMPETITIVE JOB MARKET. A. APPROACH AND COOPERATIVE LINKAGES 1. OBJECTIVES THE OBJECTIVE OF THIS PROPOSAL IS TO STRENGTHEN AND EXPAND THE GRADUATE PROGRAM IN FORESTRY AND NATURAL RESOURCES CONSERVATION IN THE COLLEGE OF AGRICULTURE AND FOOD SCIENCES BY ESTABLISHING THE MCINTIRESTENNIS ASSISTANTSHIP PROGRAM (MISAP) THAT WILL FACILITATE THE FOLLOWING: 1. RECRUITMENT, RETENTION, AND INSTRUCTION OF OUTSTANDING UNDERGRADUATE STUDENTS IN THE GRADUATE PROGRAM WITH POTENTIAL FOR ADVANCED GRADUATE STUDIES AND MORE COMPETITIVE GRADUATES. 2. PROMOTING AND STRENGTHENING MULTIDISCIPLINARY RESEARCH IN FORESTRY AND NATURAL RESOURCES RELATED PROGRAMS THROUGH UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE RESEARCH PARTICIPATION. 3. AWARDS AND RECOGNITION OF OUTSTANDING ACCOMPLISHMENTS BY STUDENTS AND FACULTY. 2. METHODOLOGY AND PLAN OF WORK OBJECTIVE 1. TO RECRUIT OUTSTANDING UNDERGRADUATE AND GRADUATE STUDENTS IN THE MCINTIRESTENNIS PROGRAM, WE WILL PUBLICIZE THE PROGRAM AND ENCOURAGE ACTIVE PARTICIPATION FROM THE FACULTY AND STUDENTS. WE WILL IDENTIFY GOOD STUDENTS AND ENCOURAGE THEM TO PARTICIPATE IN THE PROGRAM. STUDENTS IN THE COLLEGE WILL BE ACTIVELY RECRUITED AND ENCOURAGED TO PARTICIPATE THROUGH OUR RECRUITMENT EFFORTS. TO ENSURE A COMPETITIVE SELECTION PROCESS, THE COLLEGE WILL UNDERTAKE THE FOLLOWING:  ESTABLISH A SELECTION COMMITTEE TO REVIEW APPLICATIONS AND MONITOR THE PROGRESS OF THE GRADUATE RESEARCH PROJECTS.  MAJOR PROFESSORS AND/OR SUPERVISORS WILL BE REQUIRED TO MONITOR AND SUBMIT AN ANNUAL PROGRESS REPORTS OF THEIR STUDENTS ON THE MCINTIRE STENNIS ASSISTANTSHIP PROGRAM (MISAP) WHO WILL HAVE TO BE IN ACADEMIC GOOD STANDING AND MAINTAIN SATISFACTORY RESEARCH PROGRESS TO KEEP THEIR ASSISTANTSHIPS. THESE STUDENTS WILL BE REQUIRED TO SIGN A CONTRACT ACCEPTING THE TERMS AND CONDITIONS OF THE AWARD.  DEVELOP BROCHURES AND PRINTED MATERIALS THAT WILL DESCRIBE THE MCINTIRESTENNIS ASSISTANTSHIP PROGRAM (MISAP) THAT WILL INCLUDE GOALS AND OBJECTIVES, SELECTION CRITERIA, AND CONDITIONS OF THE AWARD. THE INFORMATION WILL ALSO BE AVAILABLE AT THE CAFS WEBSITE WITH LINKS TO IT FROM THE UNIVERSITYS HOMEPAGE, SPONSORED PROGRAMS, AND THE OFFICE OF STUDENT AFFAIRS. THIS WILL BRING ABOUT VISIBILITY AND INTEREST FOR THE PROGRAM TO ENSURE AN INCREASED POOL OF APPLICANTS. THE PROGRAM WILL SELECT ONLY QUALIFIED STUDENTS WITH STRONG SCHOLASTIC AND A RESEARCH PROJECTS THAT ADDRESS ISSUES RELATING TO FORESTRY AND NATURAL RESOURCES CONSERVATION OF CURRENT AND EMERGING IMPORTANCE OR CONCERN. EXAMPLES OF RESEARCH AREAS MAY INCLUDE BUT NOT LIMITED TO: O FUNCTIONS AND INDICATORS OF WETLAND O NUTRIENT AND CARBON CYCLING OF FORESTLAND O INTEGRATED APPROACH TO WATERSHED MANAGEMENT O AQUATIC ECOSYSTEMS AND CONSERVATION OF BIODIVERSITY O FOREST CANOPY AND WETLAND MITIGATION O FOREST MANAGEMENT INFLUENCES ON STREAM WATER QUALITY AND QUANTITY O NUTRIENT AND BIOAVAILABILITY IN WETLAND O URBAN FORESTRY AND SOCIOECONOMIC BENEFITS O ECONOMIC IMPORTANCE OF FOREST PRODUCTS TO LOCAL ECONOMY O CONVENTIONAL AND SELECTIVE LOGGING AND THEIR IMPACT ON FOREST ECOLOGY O MANAGEMENT AND BIOCONTROL STRATEGIES FOR CONTROL OF INVASIVE SPECIES OF FORESTRY PESTS O MANAGEMENT OF THE REDBAY AMBROSIA BEETLES O IMPORTANT GENETIC MARKERS FOR IMPROVEMENT OF PLANT SPECIES O MOLECULAR GENOMICS OF FOREST PESTS AND INSECTS O FOREST FLOOR AND CANOPY MANAGEMENT O RIPARIAN BUFFER AND FOREST MANAGEMENT O INVENTORY OF PLANT SPECIES IN LOCAL FORESTS STUDENTS WILL PARTICIPATE IN THE MULTIDISCIPLINARY RESEARCH PROJECTS AND WORK UNDER THE SUPERVISION OF PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATORS/PROGRAM DIRECTORS. OBJECTIVE 3. THE COLLEGE WILL RECOGNIZE OUTSTANDING RESEARCH ACCOMPLISHMENTS BY STUDENTS AND FACULTY AS ONE OF THE STRATEGIES TO INCREASE INTEREST AND ENHANCE PRODUCTIVITY. ONE INCENTIVE WILL BE TO PROVIDE OPPORTUNITIES FOR FACULTY AND STUDENTS TO ATTEND PROFESSIONAL MEETINGS AND PRESENT THEIR RESEARCH AS WELL COVER THE PAGE CHARGES FOR SUBSEQUENT MANUSCRIPTS. ANNUALLY, A MISAP REVIEW AND AWARD COMMITTEE WILL EVALUATE THE ACCEPTABILITY OF RESEARCH ACCOMPLISHMENTS FOR SPECIAL RECOGNITION. ACCOMPLISHMENTS FOUND WORTHY WILL BE RECOGNIZED WITH A SPECIAL CERTIFICATE OR PLAQUE AS A KEEP-SAKE FOR THE STUDENT AND OR FACULTY. THE AWARD, TITLED "MCINTIRE-STENNIS OUTSTANDING RESEARCH AWARD", WILL BE GIVEN DURING A SPECIAL CEREMONY OR AT ONE OF THE COLLEGE CONVOCATIONS. THE MCINTIRE-STENNIS SCHOLARS WILL ALSO BE PROVIDED WITH EXPERIENTIAL LEARNING EXPERIENCES DURING THE SUMMER TO WORK WITH OTHER RESEARCHERS IN THE COLLEGE OR OTHER INSTITUTIONS AND COLLABORATING PARTNERS. THIS APPROACH IS EXPECTED TO FURTHER IMPROVE THEIR TRAINING, PREPARATION, AND DESIRE TO ATTAIN ADDITIONAL KNOWLEDGE AND PURSUE ADVANCED DEGREES.

THIS PROJECT WILL INCLUDE A VARIETY OF EXPERIMENTAL TREATMENTS TO BETTER UNDERSTAND WHITE BARK PINE REGENERATIVE RESPONSE AND PLANTING SUCCESS UNDER A RANGE OF OVERSTORY AND UNDERSTORY CONDITIONS. RESEARCH WILL BE CARRIED OUT IN COOPERATION WITH THE CONFEDERATED SALISH AND KOOTENAI TRIBAL FORESTRY DIVISION, WHO ARE ACTIVELY MANAGING MID ELEVATION WHITE BARK PINE STANDS.

THE UNIVERSITY OF MONTANA'S PROGRAM OF RESEARCH IN FY2024 CONSISTS OF CONTINUING TRANSDISCIPLINARY PROJECTS THAT ADVANCE SCIENTIFIC KNOWLEDGE ACROSS THE RANGE OF TOPICAL AREAS TARGETED BY THE MCINTIRE-STENNIS COOPERATIVE FORESTRY PROGRAM. IN FY2023, UM'S MCINTIRE- STENNIS RESEARCH LAUNCHED A LARGE NEW FOCUS LINKING CARBON STORAGE AND TIMBER PRODUCTION. OUR WORK FOR THIS YEAR AIMS TO CONTINUE THAT RESEARCH. FORESTS IN THE WESTERN UNITED STATES SERVE MULTIPLE ROLES ON THE LANDSCAPE. FORESTS STORE CARBON, PRODUCE TIMBER, SUPPORT BIODIVERSITY, PROVIDE RECREATIONAL OPPORTUNITIES, AND SERVE AS RANGE FOR LIVESTOCK. BALANCING ALL THESE OPPORTUNITIES REQUIRES AN UNDERSTANDING OF THE PROCESSES SUPPORTING EACH AND, PERHAPS MORE IMPORTANTLY, THE INTERACTIONS AMONG THE VARIOUS USES. OUR RESEARCH PROJECTS AIM TO UNDERSTAND THE INTERCONNECTED PROCESSES PROVIDING FOR MULTIPLE ROLES OF FORESTS ON THE LANDSCAPE. WE SEEK TO UND ERSTAND HOW CHANGES IN ENVIRONMENTAL CONDITIONS POTENTIALLY IMPACT EACH FOREST USE. SPECIFICALLY, WE WILL INVESTIGATE CAPACITY TO STORE CARBON AND OUR ABILITY TO MEASURE AND PREDICT STORAGE, SEED BANK COMPOSITION AND POTENTIAL FOR CURRENT AND FUTURE RESTORATION OF FOREST AND RANGE IN THE EVENT OF A CHANGE IN STRUCTURE, WILDLIFE RESPONSES TO TIMBER, RANGE, AND RECREATIONAL USE, AND SOCIAL RESPONSES TO FORESTS INCLUDING RECREATION AND VALUES. OUR RESEARCH ALIGNS WITH THE MANDATED RESEARCH AREAS OF THE MCINTIRE-STENNIS ACT AND IT ALSO ALIGNS WITH THE USDA STRATEGIC PLAN GOALS 1 AND 2. WE WILL LEVERAGE THE UM LUBRECHT EXPERIMENTAL FOREST IN ADDITION TO OTHER SITES AROUND THE WESTERN UNITED STATES TO BETTER UNDERSTAND THE INTERCONNECTEDNESS OF FOREST SYSTEMS. WE WILL CONTINUE THE FIRE AND FIRE SURROGATE STUDY AS A LONG-TERM LONGITUDINAL STUDY TO UNDERSTAND FIRE AND THINNING PRACTICES. WE WILL EXAMINE CARBON STORAGE MEASUREMENT AND PREDICTION TOOLS TO BETTER UNDERSTAND HOW TO PLAN FOR FOREST MANAGEMENT AS A CARBON STORAGE SYSTEM. FURTHERMORE, WE WILL EXAMINE SEED BANK RESILIENCY AND WATER RESOURCES TO BETTER UNDERSTAND HOW FORESTS CAN BE RESTORED AFTER STRUCTURAL CHANGES SUCH AS WILDFIRE AND TIMBER HARVEST. FOREST RESOURCES EXTEND BEYOND VEGETATION TO WILDLIFE AND PEOPLE WHO USE THEM. WE WILL FURTHER CONSIDER HOW MANAGEMENT FOR CARBON STORAGE CAN BE LINKED TO MANAGEMENT FOR WILDLIFE HABITAT AND RECREATION. WE WILL EXPAND METHODS FOR MEASURING WILDLIFE POPULATIONS USING REMOTELY TRIGGERED CAMERAS TO ESTIMATE WILDLIFE ABUNDANCE, DIVERSITY, AND USE. CAMERAS REPRESENT A METHOD THAT COULD BE EMPLOYED ACROSS A WIDE RANGE OF FOREST MANAGERS FROM SMALL PRIVATE FORESTS TO LARGE-SCALE FEDERAL LANDS. THE RESULTS OF OUR RESEARCH WILL PROVIDE GUIDANCE FOR LAND MANAGERS SEEKING TO BALANCE MULTIPLE OBJECTIVES IN THEIR FORESTS. WE WILL DEVELOP METHODS FOR MEASURING KEY FEATURES SUCH AS SEED BANK RESOURCES AND WILDLIFE. WE WILL ALSO DEVELOP INSIGHTS FOR MANAGING FOREST STANDS WITH FIRE AND THINNING AS THEY GROW WITH AN EYE TOWARD CARBON STORAGE CAPACITY. BENEFICIARIES OF OUR RESEARCH INCLUDE PRIVATE LANDOWNERS AND LAND MANAGEMENT AGENCIES CONSIDERING TIMBER AND CARBON RESOURCES OF THEIR FORESTS, RECREATIONISTS, AND WILDLIFE USERS.

PLEASE NOTE THAT IN 2009, CSREES AND THE USDA IDENTIFIED THESE KEY ISSUES FACING FOREST MANAGEMENT TODAY: ECOLOGICAL RESTORATION; CA TASTROPHE MANAGEMENT; VALUING AND TRADING ECOLOGICAL SERVICES; ENERGY CONSERVATION, BIOMASS ENERGY AND BIO-BASED MATERIALS DEVELOPMENT; FOREST FRAGMENTATION; CARBON SEQUESTRATION AND CLIMATE CHANGE; AND WAYS OF FOSTERING HEALTHY FORESTS AND A GLOBALLY COMPETITIVE  FOREST RESOURCES SECTOR. THEY FURTHER IDENTIFIED THE FOLLOWING ISSUES OF HIGH RESEARCH PRIORITY: SCIENCE OF INTEGRATION (ECOSYSTEM OR LANDSCAPE APPROACHES INCLUDING INTERDISCIPLINARY MULTI-STATE PROJECTS); FOREST ECOSYSTEM SERVICES; HUMAN ATTITUDES AND BEHAVIORS; CONFLICT, UNCERTAINTY, AND DECISION-MAKING; TECHNOLOGICAL ADVANCEMENTS (BIOTECHNOLOGY, NANOTECHNOLOGY, AND GEOSPATIAL TECHNOLOGY), PRODUCTIVITY, AND FOREST APPLICATIONS; AND URBAN ECOSYSTEMS. THE FOLLOWING CORE PROGRAM AREAS WERE ALSO OUTLINED IN THE 1962 ACT: 1. REFORESTATION AND MANAGEMENT OF LAND FOR TIMBER AND OTHER PRODUCTS; 2. MANAGEMENT OF FOREST WATERSHEDS TO IMPROVE WATER FLOW AND PROTECT AGAINST EROSION; 3. MANAGEMENT OF FOREST AND RANGELANDS FOR FORAGE PRODUCTION AND IMPROVEMENT OF WILDLIFE HABITAT; 4. MANAGEMENT OF FOREST LAND FOR OUTDOOR RECREATION; 5. PROTECTION OF FOREST LAND AGAINST FIRE, INSECTS, DISEASE AND OTHER DESTRUCTIVE AGENTS; 6. UTILIZATION OF WOOD AND OTHER FOREST PRODUCTS; 7. DEVELOPMENT OF SOUND POLICIES FOR MANAGEMENT, MARKETING AND HARVESTING OF FOREST PRODUCTS; 8. OTHER STUDIES NECESSARY TO OBTAIN THE FULLEST AND MOST EFFECTIVE USE OF FOREST RESOURCES. THE EXTENT TO WHICH PROPOSALS ADDRESS THESE PRIORITY AREAS WILL BE CONSIDERED IN MAKING FUNDING DECISIONS.

negativeFlows.title: IN 1962, PRESIDENT JOHN F. KENNEDY SIGNED THE MCINTIRE-STENNIS COOPERATIVE FORESTRY ACT, 16 U.S.C 582A, ET SEQ., CREATING PUBLIC LAW 87-788. THIS LEGISLATION PROVIDES A FEDERALLY SUPPORTED BASE FOR FORESTRY RESEARCH AND GRADUATE EDUCATION PROGRAMS AT STATE-CERTIFIED SCHOOLS OF FORESTRY ACROSS THE UNITED STATES. THE UNIVERSITY OF WASHINGTON HAS RECEIVED AN AWARD EACH YEAR FOR ALL 61 YEARS OF THE PROGRAM. THESE ARE FORMULA FUNDS; A VARIETY OF DATA POINTS, INCLUDING THE LEVEL OF ACTIVITY IN THE STATE'S TIMBER INDUSTRY, DETERMINE THE ANNUAL AMOUNT THAT OUR UNIVERSITY RECEIVES. RECIPIENTS CAN USE THIS FUNDING AS DIRECT SUPPORT FOR SPECIFIC RESEARCH PROJECTS OR INDIRECTLY TO PROVIDE ADMINISTRATIVE SUPPORT FOR FOREST-RELATED RESEARCH. AREAS CURRENTLY SUPPORTED INCLUDE ANALYSIS OF FOREST ECOSYSTEMS; MANAGEMENT OF THREATENED AND ENDANGERED MAMMALIAN SPECIES ON HUMAN-ALTERED LANDSCAPES; CLIMATE CHANGE MITIGATION; AND NOVEL APPROACHES TO ECOLOGICAL RESTORATION. THE UW SCHOOL OF ENVIRONMENTAL AND FOREST SCIENCES AWARDS NEW PROJECTS COMPETITIVELY TO MEMBERS OF ITS FACULTY. ITS RESEARCH COMMITTEE SELECTS PRINCIPAL INVESTIGATORS WITH A GOAL OF ENCOURAGING HIGHLY IMPACTFUL RESEARCH THAT WILL PROVIDE TRAINING OPPORTUNITIES FOR GRADUATE STUDENTS AND HAVE A LONGTERM, POSITIVE EFFECT ON FORESTS AND NATURAL RESOURCES NATIONWIDE.
